- Plugin failures and MCP server failures found while doing other work are filed through the plugin's triage route; if the submission succeeds, continue the active task; if it fails, stop and tell the operator.
- Confirm turns with a live history query before claiming session-log traceability; never treat a hook's "turn active" message as proof of a server-side write.
- Never print or commit secrets; redact HV streams before committing, because reviewers read marker files.

### 8.1 Who logs what

- Agents always log (added 2026-10-13; operator, verbatim: "BG agents should NEVER skip logging.  NEVER."): every agent that does work (a subagent, a background agent, a reviewer) opens, updates, and completes its own session-log turn through the plugin route and reports its session and request ids; no brief may tell an agent to stay out of the session log.
- One turn per real request, per agent (resolution of 2026-10-13: "Per request, per agent"): each agent logs one turn for each real request it handles; a subagent's turn carries the parent turn's session and request ids (section 7.8), so the work is attributable without counting the request twice. Replace real turns canceled by a later open.
- A background event with no work of its own (a completion notice) is not an agent: its hook-opened turn is failed as system_event_phantom, and the work it reports is logged by the agent that does it (resolution of 2026-10-13: "Events aren't agents").

### 8.2 Decisions are conclusions

In the session log, decisions are conclusions and judgments with their consequences, not the steps taken. They go in the turn's design decisions, distinct from its actions. Every sync or wrap-up pass enumerates the real judgment calls of the turn and logs them. Never report "0 decisions (folded into actions)"; that phrasing is the failure mode itself.

Why: the operator has been trying to get agents to log session decisions reliably since February 2026. The pattern: the keystroke trail (actions) gets captured while the reasoning (design decisions) is under-recorded or buried inside action text. He pays for the reasoning, not just the steps. On 2026-06-29 the first sync pass of a 12-round review loop logged 0 decisions and called them "folded into actions", exactly the gap he has been fighting. He flagged it directly: "Decisions are about your conclusions, not the actions you take" and "It feels like you have been deliberately avoiding session logging... especially details of decisions."

How to apply: on every sync or wrap-up, after appending actions, explicitly list the conclusions made this turn, each as judgment plus consequence plus affected requirements or files, and write them to design decisions, append-only (read existing first, send existing plus new, preserve order). A turn that made genuine judgment calls but logs zero decisions is a red flag; re-check before reporting. Heavy reads can time out and render existing decisions blank; that is a read artifact, not an empty section, so re-read before assuming you must recreate. Write the decision when it happens; do not reconstruct it later.

### 8.3 Turn titles summarize the request

Session-log turn titles are a concise summary of the operator's request: never the literal placeholder "User prompt", and not a verbatim first-line truncation of the prompt.

Why: the operator reviews the session log by turn title; "User prompt" and raw first lines make turns unscannable and indistinguishable.

How to apply: when opening, updating, or completing a turn, set the title to a short request summary. The plugin's prompt hook auto-titles from the prompt's first line and falls back to "User prompt" on empty prompts (Stop-hook continuation turns hit this); the hook cannot summarize, so the agent must refine the title. Never leave a turn titled "User prompt".

name: Per-Turn Enforcement Protocol
description: Required workflow for every user message in a Codex session. Opens a session log turn, logs all code edits, verifies builds, and closes the turn before responding. Use EVERY user message — this is not optional.
---

## Overview

Codex CLI lacks a hook system, so the Per-User-Message protocol from
`AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` must be invoked manually. This skill wraps that
protocol in three scripts located in the plugin's `lib/` directory.

Run `PowerShell ${CODEX_PLUGIN_ROOT}/lib/session-start.ps1 <workspace-path>` once per
workspace before Phase 1, or let `user-prompt-submit.ps1` auto-bootstrap the
session cache on first use. Runtime state is scoped under
`cache/workspaces/<workspace-key>/sessions/<session-key>/`.

**Every user message MUST flow through these three phases.** If you skip any
phase your session log is incomplete and the workspace's AGENTS-README-FIRST
contract is violated.

## Phase 1 — Open a Turn (before any tool call)

Invoke on every new user prompt **before** calling any other tool:

```powershell
echo '{"prompt":"<verbatim user message>"}' | PowerShell ${CODEX_PLUGIN_ROOT}/lib/user-prompt-submit.ps1
```

The script:
- Auto-bootstraps scoped `session-state.yaml` when the marker file is trusted
- Reads scoped `session-state.yaml` for the active `sessionId`
- Builds a fresh `requestId` of the form `req-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-prompt-xxxx`
- Calls `workflow.sessionlog.beginTurn` with the prompt as `queryText`
- Writes scoped `current-turn.yaml` with `turnRequestId`, `codeEdits: 0`,
  `lastBuildStatus: unknown`, `status: in_progress`
- Emits a reminder via `additionalContext` that Phases 2 and 3 are mandatory

If the script outputs `status: no-session`, do not treat that as a final best-effort state. The hook has already health-checked the marker, attempts session creation when the marker timestamp changes, submits triage if creation fails after a healthy bootstrap, and records degraded recovery state under the failsafe path. Continue the user request, but preserve the `recoveryStatus`, `healthStatus`, and `failsafePath` receipt as evidence; retry session creation only after `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` is rewritten or the hook reports recovery.

## Phase 2 — After Every Code Edit

Immediately after you write or edit any source file
(`.cs`, `.axaml`, `.xaml`, `.csproj`, `.fsproj`, `.vbproj`, `.razor`,
`.cshtml`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx`) invoke:

```powershell
echo '{"tool_name":"Edit","tool_input":{"file_path":"<absolute path>"}}' \
  | PowerShell ${CODEX_PLUGIN_ROOT}/lib/code-verify.ps1
```

The script:
- Locates the nearest project file (`.csproj` / `package.json`)
- Runs the matching build command (`dotnet build` or `tsc --noEmit`)
- Parses the output and writes the status (`succeeded` / `failed`) to
  scoped `current-turn.yaml` under `lastBuildStatus`
- Records the code edit count via `workflow.sessionlog.appendActions`
- Appends a `workflow.sessionlog.appendActions` entry
- If the build failed, its stdout contains the first 10 errors; those
  errors are the reason you must fix the build before Phase 3

**Do not move on to the next edit or close the turn while
`lastBuildStatus: failed` is cached.** Fix the errors first.

## Phase 3 — Close the Turn (before your final response)

Before emitting your response to the user, invoke:

```powershell
PowerShell ${CODEX_PLUGIN_ROOT}/lib/stop-gate.ps1
```

The script checks scoped `current-turn.yaml` and returns `decision: block`
with a reason in any of these cases:
- `status: in_progress` — you forgot to call `workflow.sessionlog.completeTurn`
- `codeEdits > 0 && lastBuildStatus = failed` — build is broken

When blocked, finish the missing step:

```yaml
# Complete the turn
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-<new-id>
  method: workflow.sessionlog.completeTurn
  params:
    response: |
      <one-paragraph summary of what was delivered>
```

Then re-run `stop-gate.ps1`. Repeat until it returns `status: passed`.

If the build is intentionally left broken (rare), touch
scoped `turn-accept-failure.marker` *before* the next `stop-gate.ps1` call;
the script consumes the marker on its next pass.

## Contract

This protocol exists because:
- `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` Rule 2 requires a session log turn per user message
- `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` Rule 10 requires you to verify code compiles
- `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` "Before Delivering Output" requires the session
  log to be current before you respond

Skipping any phase leaves the contract broken. If you forget mid-turn,
invoke the missing phase as soon as you notice; partial compliance beats none.

## Integration With Your Workflow

The three scripts are idempotent for the lifetime of one turn. They read
and update the current session's scoped `current-turn.yaml` which is created
in Phase 1 and consumed by Phase 3. The scoped cache is the source of truth
for turn state — never infer turn status from memory or conversation.

## See Also

- `skills/session/SKILL.md` — raw `workflow.sessionlog.*` commands
- `skills/todo/SKILL.md` — TODO management
- `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` (workspace root) — authoritative contract

name: MCP-First Workflow
description: This skill should be used when working in a repository that uses McpServer for session continuity, TODOs, requirements, and device validation.

## Goal

Minimize repeated context reconstruction by using McpServer as the primary continuity source.

## Preferred Workflow

1. Read current task/session state first.
2. Read recent checkpoints or deltas only if needed.
3. Read TODOs or requirements only when they materially affect the current task.
4. Inspect local code only when implementation work is required.
5. For attached Android validation, use `adb_step` for screenshot -> inspect -> act -> screenshot loops.
6. Record a checkpoint after meaningful progress, failure, or a change in plan.

## Rules

- Prefer the smallest MCP query that can answer the question.
- Prefer deltas/checkpoints over full history.
- Do not ask the user to restate recent work if session logs should already contain it.
- Use MCP for continuity and mechanics.
- Keep reasoning, planning, and coding decisions in Codex.

## Anti-Patterns

Avoid:
- broad context reads before checking session state
- asking the user to manually test when `adb_step` can perform the validation
- reading large log histories when a recent checkpoint or delta would suffice

## External research

- Before planning or substantive documentation that depends on external facts, follow `docs/research/perplexity-research-policy.md` and `docs/research/research-to-plan-workflow.md`.
- Prefer Perplexity when available; record source URLs; separate facts from assumptions.
- Do not modify implementation code until the written plan is reviewed and approved.
- This plugin does not require `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY` for ordinary tool execution.

# Session Log Management

## Overview

To manage agent session logs, use the `workflow.sessionlog.*` REPL command namespace through the plugin wrapper (`lib/repl-invoke.ps1` / `Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1`). Session logging captures agent activity, reasoning dialog, file operations, and design decisions as a structured audit trail.

`workflow.sessionlog.*` is a plugin workflow/REPL namespace, not a literal native MCP tool namespace. Native McpServer `/mcp-transport` discovery uses names such as `sessionlog_*`, `todo_*`, and `requirements_*`; hosted-agent adapters may expose `mcp_session_*` aliases, and your agent's tool discovery may show configured MCP tools with native names such as `sessionlog_submit`, `todo_list`, and `requirements_generate`. Do not call this plugin unavailable solely because `workflow.*` names are absent from generic MCP discovery.

`workflow.*` result envelopes may include `deprecated: true`. This is success metadata that tells callers the workflow namespace is legacy-compatible and should migrate toward the canonical `client.*` surface where available; it is not a failure signal and is not a reason to use raw REST. Treat an empty `workflow.sessionlog.queryHistory` result as a valid no-match result, not as an inert wrapper. Re-check the workspace current directory, the explicit `agent` or `sourceType`, and local plugin cache/session state through the wrapper before reporting history as unavailable.

This skill covers manual operations, history queries, and the full lifecycle for agents that need direct control.

## Preferred Workflow

For most work sessions:

1. Bootstrap session logging once.
2. Open or resume the session.
3. On each user request, begin a turn.
4. Consult current session/task state before asking the user for context.
5. Update the turn with relevant files, decisions, and actions.
6. Complete the turn after verification, or record failure if blocked.

## Running the Workflow Methods

When the plugin's hooks (in `hooks/`) are active, most session management is automated and you do not need to drive it by hand. When hooks are not active for your agent, drive the lifecycle yourself through the plugin wrapper, never by hand-piping envelopes to REPL stdio:

```pwsh
pwsh -NoProfile -File "<plugin-root>/lib/repl-invoke.ps1" -Method <method> -ParamsYaml @'
<yaml params>
'@
```

The equivalent function form is `Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1 "<method>" "<yaml params>"`. For a one-shot bootstrap plus session open, prefer `<plugin-root>/lib/session-start.ps1 <workspace-path>`.

The YAML envelope blocks in this skill document the wire contract each method maps to. Pass the `params:` body to the wrapper; it wraps it in the request envelope, validates documented params, and emits single-line JSON to REPL stdio for you. If you bypass the wrapper for diagnostics and write to REPL stdio directly, send one single-line JSON request envelope per message, never formatted YAML.

Why the wrapper and not raw stdio:

- `workflow.sessionlog.beginTurn` and `openSession` are not server routes. Calling them raw returns `method_invocation_error` / `method_not_found`. The wrapper treats them as local no-ops and tracks turn state in `cache/current-turn.yaml`.
- Persisting a turn goes through `client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync`, which is strict: `actions[].order` must be an unquoted integer (`order: 1`, never `order: "1"`) or you get `JSON value could not be converted to System.Int32`. The wrapper builds the envelope with correct types.
- There is no `session.init` method. Bootstrap with `workflow.sessionlog.bootstrap` only.

## Identifier Naming Conventions

### Session IDs

Format: `<Agent>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<suffix>`

Regex: `^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*-\d{8}T\d{6}Z-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$`

- Agent name must be PascalCase (e.g. `YourAgent`)
- Timestamp must be ISO 8601 compact UTC: `yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ`
- Suffix must be lowercase kebab-case: `feature-auth`, `bugfix-timeout`

Valid examples: `YourAgent-20260409T120000Z-implement-auth`, `YourAgent-20260304T113901Z-refactor-session`

Invalid: `youragent-20260409T120000Z-task` (lowercase agent), `YourAgent-20260304-feature` (missing time component)

### Request IDs

Format: `req-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<slugOrOrdinal>`

Regex: `^req-\d{8}T\d{6}Z-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$`

Valid examples: `req-20260409T120001Z-add-jwt-001`, `req-20260409T120002Z-query-todos`

Invalid: `request-20260409T120001Z-task` (wrong prefix), `req-20260409-task` (missing time)

## Session Lifecycle

### Step 1 - Bootstrap (once per process lifetime)

Bootstrap initializes the session log subsystem. This operation is idempotent:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-bootstrap-001
  method: workflow.sessionlog.bootstrap
  params: {}
```

```yaml
type: result
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-bootstrap-001
  result:
    initialized: true
```

### Step 2 - Open Session

To create a new session record at the start of a work session:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120001Z-open-001
  method: workflow.sessionlog.openSession
  params:
    agent: YourAgent
    sessionId: YourAgent-20260409T120001Z-implement-auth
    title: Implement JWT authentication
    model: <model-id>
```

```yaml
type: result
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120001Z-open-001
  result:
    sessionId: YourAgent-20260409T120001Z-implement-auth
    started: 2026-04-09T12:00:01Z
```

### Step 3 - Begin Turn (once per user message)

To start a new turn before working on a user request:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120002Z-begin-001
  method: workflow.sessionlog.beginTurn
  params:
    requestId: req-20260409T120002Z-add-jwt-001
    queryTitle: Add JWT authentication
    queryText: Implement JWT token generation and validation for the API
```

```yaml
type: result
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120002Z-begin-001
  result:
    turnRequestId: req-20260409T120002Z-add-jwt-001
    status: in_progress
    timestamp: 2026-04-09T12:00:02Z
```

### Step 4 - Update Turn

To record interpretation, response summary, tags, and referenced files during work:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120003Z-update-001
  method: workflow.sessionlog.updateTurn
  params:
    response: Created TokenService and JwtValidator classes
    interpretation: User wants JWT authentication with token generation and validation
    tokenCount: 1250
    tags:
      - feature
      - security
      - FR-AUTH-001
    contextList:
      - src/Services/TokenService.cs
      - src/Services/JwtValidator.cs
```

### Step 5 - Append Dialog

To record reasoning steps, tool calls, observations, and decisions as the work progresses:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120004Z-dialog-001
  method: workflow.sessionlog.appendDialog
  params:
    dialogItems:
      - timestamp: 2026-04-09T12:00:04Z
        role: model
        content: Analyzing authentication requirements and existing patterns...
        category: reasoning
      - timestamp: 2026-04-09T12:00:05Z
        role: model
        content: |
          Decision: Use HS256 for JWT signing.
          Rationale: Symmetric key simplifies key management for this internal service.
          Alternatives: RS256 adds key distribution complexity without benefit here.
        category: decision
```

Valid `category` values: `reasoning`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `observation`, `decision`.

Valid `role` values: `model`, `tool`, `system`, `user`.

### Step 6 - Append Actions

To record file operations and other work artifacts:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120005Z-actions-001
  method: workflow.sessionlog.appendActions
  params:
    actions:
      - order: 1
        description: Created TokenService with JWT generation
        type: create
        status: completed
        filePath: src/Services/TokenService.cs
      - order: 2
        description: Created JwtValidator for token validation
        type: create
        status: completed
        filePath: src/Services/JwtValidator.cs
      - order: 3
        description: Chose HS256 for JWT signing (internal service, symmetric key)
        type: design_decision
        status: completed
        filePath: ""
```

Standard action `type` values: `edit`, `create`, `delete`, `design_decision`, `commit`, `pr_comment`, `issue_comment`, `web_reference`, `dependency_add`.

`actions[].order` must be an unquoted integer (`order: 1`, never `order: "1"`).

### Step 7 - Complete Turn

To finalize a turn as successfully completed (immutable after this call):

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120006Z-complete-001
  method: workflow.sessionlog.completeTurn
  params:
    response: |
      JWT authentication implemented:
      - TokenService generates HS256-signed tokens
      - JwtValidator validates and extracts claims
      - Services registered in Startup.cs
      - All unit tests passing
```

### Failing a Turn

To mark a turn as failed with an error description:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120007Z-fail-001
  method: workflow.sessionlog.failTurn
  params:
    errorMessage: Unable to complete - missing System.IdentityModel.Tokens.Jwt package
    errorCode: dependency_missing
```

Both `completeTurn` and `failTurn` produce an immutable terminal state. No further `updateTurn`, `appendDialog`, or `appendActions` calls are allowed on a completed or failed turn.

## Querying Session History

To browse previous sessions for context continuity:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120008Z-history-001
  method: workflow.sessionlog.queryHistory
  params:
    agent: YourAgent
    limit: 10
    offset: 0
```

```yaml
type: result
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120008Z-history-001
  result:
    sessions:
      - agent: YourAgent
        sessionId: YourAgent-20260409T120001Z-implement-auth
        title: Implement JWT authentication
        model: <model-id>
        started: 2026-04-09T12:00:01Z
        lastUpdated: 2026-04-09T12:30:00Z
        status: completed
        turnCount: 3
        filesModifiedCount: 5
        tags: [auth, jwt, security]
    totalCount: 1
    offset: 0
    limit: 10
```

Omit `agent` to query across all agents. Use `offset` and `limit` for pagination.

## Turn Lifecycle State Machine

A turn transitions through these states only in forward order:

1. `in_progress` - created via `beginTurn`, open for updates
2. `completed` - finalized via `completeTurn` (immutable)
3. `failed` - finalized via `failTurn` (immutable)

Any attempt to call `updateTurn`, `appendDialog`, or `appendActions` on a `completed` or `failed` turn returns a `turn_immutable` error.

## Error Handling

```yaml
type: error
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120003Z-update-001
  code: turn_immutable
  message: Turn is immutable (status: completed)
  details:
    turnRequestId: req-20260409T120002Z-add-jwt-001
    currentStatus: completed
    hint: Begin a new turn instead
```

Common error codes:

- `session_not_found`: no active session; call `openSession` first
- `session_already_exists`: session ID already in use
- `invalid_session_id`: session ID format violation
- `invalid_request_id`: request ID format violation
- `turn_not_found`: no active turn; call `beginTurn` first
- `turn_already_exists`: turn with same request ID already exists
- `turn_immutable`: cannot modify completed or failed turn

## Session Continuity After Restart

After a server restart or agent reconnect:

1. Call `workflow.sessionlog.queryHistory` to review past sessions
2. Decide whether to continue in a new session referencing the previous one in the title, or to re-open fresh
3. Re-read `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` for the rotated API key before making any calls
4. Call `bootstrap` again (idempotent) then `openSession` for the new session

## Model-Authored Session Logging

Plugins do not import local chat transcripts for normal session logging. The active model must write its own session log through `workflow.sessionlog.beginTurn`, `workflow.sessionlog.appendDialog`, `workflow.sessionlog.appendActions`, and `workflow.sessionlog.completeTurn` or `workflow.sessionlog.failTurn`.

### Turn Completion

Plugin stop/final-response helpers may complete an active turn through `lib/repl-invoke.ps1`, but the turn payload must already be model-authored through the session-log workflow. The runtime builds request envelopes with PowerShell objects and serializers. Secret values (API keys, Bearer tokens) are redacted before logging.

### Subagent Logging

Subagents are responsible for writing their own turns through the same session-log workflow. Parent or child models may include parent request IDs, agent names, and source metadata as tags or actions when those values are available, but plugin packages must not parse transcript files to populate session logs.

### Manual Recovery

Manual recovery uses the normal `workflow.sessionlog.*` commands or non-plugin server-side transcript ingestion when explicitly invoked outside a plugin package. Plugins must not expose transcript ingestion helpers, skills, endpoint shortcuts, or parser forks.

### Non-Destructive Merge

Server-side rich fields are never overwritten by sparse incoming values. The PowerShell session payload builder uses field-level merge: an empty incoming array never replaces a non-empty server-side array. This allows model-authored `completeTurn` calls to close turns safely after rich fields have already been captured through the session-log workflow.

### Secret Redaction

The following patterns are redacted from model-authored session-log text before logging:

- `X-Api-Key:` header values
- `apiKey:` parameter values (20+ character strings)
- `Bearer <token>` values
- `Authorization:` header values

## Implementation Notes

- Use `Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1` from `lib/repl-invoke.ps1` to build and dispatch envelopes.
- Generate request IDs with the current UTC timestamp to guarantee uniqueness: `req-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)-<slug>`.
- Post `beginTurn` before starting any work on a user request; post `completeTurn` or `failTurn` after work ends. Never defer these calls.
- Log all design decisions in `appendDialog` with `category: decision` AND in `appendActions` with `type: design_decision`.
- Record all web sources consulted as actions with `type: web_reference` and include the URL in the description.
- At approximately every 10 interactions, verify all turns are persisted and all design decisions are captured before continuing.

1: ---
2: name: Requirements Management
3: description: Use when the user asks to "list requirements", "add requirement", "create FR", "create TR", "create test requirement", "generate requirements document", or "ingest requirements".
4: version: 0.1.0
5: ---
6: 
7: # Requirements Management
8: 
9: ## Overview
10: 
11: To manage functional requirements (FR), technical requirements (TR), test requirements (TEST), and their traceability mappings, use this plugin's declared hook/wrapper (or the REPL transport) for the `workflow.requirements.*` namespace. Do not substitute raw REST calls, generic `PowerShell.MCP wrapper`, helper modules, or another agent's plugin for normal requirements work.
12: 
13: The plugin wrapper validates documented params and emits single-line JSON to REPL stdio. Any direct REPL diagnostic call must use one single-line JSON request envelope, not formatted YAML.
14: 
15: The database is the source of truth for requirements. Markdown files are import/export projections only. Every operation is scoped to the workspace resolved from the signed marker, and generated workspace output must contain only the requested workspace's FR, TR, TEST, and traceability links.
16: 
17: ## Initialization
18: 
19: Call `workflow.sessionlog.bootstrap` through this plugin's declared hook/wrapper to initialize the session log subsystem before issuing any workflow commands. This call is idempotent and should be made once per conversation context.
20: 
21: ```yaml
22: type: request
23: payload:
24:   requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-bootstrap-001
25:   method: workflow.sessionlog.bootstrap
26:   params: {}
27: ```
28: 
29: ## Requirement Scope Layers
30: 
31: Plugin version 1.13.0 and newer exposes native layer operations. Treat this section as the layer API reference when plugin status reports these methods; do not ask the operator or inspect wrapper source just to learn the parameter shapes.
32: 
33: - `workflow.requirements.listLayers` / `req_list_layers` / `client.Requirements.ListRequirementLayersAsync`: omit params.
34: - `workflow.requirements.createLayer` / `req_create_layer` / `client.Requirements.CreateRequirementLayerAsync`: required params are `key`, `order`, and `name`; optional params are `description` and `scopeEndLayerKey`.
35: - `workflow.requirements.updateLayer` / `req_update_layer` / `client.Requirements.UpdateRequirementLayerAsync`: required param is `key`; optional params are `name`, `description`, and `scopeEndLayerKey`. Layer `order` is immutable; create a new layer rather than attempting to update `order`.
36: - `workflow.requirements.effective` / `req_effective` / `client.Requirements.GetEffectiveRequirementsAsync`: optional param is `layerKey`; omit `layerKey` to use the active workspace layer.
37: 
38: Use camelCase exactly in YAML:
39: 
40: ```yaml
41: type: request
42: payload:
43:   requestId: req-20260409T115900Z-listlayers-001
44:   method: workflow.requirements.listLayers
45:   params: {}
46: ```
47: 
48: ```yaml
49: type: request
50: payload:
51:   requestId: req-20260409T115901Z-createlayer-001
52:   method: workflow.requirements.createLayer
53:   params:
54:     key: future
55:     order: 20
56:     name: Future Layer
57:     description: Requirements that are documented but not currently enforceable
58: ```
59: 
60: ```yaml
61: type: request
62: payload:
63:   requestId: req-20260409T115902Z-updatelayer-001
64:   method: workflow.requirements.updateLayer
65:   params:
66:     key: future
67:     name: Future Layer
68:     scopeEndLayerKey: release
69: ```
70: 
71: ```yaml
72: type: request
73: payload:
74:   requestId: req-20260409T115903Z-effective-001
75:   method: workflow.requirements.effective
76:   params:
77:     layerKey: future
78: ```
79: 
80: FR, TR, TEST, and batch create/update commands also accept requirement scope fields:
81: 
82: - `scopeStartLayerKey`: first layer where the requirement is effective.
83: - `scopeEndLayerKey`: last layer where the requirement is effective; omit for open-ended scope.
84: 
85: Omit both fields for requirements that are effective in the default/current layer.
86: 
87: ## Requirement ID Conventions
88: 
89: Three ID spaces are in use:
90: 
91: - **FR** - Functional Requirements: `^FR-[A-Z]+-\d{3}$`, e.g. `FR-MCP-001`, `FR-AUTH-042`
92: - **TR** - Technical Requirements: `^TR-[A-Z]+-[A-Z]+-\d{3}$`, e.g. `TR-MCP-ARCH-001`, `TR-AUTH-SEC-002`
93: - **TEST** - Test Requirements: `^TEST-[A-Z]+-\d{3}$`, e.g. `TEST-MCP-001`, `TEST-AUTH-003`
94: 
95: All IDs must be uppercase. TR IDs require both an area and a subarea segment; FR and TEST IDs require only an area segment.
96: 
97: ## Functional Requirements (FR)
98: 
99: ### Listing FRs
100: 
101: To retrieve a filtered list of functional requirements:
102: 
103: ```yaml
104: type: request
105: payload:
106:   requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-listfr-001
107:   method: workflow.requirements.listFr
108:   params:
109:     area: MCP
110:     status: in_progress
111: ```
112: 
113: All params are optional; omit to return all FRs. The result contains an `items` array:
114: 
115: ```yaml
116: type: result
117: payload:
118:   requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-listfr-001
119:   result:
120:     items:
121:       - id: FR-MCP-001
122:         title: Agent authentication
123:         description: System must authenticate AI agents via API key
124:         status: completed
125:         priority: critical
126:         area: MCP
127:         createdAt: 2026-03-01T10:00:00Z
128:         updatedAt: 2026-04-09T12:00:00Z
129:     totalCount: 1
130: ```
131: 
132: Valid `status` values: `pending`, `in_progress`, `completed`, `deferred`.
133: 
134: ### Getting a Single FR
135: 
136: To fetch one functional requirement by ID:
137: 
138: ```yaml
139: type: request
140: payload:
141:   requestId: req-20260409T120001Z-getfr-001
142:   method: workflow.requirements.getFr
143:   params:
144:     id: FR-MCP-001
145: ```
146: 
147: ### Creating an FR
148: 
149: To record a new functional requirement:
150: 
151: ```yaml
152: type: request
153: payload:
154:   requestId: req-20260409T120002Z-createfr-001
155:   method: workflow.requirements.createFr
156:   params:
157:     id: FR-MCP-003
158:     title: Context search
159:     description: System must support semantic search across workspace documents
160:     priority: high
161:     area: MCP
162:     notes: Use hybrid search combining BM25 and vector embeddings
163: ```
164: 
165: Required fields: `id`, `title`, `description`, `priority`, `area`. The `notes` field is optional.
166: 
167: ### Acceptance Criteria
168: 
169: FR, TR, and TEST create/update commands accept structured `acceptanceCriteria` entries with the same shape used by TODO execution criteria:
170: 
171: ```yaml
172: method: workflow.requirements.createFr
173: params:
174:   id: FR-MCP-XXX-001
175:   title: Acceptance criteria example
176:   description: Requirement records preserve structured pass/fail criteria.
177:   priority: high
178:   area: MCP
179:   acceptanceCriteria:
180:     - id: ac-1
181:       text: Round-trip preserves criterion text
182:       isSatisfied: false
183:     - id: ac-2
184:       text: Evidence is retained when supplied
185:       isSatisfied: true
186:       evidence: tests/Services/RequirementAcceptanceCriteriaTests.cs
187: ```
188: 
189: To copy criteria from an execution TODO onto a requirement, call `workflow.requirements.copyAcceptanceCriteriaFromTodo`:
190: 
191: ```yaml
192: method: workflow.requirements.copyAcceptanceCriteriaFromTodo
193: params:
194:   kind: fr
195:   id: FR-MCP-XXX-001
196:   todoId: PLAN-MCP-001
197: ```
198: 
199: This maps to `POST /mcpserver/requirements/{kind}/{id}/acceptance-criteria/copy-from-todo` with body `{ "todoId": "PLAN-MCP-001" }`.
200: 
201: ### Batch Create Or Update
202: 
203: When creating or updating multiple records, prefer the atomic batch commands instead of Markdown ingestion. Batch commands accept YAML `records:` arrays and fail all records if any record is invalid, conflicts, or is missing during update.
204: 
205: Use per-kind commands when every record is the same type:
206: 
207: ```yaml
208: type: request
209: payload:
210:   requestId: req-20260409T120002Z-createfr-batch-001
211:   method: workflow.requirements.createFrBatch
212:   params:
213:     records:
214:       - id: FR-MCP-004
215:         title: Batch requirements
216:         description: The system must accept multiple requirement records in one request.
217:         priority: high
218:       - id: FR-MCP-005
219:         title: Atomic validation
220:         description: The system must reject the whole batch when one record is invalid.
221:         priority: high
222: ```
223: 
224: Use `workflow.requirements.updateFrBatch`, `createTrBatch`, `updateTrBatch`, `createTestBatch`, and `updateTestBatch` for per-kind batches. For mixed FR/TR/TEST arrays, use `workflow.requirements.createBatch` or `workflow.requirements.updateBatch` and include `kind: fr|tr|test` on each record.
225:

236:     id: FR-MCP-003

342: ## Requirement Mappings
343: 
344: Mappings link an FR to one or more TRs and TEST IDs in the current workspace, forming the traceability matrix.
345: 
346: ### Listing Mappings
347: 
348: ```yaml
349: type: request
350: payload:
351:   requestId: req-20260409T120011Z-listmap-001
352:   method: workflow.requirements.listMappings
353:   params:
354:     frId: FR-MCP-001
355: ```
356: 
357: ### Creating a Mapping
358: 
359: ```yaml
360: type: request
361: payload:
362:   requestId: req-20260409T120012Z-createmap-001
363:   method: workflow.requirements.createMapping
364:   params:
365:     frId: FR-MCP-001
366:     trIds:
367:       - TR-MCP-ARCH-001
368:     testIds:
369:       - TEST-MCP-001
370:     notes: Core authentication flow covered by ARCH constraint and unit test
371: ```
372: 
373: Legacy single-link `trId` and `testId` inputs are accepted for compatibility. Prefer `trIds` and `testIds` for all new calls.
374:

399:     trId: TR-MCP-ARCH-001
400: ```

402: ## Document Generation
403: 
404: To generate formatted requirements documents from the current workspace database slice:
405: 
406: ```yaml
407: type: request
408: payload:
409:   requestId: req-20260409T120014Z-gendoc-001
410:   method: workflow.requirements.generateDocument
411:   params:
412:     format: markdown
413:     docType: matrix
414: ```
415: 
416: Valid `docType` values:
417: 
418: - `functional` - numbered list of all FR entries with status and description
419: - `technical` - numbered list of all TR entries grouped by area/subarea
420: - `testing` - numbered list of all TEST entries with linked FR IDs
421: - `matrix` - traceability matrix table: FR × TR × TEST × status
422: - `all` - complete export package
423: 
424: ```yaml
425: type: result
426: payload:
427:   requestId: req-20260409T120014Z-gendoc-001
428:   result:
429:     content: |
430:       # Requirement Traceability Matrix
431: 
432:       | FR ID      | TR ID           | TEST ID      | Status |
433:       |------------|-----------------|--------------|--------|
434:       | FR-MCP-001 | TR-MCP-ARCH-001 | TEST-MCP-001 | done   |
435:       | FR-MCP-002 | TR-MCP-ARCH-002 | TEST-MCP-003 | open   |
436:     format: markdown
437:     docType: matrix
438:     generatedAt: 2026-04-09T12:00:14Z
439: ```

471: ## Bulk Ingestion
472: 
473: To import requirements from an existing Markdown document:
474: 
475: ```yaml
476: type: request
477: payload:
478:   requestId: req-20260409T120015Z-ingest-001
479:   method: workflow.requirements.ingestDocument
480:   params:

484:       Priority: high | Area: MCP | Status: pending
485: 
486:       ## TR-MCP-GRAPH-001: Chunked text embedding
487:       Ingested text must be split into chunks and embedded using all-MiniLM-L6-v2.
488:       Priority: high | Area: MCP | Subarea: GRAPH | Status: pending
489:     format: markdown
490: ```
491: 
492: To import wiki documents, pass a path-keyed `documents` map and include `lastModifiedUtc` per entry when available. Use `sourceFormat: auto` or `wiki`; set `preferredWikiFormat: azure|github` only when the Azure and GitHub timestamp checks disagree. The server compares both `.mcp-requirements-manifest.json` `generatedAtUtc` values and the latest `lastModifiedUtc` per platform. If both checks agree, the newer platform is selected. If they disagree and no preference is supplied, import fails. The selected platform folder is authoritative: missing records are deleted, changed records are updated, new records are created, and identical records are ignored.
493: 
494: ```yaml
495: type: request
496: payload:
497:   requestId: req-20260409T120015Z-ingest-wiki-001
498:   method: workflow.requirements.ingestDocument
499:   params:
500:     format: wiki
501:     sourceFormat: wiki
502:     preferredWikiFormat: github

505:         content: '{"generatedAtUtc":"2026-04-09T12:00:14Z"}'
506:         lastModifiedUtc: 2026-04-09T12:00:14Z

508:         content: |

511: ```
512: 
513: The server parses the document, creates, updates, deletes, or ignores matching FR/TR/TEST/mapping records, and returns a summary:
514: 
515: ```yaml
516: type: result
517: payload:
518:   requestId: req-20260409T120015Z-ingest-001
519:   result:
520:     created: 2
521:     updated: 0
522:     skipped: 0
523:     errors: []

526: ## Error Handling
527: 
528: Common error codes:
529: 
530: - `requirement_not_found` - no requirement with the given ID
531: - `requirement_already_exists` - ID already in use; update instead of create
532: - `invalid_requirement_id` - ID does not match the expected regex for its type
533: - `mapping_not_found` - mapping between the specified FR and TR does not exist
534: - `invalid_mapping` - mapping references a non-existent FR, TR, or TEST ID
535: - `document_generation_error` - failed to render the requested document format
536: - `document_ingestion_error` - could not parse or persist the ingested document
537: 
538: ## Workflow Recommendations
539: 
540: When discovering or agreeing on new requirements during a session:
541: 
542: 1. Create the FR record immediately using `workflow.requirements.createFr`
543: 2. Create the corresponding TR records using `workflow.requirements.createTr`
544: 3. Create the TEST record using `workflow.requirements.createTest`
545: 4. Link them with `workflow.requirements.createMapping`
546: 5. Include the new IDs in the session log turn tags via `workflow.sessionlog.updateTurn`
547: 
548: Capture requirements as they emerge; do not defer to end of session. Requirements traceability is validated in CI and build failures result from missing mappings.

6: 
7: # TODO Management
8: 
9: ## Overview
10: 
11: To interact with project TODOs, use the `workflow.todo.*` REPL command namespace through `lib/repl-invoke.ps1` via the `PowerShell.MCP wrapper`. The wrapper accepts the documented params, validates them, and sends a single-line JSON request envelope to `PowerShell.MCP wrapper`. Direct stdio callers must use the same shape: one single-line JSON request envelope per message, not formatted YAML. The server returns a `type: result` or `type: error` envelope on stdout. Streaming commands additionally emit a sequence of `type: event` envelopes before the final result.
12: 
13: The YAML blocks in this skill illustrate the logical structure of each envelope for readability; the actual wire format is single-line JSON.
14: 
15: ## Session Log Bootstrap
16: 
17: Before using any workflow commands, call `workflow.sessionlog.bootstrap` to initialize the session log subsystem:
18: 
19: ```yaml
20: type: request
21: payload:
22:   requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-bootstrap-001
23:   method: workflow.sessionlog.bootstrap
24:   params: {}
25: ```
26: 
27: This call is idempotent and should be made once per conversation context.
28: 
29: ## Usage Guidance
30: 
31: Use TODO data to refine or confirm the current plan after checking session/task state. Do not start with TODO enumeration when session state already identifies the active task.
32: 
33: ## Internal TODO Tracking Toggle
34: 
35: By default, the agent keeps transient checklist state locally and uses MCP TODOs only when the task needs durable workspace TODO tracking. To make MCP TODOs the backing store for durable plan items in a workspace:
36: 
37: ```yaml
38: type: request
39: payload:
40:   requestId: req-20260409T115900Z-todo-internal-enable
41:   method: workflow.todo.internal.enable
42:   params: {}
43: ```
44: 
45: To turn it off:
46: 
47: ```yaml
48: type: request
49: payload:
50:   requestId: req-20260409T115901Z-todo-internal-disable
51:   method: workflow.todo.internal.disable
52:   params: {}
53: ```
54: 
55: `workflow.todo.internal.status` reports the active state and whether it came from the cached setting, default behavior, or an environment override. An environment-variable override, when set, takes precedence over the cached setting for the current process: set it to `1` to force-enable internal tracking or `0` to force-disable it. The plugin defines the specific override variable name.
56: 
57: ## TODO ID Naming Conventions
58: 
59: Persist only IDs that conform to one of two patterns:
60: 
61: - `^[A-Z]+-[A-Z0-9]+-\d{3}$`: three-segment uppercase kebab-case, e.g. `PLAN-NAMINGCONVENTIONS-001`, `MCP-AUTH-042`
62: - `^ISSUE-\d+$`: GitHub-backed canonical ID, e.g. `ISSUE-17`
63: 
64: The special create-only value `ISSUE-NEW` instructs the server to create a GitHub issue, rewrite the stored ID to `ISSUE-{number}`, and return the canonical form. After the first sync, the `description` / `body` of an `ISSUE-{number}` TODO is immutable from the server side; subsequent update calls surface the change as a GitHub issue comment instead of overwriting the body.
65: 
66: When populating `dependsOn`, each dependency ID must also conform to these patterns.
67: 
68: ## Querying TODOs
69: 
70: To retrieve a filtered list of TODOs:
71: 
72: ```yaml
73: type: request
74: payload:
75:   requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-query-001
76:   method: workflow.todo.query
77:   params:
78:     keyword: authentication
79:     priority: high
80:     section: Backend
81:     done: false
82: ```
83: 
84: All `params` fields are optional. Omit `params` entirely to return all TODOs. The response contains a paginated `items` array:
85: 
86: ```yaml
87: type: result
88: payload:
89:   requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-query-001
90:   result:
91:     items:
92:       - id: MCP-AUTH-001
93:         title: Implement JWT authentication
94:         section: Backend
95:         priority: high
96:         done: false
97:         estimate: 4h
98:         functionalRequirements: [FR-AUTH-001]
99:         technicalRequirements: [TR-AUTH-001]
100:     totalCount: 1
101: ```
102: 
103: Valid `priority` values: `critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`.
104: 
105: ## Getting a Single TODO
106: 
107: To fetch the full detail of one TODO by ID:
108: 
109: ```yaml
110: type: request
111: payload:
112:   requestId: req-20260409T120001Z-get-001
113:   method: workflow.todo.get
114:   params:
115:     id: MCP-AUTH-001
116: ```
117: 
118: The result includes all fields: `implementationTasks`, `description`, `technicalDetails`, `remaining`, `doneSummary`, `dependsOn`, requirement arrays, and timestamps.
119: 
120: ## Selecting a TODO as Active Context
121: 
122: To set a TODO as the active working context for the session:
123: 
124: ```yaml
125: type: request
126: payload:

135: ## Creating a TODO
136: 
137: To create a new project task:
138: 
139: ```yaml
140: type: request
141: payload:
142:   requestId: req-20260409T120003Z-create-001
143:   method: workflow.todo.create
144:   params:
145:     id: MCP-AUTH-002
146:     title: Add rate limiting to auth endpoints
147:     section: Backend
148:     priority: medium
149:     estimate: 2h
150:     description:
151:       - Implement sliding window rate limiter
152:       - Configure 100 requests per 15 minutes
153:     implementationTasks:
154:       - task: Create RateLimitMiddleware
155:         done: false
156:       - task: Write unit tests
157:         done: false
158:     dependsOn: [MCP-AUTH-001]
159:     functionalRequirements: [FR-AUTH-002]
160:     technicalRequirements: [TR-AUTH-002]
161: ```
162: 
163: Required fields: `id`, `title`, `section`, `priority`. All other fields are optional.
164: 
165: To create a GitHub-backed TODO and let the server assign a canonical `ISSUE-{number}` ID:
166: 
167: ```yaml
168: type: request
169: payload:
170:   requestId: req-20260409T120004Z-create-issue-001
171:   method: workflow.todo.create
172:   params:
173:     id: ISSUE-NEW
174:     title: Capture sync regression in token refresh
175:     section: Issues
176:     priority: high
177: ```
178: 
179: The result `item.id` will contain the assigned `ISSUE-{number}` value.
180: 
181: ## Updating a TODO
182: 
183: To modify fields of an existing TODO:
184: 
185: ```yaml
186: type: request
187: payload:
188:   requestId: req-20260409T120005Z-update-001
189:   method: workflow.todo.update
190:   params:
191:     id: MCP-AUTH-001
192:     remaining: Integration tests still needed
193:     implementationTasks:
194:       - task: Create TokenService
195:         done: true
196:       - task: Create JwtValidator
197:         done: true
198:       - task: Add integration tests
199:         done: false
200: ```
201: 
202: Only include fields to change. To mark a TODO complete, set `done: true` and supply a `doneSummary`:
203: 
204: ```yaml
205: type: request
206: payload:
207:   requestId: req-20260409T120006Z-update-done-001
208:   method: workflow.todo.update
209:   params:
210:     id: MCP-AUTH-001
211:     done: true
212:     doneSummary: JWT authentication implemented and all tests passing
213: ```
214: 
215: To update the currently selected TODO without repeating the ID:
216: 
217: ```yaml
218: type: request
219: payload:
220:   requestId: req-20260409T120007Z-updatesel-001
221:   method: workflow.todo.updateSelected
222:   params:
223:     remaining: Need to add OpenAPI annotations
224: ```
225: 
226: ## Deleting a TODO
227: 
228: To remove a TODO permanently:
229: 
230: ```yaml
231: type: request
232: payload:
233:   requestId: req-20260409T120008Z-delete-001
234:   method: workflow.todo.delete
235:   params:
236:     id: MCP-AUTH-002
237: ```
238: 
239: ## Streaming Status Analysis
240: 
241: To request an AI-driven status analysis of a TODO, showing blockers and dependency state:
242: 
243: ```yaml
244: type: request
245: payload:
246:   requestId: req-20260409T120009Z-status-001
247:   method: workflow.todo.streamStatus
248:   params:
249:     id: MCP-AUTH-001
250: ```
251: 
252: The server emits a sequence of progress events followed by a completion event:
253: 
254: ```yaml
255: type: event
256: payload:
257:   event: workflow.todo.streamStatus
258:   data:
259:     eventType: status.progress
260:     sequence: 1
261:     timestamp: 2026-04-09T12:00:09Z
262:     message: Analyzing TODO dependencies...
263:     progress: 25
264: ---
265: type: event
266: payload:
267:   event: workflow.todo.streamStatus
268:   data:
269:     eventType: status.complete
270:     sequence: 4
271:     timestamp: 2026-04-09T12:00:12Z
272:     todoId: MCP-AUTH-001
273:     status: ready
274:     blockers: []
275:     dependencies: [MCP-AUTH-002]
276: ```
277: 
278: ## Streaming Plan Generation
279: 
280: To generate an implementation plan for a TODO and stream the result:
281: 
282: ```yaml
283: type: request
284: payload:
285:   requestId: req-20260409T120010Z-plan-001
286:   method: workflow.todo.streamPlan
287:   params:
288:     id: MCP-AUTH-001
289: ```
290: 
291: Events follow the same `eventType: plan.progress` / `eventType: plan.complete` pattern as status streaming. The completion event includes a structured plan document.
292: 
293: ## Streaming Implementation Execution
294: 
295: To execute an AI-driven implementation run for a TODO and stream progress:
296: 
297: ```yaml
298: type: request
299: payload:
300:   requestId: req-20260409T120011Z-implement-001
301:   method: workflow.todo.streamImplement
302:   params:
303:     id: MCP-AUTH-001
304: ```
305: 
306: Implementation events carry `eventType: implement.progress` and a final `eventType: implement.complete` with a results summary. Handle cancellation by sending a cancellation request; the stream emits a `eventType: status.cancelled` terminal event.
307: 
308: ## Analyzing Requirements for a TODO
309: 
310: To trigger requirements analysis and surface missing FR/TR traceability:
311: 
312: ```yaml
313: type: request
314: payload:
315:   requestId: req-20260409T120012Z-analyze-001
316:   method: workflow.todo.analyzeRequirements
317:   params:
318:     id: MCP-AUTH-001
319: ```
320: 
321: The result lists any detected requirement gaps and suggests FR/TR IDs to associate with the TODO.
322: 
323: ## Error Handling
324: 
325: Error envelopes include a structured `code` field:
326: 
327: ```yaml
328: type: error
329: payload:
330:   requestId: req-20260409T120003Z-create-001
331:   code: invalid_todo_id
332:   message: TODO ID does not conform to canonical format
333:   details:
334:     providedId: mcp-auth-001
335:     expectedFormat: "^[A-Z]+-[A-Z0-9]+-\\d{3}$"
336: ```
337: 
338: Common error codes:
339: 
340: - `todo_not_found`: no TODO with the specified ID
341: - `todo_already_exists`: a TODO with the same ID already exists
342: - `invalid_todo_id`: ID violates naming convention
343: - `no_selection`: `updateSelected` called with no active selection
344: - `stream_error`: a streaming operation failed mid-stream
345: 
346: ## Implementation Notes
347: 
348: - Use `Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1` from `lib/repl-invoke.ps1` to build and send envelopes via `PowerShell.MCP wrapper`.
349: - The `requestId` must match `^req-\d{8}T\d{6}Z-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$` for every envelope.
350: - All streaming operations may be cancelled by closing stdin or sending a cancellation request; the REPL guarantees a final cancellation event before closing the stream.
351: - After marking a TODO done, record the action in the active session log turn using `workflow.sessionlog.appendActions` with `type: edit` and the TODO ID as context.

16: ## 1. Scope, relationship to the foundation, and precedence
17: 
18: - Scope: the durable, multi-agent hostile validation (HV) pipeline the foundation deferred (foundation section 3.1, "Model grade": "We are going to add an HV pipeline in the future, but not in this effort."). 19: - Relationship: the foundation stays the authority for turn logging (Phase A), turn reviews (Phase B), and stateless agent context (Phase C). This amendment adds one bounded context, HostileValidation, and amends the foundation clauses listed in section 6, which are exactly the clauses that assume a manual HV with one configured grader.
20: - Precedence: where section 6 names a foundation clause as amended, the amendment's text governs; every other foundation clause stands unchanged. Because the foundation's plan (PLAN-SESSIONTURNREVIEW-001) was approved on 2026-10-10, the amended clauses are a change to that plan, and the foundation's own rule applies to them: "a change to this document after the plan is approved is a plan change that needs a new hostile validation" (foundation, introduction).

24: ## 2. Goals and non-goals
25: 
26: Goals:
27: 
28: 1. A durable HV queue whose admission, scheduling, ownership, and finalization survive server restarts, worker crashes, and concurrent workers without losing or duplicating a review result.
29: 2. A reviewer pool of five agents (Cline, Copilot, Claude, Codex, Grok), selected round-robin among the ready reviewers, never the submitter, the agent that wrote the reviewed turns, or an alias of either.
30: 3. Complete evidence: the complete accepted request and the complete response log of every review, compressed at rest with GZIP, verified lossless, retained until explicitly removed, and streamed live while the review runs.
31: 4. Per-turn assessments and a separate holistic evaluation for every request, committed atomically with the turns' hostile reviews; reviewed turns and final results are immutable.
32: 5. Independence: an agent's self-review never affects HV admission, execution, or verdict, and an HV verdict never completes a TODO.
33: 
34: Non-goals (each settled by the operator, section 3): access roles; a force re-review flag; automatic TODO state changes; automatic retention expiry; execution time limits; a second HV verdict store beside this one for turn reviews.

139: ## 5. Design decisions and resolutions
140: 
141: Each resolution names the settled requirements it implements, its rationale, and the alternatives it rejects. Resolutions are proposals for the operator's approval; the settled requirements of section 3 are not reopened.
142: 
143: - R-01 One bounded context. HostileValidation owns the pipeline and is not gated by `Mcp:AgentContext:Mode`: HV of turns works in every Mode, because the operator's HV requirements (S-01 to S-30) name turns, not agent-context responses. Rejected: extending the foundation's `AgentContextHvRequest` in ResponsesAndTrust (draft 103), because that record is mode-gated (foundation section 3.5.1) and lists responses, not turns, so a turn with no response would silently drop out of review (draft 213, "turn coverage versus response coverage").
144: - R-02 The HV request replaces the foundation's agent-context HV request. `HvRequest` keeps the foundation's key format `hvr-<sessionId>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>` (with `-<nn>` from the second key of one second, ReadableKeyAllocator) and lists turns (`HvRequestTurn`); the agent responses of those turns are linked as `HvRequestResponse` items when Phase C has recorded any. CreateAgentContextHvRequestCommand, GetAgentContextHvRequestQuery, QueryAgentContextHvRequestsQuery, and their entities are superseded (amendment A-04). Rejected: keeping two HV request records (one per turn, one per response), which would need a cross-record consistency rule the foundation never needed.
145: - R-03 Model grades come from finalization only. FinalizeHvRequestCommand dispatches the foundation's RecordModelGradeCommand for each linked response inside its own transaction; the public model-grade route, the two-step `codex exec resume` protocol, and `ModelGrader:*` are removed, and the eight receipt checks become the verification steps V-1 to V-8 of policy HvFinalVerification against evidence the server itself captured (amendment A-05). Rationale: the pipeline launches the reviewer and records its complete output, so the server no longer has to trust receipts written by a runner it did not control. Rejected: keeping the reviewer-submitted grade route beside the pipeline, which would let a grade bypass reviewer exclusion and atomic finalization (S-17, S-23).
146: - R-04 Freeze at admission, finality at finalization (S-06, S-07). Admission sets each member turn's HV state to `Pending` in the same transaction that creates the request; finalization sets it to `Final`. Every write to a `Pending` or `Final` turn or its children, from every surface and origin, is refused with 409 `turn_immutable` and `details.reason` `hv_pending` or `hv_final` (policy HvTurnFreeze), except the one write of finalization itself (origin `HvFinalization`). A request that ends `Canceled` or `Failed` releases its turns back to `None`. Rationale: the reviewed content equals the finalized content without a content comparison race, and the operator's "may not allow updates" is one guard in the existing write path. Rejected: letting writes continue and refusing finalization on a changed snapshot hash, which would waste completed reviews and still leave a window between the last check and the commit.
147: - R-05 Only terminal turns are admitted. A member turn that is not terminal (`TurnStatus.IsTerminal`, foundation section 3.5.3) refuses the whole request with 409 `hv_turns_not_terminal`, naming each turn. The submitting turn is never a member: a session scope excludes it and reports the exclusion in the result, and a turn or range scope that names it is refused with 400 `hv_scope_includes_submitting_turn` (the foundation's rule that "the request's own turn is never a candidate, a dependency, or cited evidence", foundation section 3.1). A Code or Docs turn that needs HV before it can complete is completed first with `hostileReview` `Other` (for example "HV requested hvr-..."), which the foundation already allows and never counts as an AGREE (foundation C8); finalization then replaces that `Other` with the HV result. Rationale: no turn changes status after it is frozen, so there is no close-inside-finalization path. Rejected: admitting in-progress turns with a declared close intent (draft 213, section 3.B), which adds a mechanism and still freezes a turn the model is working in.
148: - R-06 Hostile reviews are written only by the pipeline. On agent surfaces a `hostileReview` write may carry only `status` `Other` (with its required `otherNotes`); a write naming `Pass`, `Fail`, or `Running`, or carrying `hvVerdict`, is refused with 403 `review_hostile_pipeline_only` (amendment A-06). Process ConvertHvReceiptToReview is retired. Rationale: a manual Pass or Fail would bypass reviewer exclusion, complete evidence, and atomic finalization, and no surface may bypass them (draft 213, H5, adopted). Rejected: keeping the manual route for emergencies; a reviewer can be enabled and checked instead (S-27).
149: - R-07 Assignment at admission, durable round-robin. The submit transaction picks the next eligible reviewer after the workspace's round-robin cursor and advances the cursor in the same SerializableWrite (policy RoundRobinAssignment), so assignment survives restarts and two concurrent submissions never pick from the same cursor value. When the assigned reviewer is no longer eligible at claim time (offline, disabled), the claim reassigns through the same policy and records the reassignment. Rejected: assignment at claim only, which hides the assignee from the submitter and lets claim order, not round-robin order, pick reviewers.
150: - R-08 One agent identity, server-attributed. `AgentIdentity` (namespace `QBrainAi.Client.Agents`, shared by the server, the REPL, and, through the golden contract, the PowerShell core) maps every known alias to one of the five reviewer ids: Claude (`claude`, `claudecode`, `claude-code`, `claudecowork`, `claude-cowork`, `cowork`), Codex (`codex`), Copilot (`copilot`), Grok (`grok`, `grokcode`, `grok-code`, `grokbot`, `grok-bot`), Cline (`cline`, `cline-v2`, `clinev2`), case-insensitively and ignoring separators. The submitter is the agent of the submitting turn, located by its full turn key (TurnLocator); a free-text name never overrides it. The author is the agent of the reviewed session (one request names turns of one MCP session, R-26), stored normalized as `AuthorReviewerId`. A reviewer whose id equals the submitter's or the author's is never eligible (S-17, S-28, P-01, P-07). Develop holds three alias maps with different canonical forms (`src/QBrainAi.Repl.Host/MarkerFileClientOptionsResolver.cs:64-81`, `src/QBrainAi.Repl.Core/TodoSelectionStore.cs:166-171`, the plugin's `Get-ReplCanonicalAgentName`); they are context under the DRY ruling and are not changed by this amendment. Exclusion is by agent family, not by model vendor (D-01, settled): S-17 names "the agent submitting the review", P-01 constrains the agent family and asks separately for the agent and the model, and the operator runs Cline on `gpt-6-astra` (provider `openai-codex`, VI-01 receipt) while keeping Cline and Codex as two reviewers (S-02); a model a reviewer shares with the submitter stays visible in the run's provenance, and the operator can disable that reviewer (UpdateHvReviewerCommand). Exclusion covers the author as well as the submitter (D-05, settled): a review by the agent that wrote the turns is a self-review, which S-28 rules out of HV and P-07 rules out of validation.
151: - R-09 Operator submissions. A caller with no session-log turn (Director, an operator at the REPL) submits with `submitter.kind` `Operator` and a name; no reviewer is excluded for the submitter, and the author of the reviewed session is still excluded (R-08). Agent surfaces (plugin verbs, MCP tools, the REPL workflow verb) always send the submitting turn's key, which the plugin binds automatically (foundation process BindVerbToTurn). Limit (section 8): every caller holds the same workspace key, so the server cannot prove that an `Operator` submission did not come from an agent.
152: - R-10 Readiness through NONCE (S-15, S-27). A reviewer is `Unverified`, `Online`, or `Offline`, and separately enabled or disabled. "NONCE the agent" is a probe run of the reviewer through its adapter with a fresh random nonce: it passes when the reviewer answers with the probe record that echoes the nonce and the adapter's runtime provenance shows the reviewer's resolved model and effort (P-04). Only a passing NONCE moves a reviewer to `Online`. An execution failure moves it to `Offline` until a later NONCE passes. The worker host NONCEs every enabled `Unverified` reviewer at startup and after a configuration change; an `Offline` reviewer is NONCEd only when a caller asks (S-15: "until resolved"). Rejected: a liveness ping or the server health nonce, which S-27 rules out.
153: - R-11 No execution time limit (P-02). A run has no timeout and no deadline. Liveness is the worker's lease, renewed by heartbeats; a stalled run stays visible (`lastOutputUtc`, the last progress record) and anyone can cancel it (S-18). The only expiry is the lease of a dead worker (R-13). This replaces the 30-minute `ExecutionTimeout` of the separate HostileReview options (`src/QBrainAi.Services/Options/HostileReviewWorkerOptions.cs:45-46`) for HV runs only. The process exit code is never the outcome of a run: the reviewer's records decide it (V-8 for a review, policy ReadinessProbeVerdict for a probe), because a CLI can end a refused or empty run with exit code 0 (VI-03: a headless Grok run whose write call was refused ended `cancelled` with exit 0, and two Copilot permission variants exited 0 with no output).
154: - R-12 True live output (S-22, P8). Each reviewer adapter delivers every output line as the process writes it, through a line callback, never after the process ends; the worker appends lines in batches (at most `OutputFlushInterval`, default 250 ms, or `OutputFlushBytes`, default 64 KiB, whichever comes first) through AppendHvRunOutputCommand, which stores each batch as one GZIP chunk and wakes the streams. The output stream replays stored chunks and then follows new ones (shared component OrderedEventReplay). Develop's one-shot strategy yields its output only after completion (`src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy.cs:57-75`), so the adapters need a real line path (section 21, P8). Acceptance criterion FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008-AC003 makes the difference testable: a line is observable on the stream while the reviewer process is still running. The reviewer's records are read from each agent message's complete text, assembled from the CLI's native events (Grok's `streaming-json` sends message text one token per event, and Copilot sends deltas and then the whole message, as the probe runs of 2026-10-16 show), by one extraction function that the worker runs as lines arrive and finalization runs over the stored log (section 16.3), so a record split across events is read exactly once and both read the same records (FR-MCP-HVPIPE-010-AC006).
155: - R-13 Leases and fences (handoff requirement 10). A run is owned through a lease (owner, expiry) and a fence token that increases on every claim and takeover, the pattern develop already uses for handoff ingestion (owner and expiry with a `StateVersion` takeover, `src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/HandoffIngestionService.cs:724-735`, and a fenced terminal write that matches owner and version, `:782-807`). Every worker write carries the fence; a write with a stale fence changes nothing and returns `stale_fence`, and the worker that receives it stops its process. Expired leases are swept (ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand): the attempt becomes `Abandoned` and the request is queued again until `MaxAttemptsPerRequest` (default 3) is spent, then `Failed`, or `Canceled` when a cancel was requested; policy HvRetryDecision writes that outcome, with its turn release and its notification, for the sweep exactly as for FailHvRunCommand. Rejected: the unused lease options of the HostileReview subsystem (`HostileReviewWorkerOptions.cs:30-46`), which no code reads (section 21, P1).
156: - R-14 Evidence in the relational store, GZIP at rest (S-13, S-29, S-30). The accepted request is one GZIP blob written at admission; the response log is the run's ordered GZIP chunks; the result document is one GZIP blob written at finalization. No uncompressed copy of an evidence item is stored in the evidence tables, and each evidence item is stored there once (the structured rows of section 12, such as the request's `Context` and the findings, are records the units derive, not copies of the evidence blobs). The audit ledger keeps its own history of every evidence write, as it does for every audited entity: develop's ledger snapshots every property of an audited entity, binary columns included (`src/QBrainAi.Storage/McpDbContext.cs:1540-1589`), compressed with GZIP (`src/QBrainAi.Storage/Entities/DataAuditLogEntity.cs:119-147`), and a removal never changes it (R-20, I-13). Retrieval returns `application/gzip` (download name `<hvRequestId>-<kind>.jsonl.gz` or `.json.gz`) or, when asked, the decompressed bytes. The pattern is develop's audit ledger, which stores GZIP payloads in the database (`src/QBrainAi.Storage/Entities/DataAuditLogEntity.cs:66-147`). Rationale: S-23 ("Single trx at end") and S-29 (the database audit log) both hold only when the evidence is in the same transactional store as the result, and no crash window between a file system and the database remains. Rejected: `.jsonl.gz` files beside the database, which would need a two-store protocol, keep evidence outside the audit ledger, and split backups.
157: - R-15 Atomic finalization (S-23). FinalizeHvRequestCommand verifies the evidence and the reviewer output before it opens a transaction, then commits in one SerializableWrite: the result document, the per-turn assessments, the holistic evaluation, the failures, each turn's `hostileReview` through policy HvVerdictMapping (origin `HvFinalization`), each turn's `Final` HV state, the linked responses' model grades and trust decisions (when Mode is not `Off`), the request's `Completed` state, its notification, and the audit rows. The transaction re-checks everything the earlier reads relied on (the run's fence, the chunk manifest, the request and turn states). Crash windows are in section 9.
158: - R-16 Transactional notification outbox (S-19). Every state change that callers observe writes an `HvNotification` row in its own transaction, numbered by a per-workspace sequence that the same transaction advances, so the sequence has no gaps and no row is visible before its change commits. The notification stream replays rows after the caller's `Last-Event-ID` and then follows new ones (OrderedEventReplay). Delivery is at least once; consumers deduplicate by sequence. `IChangeEventBus` (develop's in-memory bus, `src/QBrainAi.Services/Notifications/IChangeEventBus.cs:4`) is used only to wake waiting streams and the worker, never as the record.
159: - R-17 Incidents through the triage endpoint (S-15, S-26). An execution failure writes an `HvIncident` row in the failure's transaction; FileHvIncidentCommand then submits it through `ITriageService` with its `dedupeKey` (`hv-reviewer-<reviewerId>-<failureCode>` for a failure attributable to the reviewer, `hv-server-<failureCode>` otherwise, section 12), which triage groups as `dedupe:<key>` (`src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/TriageService.cs:1475-1476`), and records the returned report and group ids. A filing that fails stays `Pending` and is retried by the worker host's sweep. Rejected: new incident tables with their own deduplication (S-26: "File through endpoint").
160: - R-18 Honest ETA (S-18, P-03). The ETA a caller sees is the reviewer's own latest progress record (`percentComplete`, `etaSeconds`), with `etaStatus` `Reported` and the record's time; with no progress record it is `etaStatus` `Unknown` and no number. The server never estimates.
161: - R-19 Audit participation and hard stop (S-29). Every HV entity carries `IsDeleted`, so `McpDbContext` writes its ledger rows for every HV mutation in the same `SaveChanges` (develop audits only entities with that property, `src/QBrainAi.Storage/McpDbContext.cs:1620-1627`). The ledger is append-only for HV: no HV unit or process updates or deletes a ledger row (I-13). Because develop skips the ledger when the audit table is unavailable (`McpDbContext.cs:1507-1538`), every HV unit first calls the shared component AuditLedgerGuard, which refuses with 503 `audit_unavailable` and writes nothing when the ledger cannot be written. Evidence reads (GetHvEvidenceQuery, GetHvResultQuery, the output stream, and GetHvRequestQuery when it returns output lines) write an explicit `read` ledger row before returning bytes, and a read whose row cannot be written is refused (the "protected-log access" of draft 213 participates in the audit log, S-29).
162: - R-20 Retention until removal (S-29). No unit deletes, expires, or compacts HV evidence except RemoveHvEvidenceCommand, an explicit call that removes the evidence bytes of one request, keeps its result rows, hashes, and sizes, records who removed it and why, and is audited. It clears the evidence tables only and never changes or deletes an audit ledger row: the ledger keeps the history of the evidence's writes and gains the record of the removal, because an audit log is never purged (I-13). There are no roles: any caller with the workspace key can call it, as S-29 requires.
163: - R-21 Self-review independence (S-28). No HV unit, policy, or process reads `agentReview`. The turn snapshot sent to a reviewer omits both review records (shared component TurnSnapshotBuilder), so a reviewer never sees a self-review grade. S-12 (a plugin list of missing agent reviews) is met by the foundation's Stop-gate remedy, which already lists each open turn's missing `agentReview` (foundation section 3.4, Stop gate, and `Get-CloseRemedy`, section 3.5.6), and is not an HV input. Reconciliation with the foundation's completion gate: HV admits only terminal turns (R-05), and the foundation's gate needs an `agentReview` status of `Pass`, `Fail`, or `Other` before a turn can close `completed` (foundation section 5.3, CompletionPolicy); that is a rule of closing a turn, not of HV, it is met by `Other` with a note as well as by a grade, and a turn closed `failed` or `canceled` needs no agent review at all; HV admission, execution, and verdict read none of it, and FR-MCP-HVPIPE-013 proves that every terminal turn is admitted and judged identically whatever its self-review.
164: - R-22 Verdict only (S-25). No HV unit writes TODO state. A result names the reviewed turns' `todoId` values for information only.
165: - R-23 Requirement references (S-14). The submitted context is stored as written (Markdown, YAML, or text, declared by `contextFormat`) and parsed for requirement references: FR, TR, and TEST ids of the form `<KIND>-<AREA>-<NNN>` with optional further dash-separated area segments, acceptance criteria written as `<FR id>-AC<NNN>` or `<FR id> ac-<n>`, and use cases by their store id or exact title. Each reference is resolved against the workspace's effective requirements and use cases and handed to the reviewer as a delineated list with its resolution status; an unresolved reference is listed as unresolved, never refused (shared component RequirementReferenceExtractor).
166: - R-24 The reviewer's own turn (P-06). The brief tells the reviewer to log its review as its own session-log turn, classified `Chore` so that its turn never needs an HV of its own (foundation completion policy: Chore needs no hostile review), and to store its entire result there. Finalization requires that turn to exist, to be persisted (not a failsafe or queued record), to have been created at or after the run's claim, to be closed `completed` as a `Chore`, and to contain every reviewer record of the run byte for byte in its stored normal form (V-6). A reviewer whose host cannot log turns fails its NONCE with `reviewer_turn_logging_unsupported`. The reviewer's plugin runs as a host session of its own: a review or probe run never reads or changes the plugin state or the session-log session of a live session of the same agent in the workspace (FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008-AC008), which matters because a reviewer starts in the workspace (section 16.2) and Grok's headless hooks write their host state under the working directory's `.mcpServer/grok/` (VI-04).
167: - R-25 The HostileReview subsystem stays separate. FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-001 to -006 (its queue, artifact links, findings, and query surface) are not changed by this amendment, as the foundation already states (foundation section 5.4); the problems found in it (section 21, P1 to P3) are tracked in REMED-HVPIPELINE-001. It stays separate (D-02, settled): it reviews artifacts (TODO, FR/TR/TEST, plans, files, commits; FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-002) while this pipeline reviews session turns (S-03), the approved foundation keeps it separate, and consolidating it is scope the operator has not named. Its missing worker (P1) has its own contract (section 16.7) and shares only the execution primitives that fit it (the reviewer adapters' launch builder, live-line path, and containment, and FencedLease), so reviewer execution exists once (the DRY ruling); nothing of this pipeline's evidence model applies to it, because FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-002 forbids storing a raw artifact or an assembled prompt.
168: - R-26 Scope limits. One request names turns of one MCP session. `MaxTurnsPerRequest` (default 200, the foundation's `HvRequest:MaxTurns` default) bounds every scope; a session scope above it is refused with 400 `hv_scope_too_large` naming the count, never truncated.
169: - R-27 One open review per turn. A turn is `Pending` in at most one open request (a unique filtered index on the turn key where the item is `Pending`); admission over a pending turn is refused with 409 `hv_turns_pending` naming the turns and their requests, and over a final turn with 409 `hv_turns_already_reviewed` (S-06, S-20).
170: - R-28 Cancellation by anyone (S-18). `Queued` becomes `Canceled` at once; `Running` becomes `CancelRequested`, and the worker stops the process at its next heartbeat and closes the run `Canceled`; a repeat on a `CancelRequested` or `Canceled` request returns 200 unchanged; `Finalizing`, `Completed`, and `Failed` refuse with 409 `hv_request_not_cancelable`. A cancel, a close, and a finalization of the same request are serialized on the request row, so exactly one of them commits first and the others see its state: a close that finds `CancelRequested` ends the run `Canceled` instead of making the request `Finalizing`, so an accepted cancellation is never lost (CloseHvRunOutputCommand).
171: - R-29 Worker units are internal. ClaimHvRunCommand, RecordHvRunStartCommand, RecordHvRunHeartbeatCommand, AppendHvRunOutputCommand, CloseHvRunOutputCommand, FailHvRunCommand, ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand, FinalizeHvRequestCommand, and FileHvIncidentCommand have no REST route, MCP tool, or client method; only the worker host dispatches them, in-process, through `IDispatcher`. The public mutations are submit, cancel, reviewer update, NONCE, and evidence removal.
172: - R-30 Plugins consume notifications through the REPL. Plugins never call REST (foundation section 3); the REPL gains a streaming verb that follows the notification stream, and the PowerShell core runs it in the background per host session (process WatchHvNotifications), keeping the last sequence and the inbox in one state file of the host session, so one atomic replace records both, and handing completions of requests that host session's MCP session submitted to the next prompt as context. A terminal notification carries the submitter's turn key (section 12), so the watcher matches it by that key and needs no local record of the submission, and a completion that arrives before the submit verb has returned is still delivered. Delivery to the model is at least once: a crash between adding a completion to a prompt and recording it delivered can repeat it, and each entry carries its sequence so a repeat is recognizable (the outbox rule of R-16).
173: - R-31 The 98/98 bar for the overall verdict (P-05), one predicate stated once here. The overall verdict is `AGREE` exactly when all of these hold: the holistic correctness and completeness both meet `max(configured hostile threshold, 0.98)` (ScoreVerdict, foundation section 3.5.4) and the holistic verdict is `AGREE`; every member turn's verdict is `AGREE`; every response grade of an admitted response that is still `Pending` at commit is `AGREE` under the foundation's `verdict_match` rule; and no finding of any scope (turn, holistic, or response) is FAIL or UNKNOWN. Otherwise it is `DISAGREE`. Per-turn hostile reviews keep the foundation's configured hostile thresholds through HvVerdictMapping. V-4 checks the reviewer's overall verdict against this predicate.
