139: ## 5. Design decisions and resolutions
140: 
141: Each resolution names the settled requirements it implements, its rationale, and the alternatives it rejects. Resolutions are proposals for the operator's approval; the settled requirements of section 3 are not reopened.
142: 
143: - R-01 One bounded context. HostileValidation owns the pipeline and is not gated by `Mcp:AgentContext:Mode`: HV of turns works in every Mode, because the operator's HV requirements (S-01 to S-30) name turns, not agent-context responses. Rejected: extending the foundation's `AgentContextHvRequest` in ResponsesAndTrust (draft 103), because that record is mode-gated (foundation section 3.5.1) and lists responses, not turns, so a turn with no response would silently drop out of review (draft 213, "turn coverage versus response coverage").
144: - R-02 The HV request replaces the foundation's agent-context HV request. `HvRequest` keeps the foundation's key format `hvr-<sessionId>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>` (with `-<nn>` from the second key of one second, ReadableKeyAllocator) and lists turns (`HvRequestTurn`); the agent responses of those turns are linked as `HvRequestResponse` items when Phase C has recorded any. CreateAgentContextHvRequestCommand, GetAgentContextHvRequestQuery, QueryAgentContextHvRequestsQuery, and their entities are superseded (amendment A-04). Rejected: keeping two HV request records (one per turn, one per response), which would need a cross-record consistency rule the foundation never needed.
145: - R-03 Model grades come from finalization only. FinalizeHvRequestCommand dispatches the foundation's RecordModelGradeCommand for each linked response inside its own transaction; the public model-grade route, the two-step `codex exec resume` protocol, and `ModelGrader:*` are removed, and the eight receipt checks become the verification steps V-1 to V-8 of policy HvFinalVerification against evidence the server itself captured (amendment A-05). Rationale: the pipeline launches the reviewer and records its complete output, so the server no longer has to trust receipts written by a runner it did not control. Rejected: keeping the reviewer-submitted grade route beside the pipeline, which would let a grade bypass reviewer exclusion and atomic finalization (S-17, S-23).
146: - R-04 Freeze at admission, finality at finalization (S-06, S-07). Admission sets each member turn's HV state to `Pending` in the same transaction that creates the request; finalization sets it to `Final`. Every write to a `Pending` or `Final` turn or its children, from every surface and origin, is refused with 409 `turn_immutable` and `details.reason` `hv_pending` or `hv_final` (policy HvTurnFreeze), except the one write of finalization itself (origin `HvFinalization`). A request that ends `Canceled` or `Failed` releases its turns back to `None`. Rationale: the reviewed content equals the finalized content without a content comparison race, and the operator's "may not allow updates" is one guard in the existing write path. Rejected: letting writes continue and refusing finalization on a changed snapshot hash, which would waste completed reviews and still leave a window between the last check and the commit.
147: - R-05 Only terminal turns are admitted. A member turn that is not terminal (`TurnStatus.IsTerminal`, foundation section 3.5.3) refuses the whole request with 409 `hv_turns_not_terminal`, naming each turn. The submitting turn is never a member: a session scope excludes it and reports the exclusion in the result, and a turn or range scope that names it is refused with 400 `hv_scope_includes_submitting_turn` (the foundation's rule that "the request's own turn is never a candidate, a dependency, or cited evidence", foundation section 3.1). A Code or Docs turn that needs HV before it can complete is completed first with `hostileReview` `Other` (for example "HV requested hvr-..."), which the foundation already allows and never counts as an AGREE (foundation C8); finalization then replaces that `Other` with the HV result. Rationale: no turn changes status after it is frozen, so there is no close-inside-finalization path. Rejected: admitting in-progress turns with a declared close intent (draft 213, section 3.B), which adds a mechanism and still freezes a turn the model is working in.
148: - R-06 Hostile reviews are written only by the pipeline. On agent surfaces a `hostileReview` write may carry only `status` `Other` (with its required `otherNotes`); a write naming `Pass`, `Fail`, or `Running`, or carrying `hvVerdict`, is refused with 403 `review_hostile_pipeline_only` (amendment A-06). Process ConvertHvReceiptToReview is retired. Rationale: a manual Pass or Fail would bypass reviewer exclusion, complete evidence, and atomic finalization, and no surface may bypass them (draft 213, H5, adopted). Rejected: keeping the manual route for emergencies; a reviewer can be enabled and checked instead (S-27).
149: - R-07 Assignment at admission, durable round-robin. The submit transaction picks the next eligible reviewer after the workspace's round-robin cursor and advances the cursor in the same SerializableWrite (policy RoundRobinAssignment), so assignment survives restarts and two concurrent submissions never pick from the same cursor value. When the assigned reviewer is no longer eligible at claim time (offline, disabled), the claim reassigns through the same policy and records the reassignment. Rejected: assignment at claim only, which hides the assignee from the submitter and lets claim order, not round-robin order, pick reviewers.
150: - R-08 One agent identity, server-attributed. `AgentIdentity` (namespace `QBrainAi.Client.Agents`, shared by the server, the REPL, and, through the golden contract, the PowerShell core) maps every known alias to one of the five reviewer ids: Claude (`claude`, `claudecode`, `claude-code`, `claudecowork`, `claude-cowork`, `cowork`), Codex (`codex`), Copilot (`copilot`), Grok (`grok`, `grokcode`, `grok-code`, `grokbot`, `grok-bot`), Cline (`cline`, `cline-v2`, `clinev2`), case-insensitively and ignoring separators. The submitter is the agent of the submitting turn, located by its full turn key (TurnLocator); a free-text name never overrides it. The author is the agent of the reviewed session (one request names turns of one MCP session, R-26), stored normalized as `AuthorReviewerId`. A reviewer whose id equals the submitter's or the author's is never eligible (S-17, S-28, P-01, P-07). Develop holds three alias maps with different canonical forms (`src/QBrainAi.Repl.Host/MarkerFileClientOptionsResolver.cs:64-81`, `src/QBrainAi.Repl.Core/TodoSelectionStore.cs:166-171`, the plugin's `Get-ReplCanonicalAgentName`); they are context under the DRY ruling and are not changed by this amendment. Exclusion is by agent family, not by model vendor (D-01, settled): S-17 names "the agent submitting the review", P-01 constrains the agent family and asks separately for the agent and the model, and the operator runs Cline on `gpt-6-astra` (provider `openai-codex`, VI-01 receipt) while keeping Cline and Codex as two reviewers (S-02); a model a reviewer shares with the submitter stays visible in the run's provenance, and the operator can disable that reviewer (UpdateHvReviewerCommand). Exclusion covers the author as well as the submitter (D-05, settled): a review by the agent that wrote the turns is a self-review, which S-28 rules out of HV and P-07 rules out of validation.
151: - R-09 Operator submissions. A caller with no session-log turn (Director, an operator at the REPL) submits with `submitter.kind` `Operator` and a name; no reviewer is excluded for the submitter, and the author of the reviewed session is still excluded (R-08). Agent surfaces (plugin verbs, MCP tools, the REPL workflow verb) always send the submitting turn's key, which the plugin binds automatically (foundation process BindVerbToTurn). Limit (section 8): every caller holds the same workspace key, so the server cannot prove that an `Operator` submission did not come from an agent.
152: - R-10 Readiness through NONCE (S-15, S-27). A reviewer is `Unverified`, `Online`, or `Offline`, and separately enabled or disabled. "NONCE the agent" is a probe run of the reviewer through its adapter with a fresh random nonce: it passes when the reviewer answers with the probe record that echoes the nonce and the adapter's runtime provenance shows the reviewer's resolved model and effort (P-04). Only a passing NONCE moves a reviewer to `Online`. An execution failure moves it to `Offline` until a later NONCE passes. The worker host NONCEs every enabled `Unverified` reviewer at startup and after a configuration change; an `Offline` reviewer is NONCEd only when a caller asks (S-15: "until resolved"). Rejected: a liveness ping or the server health nonce, which S-27 rules out.
153: - R-11 No execution time limit (P-02). A run has no timeout and no deadline. Liveness is the worker's lease, renewed by heartbeats; a stalled run stays visible (`lastOutputUtc`, the last progress record) and anyone can cancel it (S-18). The only expiry is the lease of a dead worker (R-13). This replaces the 30-minute `ExecutionTimeout` of the separate HostileReview options (`src/QBrainAi.Services/Options/HostileReviewWorkerOptions.cs:45-46`) for HV runs only. The process exit code is never the outcome of a run: the reviewer's records decide it (V-8 for a review, policy ReadinessProbeVerdict for a probe), because a CLI can end a refused or empty run with exit code 0 (VI-03: a headless Grok run whose write call was refused ended `cancelled` with exit 0, and two Copilot permission variants exited 0 with no output).
154: - R-12 True live output (S-22, P8). Each reviewer adapter delivers every output line as the process writes it, through a line callback, never after the process ends; the worker appends lines in batches (at most `OutputFlushInterval`, default 250 ms, or `OutputFlushBytes`, default 64 KiB, whichever comes first) through AppendHvRunOutputCommand, which stores each batch as one GZIP chunk and wakes the streams. The output stream replays stored chunks and then follows new ones (shared component OrderedEventReplay). Develop's one-shot strategy yields its output only after completion (`src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy.cs:57-75`), so the adapters need a real line path (section 21, P8). Acceptance criterion FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008-AC003 makes the difference testable: a line is observable on the stream while the reviewer process is still running. The reviewer's records are read from each agent message's complete text, assembled from the CLI's native events (Grok's `streaming-json` sends message text one token per event, and Copilot sends deltas and then the whole message, as the probe runs of 2026-10-16 show), by one extraction function that the worker runs as lines arrive and finalization runs over the stored log (section 16.3), so a record split across events is read exactly once and both read the same records (FR-MCP-HVPIPE-010-AC006).
155: - R-13 Leases and fences (handoff requirement 10). A run is owned through a lease (owner, expiry) and a fence token that increases on every claim and takeover, the pattern develop already uses for handoff ingestion (owner and expiry with a `StateVersion` takeover, `src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/HandoffIngestionService.cs:724-735`, and a fenced terminal write that matches owner and version, `:782-807`). Every worker write carries the fence; a write with a stale fence changes nothing and returns `stale_fence`, and the worker that receives it stops its process. Expired leases are swept (ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand): the attempt becomes `Abandoned` and the request is queued again until `MaxAttemptsPerRequest` (default 3) is spent, then `Failed`, or `Canceled` when a cancel was requested; policy HvRetryDecision writes that outcome, with its turn release and its notification, for the sweep exactly as for FailHvRunCommand. Rejected: the unused lease options of the HostileReview subsystem (`HostileReviewWorkerOptions.cs:30-46`), which no code reads (section 21, P1).
156: - R-14 Evidence in the relational store, GZIP at rest (S-13, S-29, S-30). The accepted request is one GZIP blob written at admission; the response log is the run's ordered GZIP chunks; the result document is one GZIP blob written at finalization. No uncompressed copy of an evidence item is stored in the evidence tables, and each evidence item is stored there once (the structured rows of section 12, such as the request's `Context` and the findings, are records the units derive, not copies of the evidence blobs). The audit ledger keeps its own history of every evidence write, as it does for every audited entity: develop's ledger snapshots every property of an audited entity, binary columns included (`src/QBrainAi.Storage/McpDbContext.cs:1540-1589`), compressed with GZIP (`src/QBrainAi.Storage/Entities/DataAuditLogEntity.cs:119-147`), and a removal never changes it (R-20, I-13). Retrieval returns `application/gzip` (download name `<hvRequestId>-<kind>.jsonl.gz` or `.json.gz`) or, when asked, the decompressed bytes. The pattern is develop's audit ledger, which stores GZIP payloads in the database (`src/QBrainAi.Storage/Entities/DataAuditLogEntity.cs:66-147`). Rationale: S-23 ("Single trx at end") and S-29 (the database audit log) both hold only when the evidence is in the same transactional store as the result, and no crash window between a file system and the database remains. Rejected: `.jsonl.gz` files beside the database, which would need a two-store protocol, keep evidence outside the audit ledger, and split backups.
157: - R-15 Atomic finalization (S-23). FinalizeHvRequestCommand verifies the evidence and the reviewer output before it opens a transaction, then commits in one SerializableWrite: the result document, the per-turn assessments, the holistic evaluation, the failures, each turn's `hostileReview` through policy HvVerdictMapping (origin `HvFinalization`), each turn's `Final` HV state, the linked responses' model grades and trust decisions (when Mode is not `Off`), the request's `Completed` state, its notification, and the audit rows. The transaction re-checks everything the earlier reads relied on (the run's fence, the chunk manifest, the request and turn states). Crash windows are in section 9.
158: - R-16 Transactional notification outbox (S-19). Every state change that callers observe writes an `HvNotification` row in its own transaction, numbered by a per-workspace sequence that the same transaction advances, so the sequence has no gaps and no row is visible before its change commits. The notification stream replays rows after the caller's `Last-Event-ID` and then follows new ones (OrderedEventReplay). Delivery is at least once; consumers deduplicate by sequence. `IChangeEventBus` (develop's in-memory bus, `src/QBrainAi.Services/Notifications/IChangeEventBus.cs:4`) is used only to wake waiting streams and the worker, never as the record.
159: - R-17 Incidents through the triage endpoint (S-15, S-26). An execution failure writes an `HvIncident` row in the failure's transaction; FileHvIncidentCommand then submits it through `ITriageService` with its `dedupeKey` (`hv-reviewer-<reviewerId>-<failureCode>` for a failure attributable to the reviewer, `hv-server-<failureCode>` otherwise, section 12), which triage groups as `dedupe:<key>` (`src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/TriageService.cs:1475-1476`), and records the returned report and group ids. A filing that fails stays `Pending` and is retried by the worker host's sweep. Rejected: new incident tables with their own deduplication (S-26: "File through endpoint").
160: - R-18 Honest ETA (S-18, P-03). The ETA a caller sees is the reviewer's own latest progress record (`percentComplete`, `etaSeconds`), with `etaStatus` `Reported` and the record's time; with no progress record it is `etaStatus` `Unknown` and no number. The server never estimates.
161: - R-19 Audit participation and hard stop (S-29). Every HV entity carries `IsDeleted`, so `McpDbContext` writes its ledger rows for every HV mutation in the same `SaveChanges` (develop audits only entities with that property, `src/QBrainAi.Storage/McpDbContext.cs:1620-1627`). The ledger is append-only for HV: no HV unit or process updates or deletes a ledger row (I-13). Because develop skips the ledger when the audit table is unavailable (`McpDbContext.cs:1507-1538`), every HV unit first calls the shared component AuditLedgerGuard, which refuses with 503 `audit_unavailable` and writes nothing when the ledger cannot be written. Evidence reads (GetHvEvidenceQuery, GetHvResultQuery, the output stream, and GetHvRequestQuery when it returns output lines) write an explicit `read` ledger row before returning bytes, and a read whose row cannot be written is refused (the "protected-log access" of draft 213 participates in the audit log, S-29).
162: - R-20 Retention until removal (S-29). No unit deletes, expires, or compacts HV evidence except RemoveHvEvidenceCommand, an explicit call that removes the evidence bytes of one request, keeps its result rows, hashes, and sizes, records who removed it and why, and is audited. It clears the evidence tables only and never changes or deletes an audit ledger row: the ledger keeps the history of the evidence's writes and gains the record of the removal, because an audit log is never purged (I-13). There are no roles: any caller with the workspace key can call it, as S-29 requires.
163: - R-21 Self-review independence (S-28). No HV unit, policy, or process reads `agentReview`. The turn snapshot sent to a reviewer omits both review records (shared component TurnSnapshotBuilder), so a reviewer never sees a self-review grade. S-12 (a plugin list of missing agent reviews) is met by the foundation's Stop-gate remedy, which already lists each open turn's missing `agentReview` (foundation section 3.4, Stop gate, and `Get-CloseRemedy`, section 3.5.6), and is not an HV input. Reconciliation with the foundation's completion gate: HV admits only terminal turns (R-05), and the foundation's gate needs an `agentReview` status of `Pass`, `Fail`, or `Other` before a turn can close `completed` (foundation section 5.3, CompletionPolicy); that is a rule of closing a turn, not of HV, it is met by `Other` with a note as well as by a grade, and a turn closed `failed` or `canceled` needs no agent review at all; HV admission, execution, and verdict read none of it, and FR-MCP-HVPIPE-013 proves that every terminal turn is admitted and judged identically whatever its self-review.
164: - R-22 Verdict only (S-25). No HV unit writes TODO state. A result names the reviewed turns' `todoId` values for information only.
165: - R-23 Requirement references (S-14). The submitted context is stored as written (Markdown, YAML, or text, declared by `contextFormat`) and parsed for requirement references: FR, TR, and TEST ids of the form `<KIND>-<AREA>-<NNN>` with optional further dash-separated area segments, acceptance criteria written as `<FR id>-AC<NNN>` or `<FR id> ac-<n>`, and use cases by their store id or exact title. Each reference is resolved against the workspace's effective requirements and use cases and handed to the reviewer as a delineated list with its resolution status; an unresolved reference is listed as unresolved, never refused (shared component RequirementReferenceExtractor).
166: - R-24 The reviewer's own turn (P-06). The brief tells the reviewer to log its review as its own session-log turn, classified `Chore` so that its turn never needs an HV of its own (foundation completion policy: Chore needs no hostile review), and to store its entire result there. Finalization requires that turn to exist, to be persisted (not a failsafe or queued record), to have been created at or after the run's claim, to be closed `completed` as a `Chore`, and to contain every reviewer record of the run byte for byte in its stored normal form (V-6). A reviewer whose host cannot log turns fails its NONCE with `reviewer_turn_logging_unsupported`. The reviewer's plugin runs as a host session of its own: a review or probe run never reads or changes the plugin state or the session-log session of a live session of the same agent in the workspace (FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008-AC008), which matters because a reviewer starts in the workspace (section 16.2) and Grok's headless hooks write their host state under the working directory's `.mcpServer/grok/` (VI-04).
167: - R-25 The HostileReview subsystem stays separate. FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-001 to -006 (its queue, artifact links, findings, and query surface) are not changed by this amendment, as the foundation already states (foundation section 5.4); the problems found in it (section 21, P1 to P3) are tracked in REMED-HVPIPELINE-001. It stays separate (D-02, settled): it reviews artifacts (TODO, FR/TR/TEST, plans, files, commits; FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-002) while this pipeline reviews session turns (S-03), the approved foundation keeps it separate, and consolidating it is scope the operator has not named. Its missing worker (P1) has its own contract (section 16.7) and shares only the execution primitives that fit it (the reviewer adapters' launch builder, live-line path, and containment, and FencedLease), so reviewer execution exists once (the DRY ruling); nothing of this pipeline's evidence model applies to it, because FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-002 forbids storing a raw artifact or an assembled prompt.
168: - R-26 Scope limits. One request names turns of one MCP session. `MaxTurnsPerRequest` (default 200, the foundation's `HvRequest:MaxTurns` default) bounds every scope; a session scope above it is refused with 400 `hv_scope_too_large` naming the count, never truncated.
169: - R-27 One open review per turn. A turn is `Pending` in at most one open request (a unique filtered index on the turn key where the item is `Pending`); admission over a pending turn is refused with 409 `hv_turns_pending` naming the turns and their requests, and over a final turn with 409 `hv_turns_already_reviewed` (S-06, S-20).
170: - R-28 Cancellation by anyone (S-18). `Queued` becomes `Canceled` at once; `Running` becomes `CancelRequested`, and the worker stops the process at its next heartbeat and closes the run `Canceled`; a repeat on a `CancelRequested` or `Canceled` request returns 200 unchanged; `Finalizing`, `Completed`, and `Failed` refuse with 409 `hv_request_not_cancelable`. A cancel, a close, and a finalization of the same request are serialized on the request row, so exactly one of them commits first and the others see its state: a close that finds `CancelRequested` ends the run `Canceled` instead of making the request `Finalizing`, so an accepted cancellation is never lost (CloseHvRunOutputCommand).
171: - R-29 Worker units are internal. ClaimHvRunCommand, RecordHvRunStartCommand, RecordHvRunHeartbeatCommand, AppendHvRunOutputCommand, CloseHvRunOutputCommand, FailHvRunCommand, ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand, FinalizeHvRequestCommand, and FileHvIncidentCommand have no REST route, MCP tool, or client method; only the worker host dispatches them, in-process, through `IDispatcher`. The public mutations are submit, cancel, reviewer update, NONCE, and evidence removal.
172: - R-30 Plugins consume notifications through the REPL. Plugins never call REST (foundation section 3); the REPL gains a streaming verb that follows the notification stream, and the PowerShell core runs it in the background per host session (process WatchHvNotifications), keeping the last sequence and the inbox in one state file of the host session, so one atomic replace records both, and handing completions of requests that host session's MCP session submitted to the next prompt as context. A terminal notification carries the submitter's turn key (section 12), so the watcher matches it by that key and needs no local record of the submission, and a completion that arrives before the submit verb has returned is still delivered. Delivery to the model is at least once: a crash between adding a completion to a prompt and recording it delivered can repeat it, and each entry carries its sequence so a repeat is recognizable (the outbox rule of R-16).
173: - R-31 The 98/98 bar for the overall verdict (P-05), one predicate stated once here. The overall verdict is `AGREE` exactly when all of these hold: the holistic correctness and completeness both meet `max(configured hostile threshold, 0.98)` (ScoreVerdict, foundation section 3.5.4) and the holistic verdict is `AGREE`; every member turn's verdict is `AGREE`; every response grade of an admitted response that is still `Pending` at commit is `AGREE` under the foundation's `verdict_match` rule; and no finding of any scope (turn, holistic, or response) is FAIL or UNKNOWN. Otherwise it is `DISAGREE`. Per-turn hostile reviews keep the foundation's configured hostile thresholds through HvVerdictMapping. V-4 checks the reviewer's overall verdict against this predicate.

214: - `Queued` and `Running` hold the turns `Pending`. `Completed`, `Failed`, and `Canceled` are terminal and never change again (S-06, S-20). A request whose attempt fails returns to `Queued` with its assignment re-evaluated (R-07); with no eligible reviewer it stays `Queued`, its ETA `Unknown`, until a reviewer passes a NONCE or the request is canceled, so no work is lost to an outage.
215: - `CancelRequested` is not terminal: the request is canceled when the worker has stopped the process, when its run closes or fails first (CloseHvRunOutputCommand and FailHvRunCommand through policy HvRetryDecision, R-28), or when the lease of a dead worker expires.

217: ### 7.2 Run attempt
218: 
219: ```mermaid
220: stateDiagram-v2
221:     [*] --> Claimed: ClaimHvRunCommand, lease and fence
222:     Claimed --> Running: RecordHvRunStartCommand, process started
223:     Running --> Running: heartbeat renews the lease, output appended
224:     Running --> OutputClosed: CloseHvRunOutputCommand
225:     Claimed --> Failed: FailHvRunCommand, process never started, or worker_shutdown
226:     Running --> Failed: FailHvRunCommand, execution failure
227:     Running --> Canceled: cancel observed at a heartbeat
228:     OutputClosed --> Canceled: cancel found at close
229:     Claimed --> Abandoned: lease expired, ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand
230:     Running --> Abandoned: lease expired, ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand
231:     OutputClosed --> Succeeded: FinalizeHvRequestCommand committed, or probe passed
232:     OutputClosed --> Failed: verification failed, or probe failed
233:     Succeeded --> [*]
234:     Failed --> [*]
235:     Abandoned --> [*]
236:     Canceled --> [*]
237: ```
238: 
239: A run is either a `Review` run of an HV request or a `Probe` run of a reviewer's NONCE (R-10); both use the same lease, fence, output, and close units, so the probe needs no second execution path.

241: ### 7.3 Reviewer readiness
242: 
243: ```mermaid
244: stateDiagram-v2
245:     [*] --> Unverified: seeded from configuration
246:     Unverified --> Online: NONCE probe passed
247:     Unverified --> Offline: NONCE probe failed
248:     Online --> Offline: execution failure, incident filed
249:     Offline --> Online: NONCE probe passed
250:     Online --> Unverified: strategy, agent path, model, or effort changed
251:     Offline --> Unverified: strategy, agent path, model, or effort changed
252: ```
253: 
254: `Enabled` is a separate flag set by UpdateHvReviewerCommand: a disabled reviewer is never eligible and is never NONCEd automatically, whatever its readiness. Eligibility (policy HvReviewerEligibility) is enabled, `Online`, and neither the submitter nor the author of the reviewed turns (R-08).

256: ### 7.4 HV state of a turn
257: 
258: ```mermaid
259: stateDiagram-v2
260:     [*] --> None
261:     None --> Pending: admitted by SubmitHvRequestCommand
262:     Pending --> None: request Canceled or Failed
263:     Pending --> Final: FinalizeHvRequestCommand
264:     Final --> [*]

267: While `Pending` or `Final`, policy HvTurnFreeze refuses every write to the turn and its children except finalization's own (A-07, A-08). A turn that already holds a `Pass` or `Fail` hostile review when the column is added starts `Final`, with no request id (A-11).

269: ## 8. Invariants and limits
270: 
271: Invariants, each owned by the named component and proved by the acceptance criteria of section 19:
272: 
273: - I-01 A turn is `Pending` in at most one open request, and a `Final` turn is never admitted again (R-27, HvAdmissionEligibility).
274: - I-02 The content a reviewer reviewed is the content finalized: no write reaches a `Pending` turn between admission and finalization (HvTurnFreeze), and finalization re-hashes each turn's snapshot and refuses on any difference (V-2).
275: - I-03 A request is finalized at most once; a second finalization returns the stored result and writes nothing (FinalizeHvRequestCommand).
276: - I-04 Nothing of a finalization is visible unless all of it is: result, per-turn assessments, holistic evaluation, failures, turn reviews, turn finality, grades, trust decisions, request state, notification, and audit rows commit together (R-15, S-23).
277: - I-05 Only the run that holds the current fence can append output, close output, or fail; a stale fence changes nothing (R-13).
278: - I-06 The response log of a finalized run is complete: its chunks are contiguous from sequence 1, each chunk's SHA-256 matches its decompressed bytes, the chain hash over the chunks' SHA-256 values equals the run's `OutputChainSha256` (section 12), every line parses as one JSON object, and the log contains exactly one `hv_verdict` record (V-1).
279: - I-07 The reviewer is never the submitter or the author of the reviewed turns, by canonical id (V-5, R-08).
280: - I-08 Varying a turn's `agentReview` (absent, any status, any score) changes neither admission, nor assignment, nor the brief's bytes, nor the verdict mapping (R-21).
281: - I-09 No HV unit changes TODO state (R-22).
282: - I-10 No HV write happens without its audit ledger rows (R-19).
283: - I-11 Evidence bytes are removed from the evidence tables only by RemoveHvEvidenceCommand (R-20).
284: - I-12 Every notification row is committed with the change it reports, and sequences are gap-free per workspace (R-16).
285: - I-13 The audit ledger is append-only: no HV unit or process updates or deletes a ledger row, and a removal of evidence leaves every earlier ledger row unchanged (R-19, R-20).
286: 
287: Limits stated plainly:
288: 
289: - L-01 Agent identity rests on the workspace key: every caller holds the same key, so the server cannot prove which agent sent a request. Exclusion is enforced against the agent of the submitting turn the server finds and the agent of the reviewed session; an `Operator` submission excludes only the author (R-09). This is the foundation's existing identity model (foundation section 6.3: "every agent of a workspace authenticates with the workspace key"), not a new weakness.
290: - L-02 A reviewer can run more than once for one request (at-least-once execution): a worker crash after the reviewer finished but before its output was closed leads to a new attempt. The request still finalizes at most once (I-03), and every attempt's output stays as evidence.
291: - L-03 Incident deduplication is per triage group: a filing retried after a crash between the triage commit and the recording of its report id can add a second report to the same group, never a second group (R-17).
292: - L-04 A reviewer CLI that cannot report its runtime model and effort cannot pass a NONCE, so it stays `Unverified` or `Offline` (R-10, P-04). Verified on 2026-10-16 (VI-01): Codex, Claude, Grok, and Copilot record both in their own run records; Cline records the model and only whether thinking was on, never the effort level, so Cline cannot pass a NONCE until it records the effort of a run (D-06, settled: P-04 fails closed).
293: 
294: ## 9. Crash windows and recovery
295: 
296: Each window names what is durable at the crash and what recovers it. "Sweep" is the worker host's periodic pass (process HvWorkerHost).
297: 
298: - W-01 Crash after the submit commit, before the worker wakes: the request is `Queued` in the store; the next poll claims it.
299: - W-02 Crash after a claim, before RecordHvRunStartCommand commits (the process may or may not have started; a started one ends with the worker, W-03): the run's lease expires; the sweep marks the attempt `Abandoned` and the request `Queued`, or `Failed` or `Canceled` with its turns released when its attempts are spent or a cancel was requested (ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand, policy HvRetryDecision).
300: - W-03 Worker crash while the reviewer runs: the reviewer runs inside a containment bound to its worker process, so the reviewer and every descendant end when the worker dies, however abruptly (process RunReviewerProcess, FR-MCP-HVPIPE-007-AC008); no process is ever ended by a recorded process id, which the operating system can reuse. This is not a review deadline: only the worker's own death ends the run this way. The output already appended is durable; the lease expires and the sweep queues a new attempt. A worker that is alive but lost its lease (a pause longer than the lease) gets `stale_fence` on its next write and stops its process (I-05).
301: - W-04 Crash after the reviewer exits, before CloseHvRunOutputCommand commits: as W-03, a new attempt runs (L-02).
302: - W-05 Crash after CloseHvRunOutputCommand commits (request `Finalizing`), before finalization: the sweep dispatches FinalizeHvRequestCommand for every `Finalizing` request (idempotent, I-03).
303: - W-06 Crash or failure inside the finalization transaction: it rolls back; the request stays `Finalizing` and the sweep runs finalization again.
304: - W-07 Crash after the finalization commit, before any stream delivers its notification: the notification row is durable; streams and pollers replay it by sequence (R-16).
305: - W-08 Crash after an incident row commits, before triage filing: the incident stays `Pending`; the sweep files it (FileHvIncidentCommand).
306: - W-09 Crash after triage accepts a filing, before the report id is recorded: the retry files again under the same `dedupeKey`, which joins the same triage group (L-03).
307: - W-10 Cancel racing finalization, claim, or close: all of them change the request row inside SerializableWrite, so one commits first and the other sees the committed state (R-28).
308: - W-11 Two workers claiming one request: the claim is a conditional update on the request's state and version inside SerializableWrite; exactly one claim commits.
309: - W-12 The audit ledger becomes unavailable during a run: AppendHvRunOutputCommand refuses with 503 `audit_unavailable` and writes nothing; the worker stops the reviewer process (a hard stop, S-29), cannot record the failure while the ledger is down, and the lease expiry later queues a new attempt; nothing is ever reported complete without its audit rows.

311: ## 10. Configuration: `HostileValidationOptions`
312: 
313: Section `Mcp:HostileValidation`, declared under the canonical root as `QBrainAi: HostileValidation:` in `appsettings.yaml` and projected onto `Mcp:` by `CanonicalSectionProjectionProvider`, as foundation section 6.2 declares `AgentContext`; class `HostileValidationOptions` in `src/QBrainAi.Services/HostileValidation/HostileValidationOptions.cs` with `SectionName = "Mcp:HostileValidation"`, `Validate()`, and `ValidateOnStart()`; per instance through `McpInstanceResolver`.
314: 
315: - `Reviewers` (list): exactly one entry for each of `Cline`, `Copilot`, `Claude`, `Codex`, and `Grok` (S-02); each entry has `Enabled` (default true), `ExecutionStrategy` (an existing strategy name, `src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/IAgentExecutionStrategy.cs:6-46`), `AgentPath` (the CLI to launch), `Model` (null means the CLI's default model, recorded from the runtime provenance; Copilot needs a configured model, because its default `auto` routes each prompt to a model of its own choosing, which two probe prompts of 2026-10-16 showed by landing on `mai-code-1.1-flash` and `gpt-6-luna`, and it refuses `--reasoning-effort` without an explicit model, so V-7 could not hold, VI-02), `Effort` (null means the highest effort the reviewer's CLI accepts, verified on 2026-10-16 (VI-08): Codex `max` (its rollout recorded `effort` `max`), Claude `max` (its transcript recorded `effort` `max`), Cline `xhigh` (the highest `--thinking` level), Grok `xhigh` (Grok 1.0.60 refuses `max`: "unknown effort level 'max'; use one of: xhigh, high, medium, low"), and Copilot `max` (the highest `--reasoning-effort` value, which the configured model's NONCE proves); develop's one-shot constants at `OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy.cs:23-26` differ for Codex (`xhigh`) and Grok (`max`, which Grok refuses), problem P9), and `MaxConcurrentRuns` (default 1, 1..8).
316: - `MaxTurnsPerRequest` (default 200, 1..2000).
317: - `MaxAttemptsPerRequest` (default 3, 1..10).
318: - `LeaseDuration` (default 5 minutes) and `HeartbeatInterval` (default 60 seconds; must be less than half of `LeaseDuration`).
319: - `OutputFlushInterval` (default 250 milliseconds, 50..5000) and `OutputFlushBytes` (default 65536, 1024..4194304); the default interval is kept only after its storage cost is measured (VI-05).
320: - `PollInterval` (default 2 seconds) and `WorkerEnabled` (default true).
321: - There is no execution timeout and no output size limit (R-11, S-22: "Output should be captured live and streamed").
322: - Startup validation fails on an unknown or duplicate reviewer id, a missing one of the five, an unknown execution strategy, an enabled Copilot entry without a configured `Model`, or a value outside its range.
323: - Seeding: at startup each reviewer entry is inserted as an `HvReviewer` row when the workspace has none for its id (readiness `Unverified`); an existing row is never overwritten, because UpdateHvReviewerCommand is the real-time management surface (S-02), the pattern develop uses for agent definitions seeded per workspace (`SeedWorkspaceAgentsAsync`, `src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/IAgentPoolService.cs:83`).

325: ## 11. Shared components (new, each defined once)
326: 
327: The foundation's shared components (foundation section 3.5) are reused unchanged: SerializableWrite, IdempotentCreate with PayloadFingerprint, ReadableKeyAllocator, PagedQuery with PageBounds, ClassifiedErrorException with ErrorCodes, SecretRedactor, ContentHasher, TurnLocator, TurnWritePipeline, ScoreLexeme, ScoreVerdict, and WorkspaceResolutionBehavior. The components below are new; each has one implementation, one test class named for it, and one diagram here, and every unit that uses one draws it as a single call node.
328: 
329: ### 11.1 FencedLease (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Storage.Leases`)
330: 
331: Claims, renews, and takes over the lease of one row, and guards every fenced write, following develop's handoff-ingestion pattern (`HandoffIngestionService.cs:724-735,782-807`). Operations: `Claim(row, owner, duration)` (only when the row has no lease or an expired one; the fence token increments), `Renew(row, owner, fence, duration)`, `Guard(row, owner, fence)` (the precondition of every fenced write), `Release(row, owner, fence)`. Each runs inside the caller's SerializableWrite. Used by ClaimHvRunCommand, RecordHvRunStartCommand, RecordHvRunHeartbeatCommand, AppendHvRunOutputCommand, CloseHvRunOutputCommand, FailHvRunCommand, and ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand, and by the HostileReview worker's ClaimHostileReviewAttemptCommand, CompleteHostileReviewAttemptCommand, and ExpireHostileReviewLeasesCommand (section 16.7).
332: 
333: ```mermaid
334: flowchart TD
335:     S(["FencedLease: operation, row, owner, fence"]) --> OP{"Operation?"}
336:     OP -->|Claim| CL{"Lease absent or expired?"}
337:     CL -->|no| E1(["held: another owner holds a live lease"])
338:     CL -->|yes| CT["Set owner and expiry, increment the fence token"]
339:     CT --> OK1(["claimed: the new fence token"])
340:     OP -->|"Renew, Guard, or Release"| G{"Owner and fence equal the stored ones?"}
341:     G -->|no| E2(["stale_fence: nothing changed"])
342:     G -->|yes| W{"Operation?"}
343:     W -->|Renew| RN["Extend the expiry"]
344:     RN --> OK2(["renewed"])
345:     W -->|Guard| OK3(["guarded: the caller's write proceeds"])
346:     W -->|Release| RL["Clear owner and expiry"]
347:     RL --> OK4(["released"])
348: ```
349: 
350: ### 11.2 GzipCodec (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Storage.Compression`)
351: 
352: `Compress(bytes)` returns one GZIP member; `Decompress(bytes)` returns the original bytes; `RoundTrip(original, compressed)` decompresses and compares length and SHA-256 (through ContentHasher's hex form over raw bytes) and fails with `evidence_corrupt` on any difference, so no compressed blob is stored unverified. It follows `DataAuditLogEntity`'s encode and decode (`DataAuditLogEntity.cs:119-147`); that entity's private copy is context, not work. Used by SubmitHvRequestCommand (request evidence), AppendHvRunOutputCommand (chunks), FinalizeHvRequestCommand (result document, chunk verification), and GetHvRequestQuery, GetHvResultQuery, GetHvEvidenceQuery, and OrderedEventReplay (reads).
353: 
354: ```mermaid
355: flowchart TD
356:     S(["GzipCodec: operation, bytes"]) --> OP{"Operation?"}
357:     OP -->|Compress| C["Write one GZIP member at the configured level"]
358:     C --> RT[["GzipCodec RoundTrip on the result"]]
359:     RT -->|equal| OK1(["compressed bytes"])
360:     RT -->|different| E1(["evidence_corrupt"])
361:     OP -->|Decompress| D{"Valid GZIP member?"}
362:     D -->|no| E2(["evidence_corrupt"])
363:     D -->|yes| OK2(["original bytes"])
364:     OP -->|RoundTrip| R["Decompress, compare length and SHA-256 with the original"]
365:     R -->|equal| OK3(["equal"])
366:     R -->|different| E3(["evidence_corrupt"])
367: ```
368: 
369: ### 11.3 AuditLedgerGuard (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Storage.Auditing`)
370: 
371: `EnsureAvailable()` checks, inside the caller's transaction, that the `DataAuditLogs` table is writable and refuses with 503 `audit_unavailable` (`retryable: true`) when it is not, closing for HV the skip of `McpDbContext.AppendAuditRows` (`McpDbContext.cs:1507-1538`); `RecordRead(entityKind, entityKey, actor)` adds one ledger row with action `read` for an evidence access (R-19). Every HV unit calls `EnsureAvailable()` before any other step that writes; GetHvEvidenceQuery, GetHvResultQuery, the output stream, and GetHvRequestQuery when it returns output lines call `RecordRead` before returning bytes.
372: 
373: ```mermaid
374: flowchart TD
375:     S(["AuditLedgerGuard: operation"]) --> A{"DataAuditLogs writable in this transaction?"}
376:     A -->|no| E(["503 audit_unavailable, retryable: nothing written"])
377:     A -->|yes| OP{"Operation?"}
378:     OP -->|EnsureAvailable| OK1(["available"])
379:     OP -->|RecordRead| R["Add one ledger row: action read, entity kind and key, actor, request id"]
380:     R --> OK2(["read recorded with the caller's commit"])

435: ### 11.8 OrderedEventReplay (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Streaming`)
436: 
437: Serves a Server-Sent Events stream from durable ordered rows: parses `Last-Event-ID` (absent means from the beginning of the requested stream, a malformed value is 400 `validation_error` with `details.field` `Last-Event-ID`), sends every stored event after it in order with its `id:`, then waits on the `IChangeEventBus` wake-up (or a poll interval) and sends new rows; it sends a comment line every 15 seconds while idle so proxies keep the connection, and ends when the caller disconnects or the stream's source reaches a terminal event. Develop's event stream has no replay and no event ids (`src/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp/Controllers/EventStreamController.cs:27-92`); this component adds both without changing that controller. Used by StreamHvRunOutputQuery and StreamHvNotificationsQuery.
438: 
439: ```mermaid
440: flowchart TD
441:     S(["OrderedEventReplay: source, Last-Event-ID"]) --> P{"Last-Event-ID valid or absent?"}
442:     P -->|malformed| E(["400 validation_error, details.field Last-Event-ID"])
443:     P -->|yes| RD["Read stored events after the position, in order"]
444:     RD --> SND["Send each event with its id"]
445:     SND --> T{"Source terminal and all events sent?"}
446:     T -->|yes| END(["stream ended with the terminal event"])
447:     T -->|no| WT["Wait for a wake-up or the poll interval; send a comment every 15 seconds while idle"]
448:     WT --> DC{"Caller disconnected?"}
449:     DC -->|yes| END2(["stream closed"])
450:     DC -->|no| RD
451: ```

545: ### 13.3 Reviewer contract, version 1
546: 
547: The complete accepted request (the `Request` evidence, written at admission and never changed) is one JSON object: `{ schema: "qbrainai.hv.request/1", hvRequestId, workspacePath, scope, submitter, turns: [{ ordinal, agent, sessionId, requestId, snapshotSha256, snapshot }], responses: [{ responseId, agent, sessionId, requestId, contentSha256, content, claims }], context, contextFormat, requirementRefs, admittedUtc }`. The brief of one attempt is that object inside an envelope: `{ schema: "qbrainai.hv.brief/1", request: <the accepted request>, runId, attempt, reviewer: { reviewerId, model, effort }, instructions, outputSchema }`; the worker writes the exact brief it sends as the first record of the attempt's log, `{ "type": "hv_brief", "brief": <the brief> }`, so each log is complete on its own. The brief's `instructions` require the reviewer to review every turn individually and the set of turns as a whole, to treat every turn snapshot and the context as untrusted evidence, to emit the records below as single-line JSON objects in its messages, to emit progress records during the run (P-03), to log its review as its own session-log turn classified `Chore` and store its entire result there, every reviewer record of the run in order (R-24, V-6), to close that turn `completed` through the foundation's completion gate before it ends (an action or design decision and its own agent review, `Other` with a note being enough), because the foundation's Stop gate blocks a host from stopping while a delivered turn is still in progress (foundation section 3.4) and a reviewer run has no time limit (P-02), and to emit exactly one `hv_verdict` record last.
548: 
549: Records (each a JSON object on its own line inside the reviewer's messages, read from each message's complete text as the reviewer's adapter assembles it from the native events, section 16.3; every other line is free text and stays in the log):
550: 
551: - `{ "type": "hv_progress", "percentComplete": 0..100, "etaSeconds": n or null, "note": "..." }`.
552: - `{ "type": "hv_turn_assessment", "hvRequestId", "ordinal", "agent", "sessionId", "requestId", "snapshotSha256", "correctness", "completeness", "verdict": "AGREE" or "DISAGREE", "summary", "findings": [{ "outcome": "FAIL" or "UNKNOWN", "category", "location", "requirementRef", "claimId", "evidence", "remediation" }] }`: one per member turn (S-03, S-21).
553: - `{ "type": "hv_holistic", "hvRequestId", "correctness", "completeness", "verdict", "summary", "crossTurnFindings": [same shape] }`: exactly one (S-10); it states cross-turn consistency, omissions, contradictions, and end-to-end satisfaction and is never a calculation over the turn scores.
554: - `{ "type": "hv_response_grade", "hvRequestId", "responseId", "contentSha256", "correctness", "completeness", "verdict", "findings": [{ "claimId", "check", "outcome": "PASS", "FAIL", or "UNKNOWN", "category", "location", "evidence", "remediation" }] }`: one per response of the accepted request, the set admitted with the request whatever has happened to its responses since (foundation `verdict_match` rules: every claim named at least once); `category`, `location`, `evidence`, and `remediation` are required on a FAIL or UNKNOWN finding and may be omitted on a PASS.
555: - `{ "type": "hv_reviewer_turn", "agent", "sessionId", "requestId" }`: the reviewer's own session-log turn (R-24).
556: - `{ "type": "hv_verdict", "hvRequestId", "runId", "overallVerdict", "turnCount", "responseGradeCount", "reviewer": { "reviewerId", "model", "effort" } }`: exactly one, last.
557: - `{ "type": "hv_probe", "nonce", "model", "effort" }`: the answer to a NONCE probe brief (R-10). A probe brief asks for this record and, as a review brief does, for the reviewer's own `Chore` turn and its `hv_reviewer_turn` record (R-24); policy ReadinessProbeVerdict reads both.
558: 
559: The response log is the reviewer process's complete output as JSONL: the worker's `hv_brief` record first; then, when the adapter runs the CLI in a JSON streaming mode, each native event line as written, and otherwise each output line wrapped as `{ "type": "hv_raw", "stream": "stdout" or "stderr", "line": "..." }`; and, after the process exits, the adapter's provenance lines `{ "type": "hv_provenance", "model", "effort", "source", "sourceSha256" }`, which name the runtime receipt they were read from and its hash (P-04). The adapter extracts the reviewer's records from the agent message text of the native events (section 16.3). `hv_brief`, `hv_raw`, and `hv_provenance` are written only by the worker as top-level log lines and are never accepted from the reviewer's message text, so a reviewer cannot forge them.

561: ### 13.4 Standard result document (S-13)
562: 
563: `GET /requests/{hvRequestId}/result` returns `HvResultDocument`:
564: 
565: `{ schema: "qbrainai.hv.result/1", hvRequestId, status, scope, submitter, reviewer: { reviewerId, expectedModel, expectedEffort, runtimeModel, runtimeEffort, runId, attempt, reviewerAgent, reviewerSessionId, reviewerRequestId }, request: <the complete accepted request of section 13.3>, responseLog: [<every JSONL record of the finalized run, in order, starting with its hv_brief record>], turnAssessments: [{ ordinal, agent, sessionId, requestId, correctness, completeness, verdict, mappedReviewStatus, summary, findings }], holistic: { correctness, completeness, verdict, summary, crossTurnFindings }, failures: [{ ordinal, scope, turnOrdinal, agent, sessionId, requestId, responseId, check, outcome, category, location, requirementRef, claimId, evidence, remediation }], responseGrades: [{ responseId, disposition, gradeId, verdict, correctness, completeness, findings }], overallVerdict, thresholds: { correctness, completeness }, evidence: { request: { sha256, bytes, compressedBytes }, responseLog: { chainSha256, bytes, lines, chunks }, result: { sha256 } }, todoIds: [string], finalizedUtc }`.
566: 
567: - `turnAssessments` lists every requested turn with its score (S-21); `failures` is the delineated list of every FAIL and UNKNOWN of every scope (`Turn`, `Holistic`, `Response`), each with its remediation (S-13); `responseGrades` lists every response of the accepted request with its grade record and findings, and its `disposition` (`Graded`, or `Closed` when the response left the review before the commit, whose grade record is kept here but applied to nothing); `request` and `responseLog` are complete (S-13); `evidence.result.sha256` is `ResultSha256`, the digest of the stored `Result` payload, which excludes this field (section 12); `todoIds` is information only (R-22).
568: - With `Accept-Encoding: gzip` the document is sent compressed; the `responseLog` array is streamed from the chunks, so the server holds no uncompressed copy (R-14).
569: - Before finalization the route answers 409 `hv_result_not_ready` with the request's status; after evidence removal it answers 410 `hv_evidence_removed` with the hashes and sizes it still holds.

571: ### 13.5 Streams
572: 
573: - Output stream: event `hv_output` with `id` `<runId>:<sequence>` and data `{ runId, sequence, lines: [string] }`, one event per stored chunk; event `hv_run_closed` with data `{ runId, status }` when the run ends; a new attempt starts a new run id in the same stream, so `Last-Event-ID` `<runId>:<sequence>` resumes after that chunk of that run. Per S-18 a caller attaches to "any running hv": the stream serves the request's runs in attempt order.

685: ### 14.2 Admission, queries, and cancellation

687: #### SubmitHvRequestCommand: admit an HV request [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-002, -004, -005, -006, -007, -011, -013, -018]
688: 
689: - Handler: `SubmitHvRequestCommand(string WorkspacePath, SubmitHvRequestRequest Request) : ICommand<HvRequestResult>`.
690: - Callers: any agent or operator; the plugin verb `workflow.hv.submit` binds the submitting turn automatically (process SubmitHvFromPlugin, section 16.4).
691: - Order of checks:
692:   1. Shape (no store read): the scope fields for its kind (400 `hv_scope_invalid` with `details.field`), the submitter fields for its kind (400 `validation_error` with `details.field` under `submitter`), a nonblank `idempotencyKey` of at most 128 characters, `contextFormat` known and `context` at most 65536 characters (400 `validation_error`).
693:   2. Reads before the transaction (foundation section 3.1, "Database-only delegates"): RequirementReferenceExtractor over `context`.
694:   3. SerializableWrite delegate: AuditLedgerGuard; IdempotentCreate on `IdempotencyKey` (policy `Conflict`, fingerprint of the client inputs): the same inputs return 200 with the stored request, other inputs 409 `conflict` with `retryable: false`; TurnLocator on the submitting turn for `submitter.kind` `Agent` (`InvalidIdentifier`, `SessionNotFound`, or `TurnNotFound` is 400 `validation_error` with `details.field` `submitter`); policy HvScopeResolution; policy HvAdmissionEligibility; policy RoundRobinAssignment; then the inserts.
695:   4. Inserts in the delegate: the `hvr-` key (ReadableKeyAllocator); `HvRequest` `Queued` with `AssignedReviewerId` and `AuthorReviewerId`; one `HvRequestTurn` per member, each with its TurnSnapshotBuilder snapshot hash, class, and hostile status at admission (S-09); the requirement references; one `HvRequestResponse` `Pending` per agent response of a member turn whose status is `Submitted`, `Grading`, `Trusted`, or `Stale` and that is not `Pending` in another open request (when Phase C has recorded responses); the `Request` evidence through GzipCodec (section 13.3); policy HvTurnFreeze `Freeze` on every member turn (`HvState` `Pending`, `HvRequestId`); the round-robin cursor advance; NotificationOutbox `hv_queued`.
696:   5. After the commit the worker is woken (S-24, auto-start).
697: - Response 201 `HvRequestResult` with Location `/qbrainai/hostile-validation/requests/{hvRequestId}`; a repeat with the same key and inputs is 200 with the stored request and its current state.
698: - Concurrency: two submissions over overlapping turns are serialized by SerializableWrite; the second sees the first's `Pending` items and is refused with `hv_turns_pending` (I-01; the unique filtered index ends a racing insert, and the retried attempt finds the winner). Two submissions over disjoint turns take consecutive cursor values, so round-robin order holds under concurrency.
699: - Errors, in order: 400 `hv_scope_invalid`, `validation_error` (submitter, key, context, `workspacePath`), `hv_scope_too_large`, `hv_scope_includes_submitting_turn`, `hv_scope_empty`; 409 `conflict` (`retryable: false` key reused, `retryable: true` exhausted), `hv_turns_not_terminal`, `hv_turns_pending`, `hv_turns_already_reviewed`, `hv_no_reviewer_available` (with `details.reviewers`); 500 `evidence_corrupt` (the accepted request failed its GZIP round trip; nothing saved); 503 `audit_unavailable`.
700: 
701: ```mermaid
702: flowchart TD
703:     S(["Handler runs: POST requests"]) --> SH{"Scope, submitter, key, and context well formed?"}
704:     SH -->|"scope"| E1(["400 hv_scope_invalid, details.field"])
705:     SH -->|"submitter, key, or context"| E2(["400 validation_error, details.field"])
706:     SH -->|yes| RX[["RequirementReferenceExtractor on the context"]]
707:     RX --> SW[["SerializableWrite with AuditLedgerGuard"]]
708:     SW -->|"audit unavailable"| E3(["503 audit_unavailable"])
709:     SW -->|"attempts exhausted"| E4(["409 conflict, retryable true"])
710:     SW -->|attempt| IC[["IdempotentCreate lookup, policy Conflict"]]
711:     IC -->|"stored, same inputs"| R2(["200 the stored request"])
712:     IC -->|"key reused, other inputs"| E5(["409 conflict, retryable false"])
713:     IC -->|absent| AC[["AdmitRequestChecks"]]
714:     AC -->|refused| E6(["Refusal of AdmitRequestChecks, drawn there"])
715:     AC -->|"members and reviewer"| INS[["InsertAdmittedRequest"]]
716:     INS -->|"key collision: attempt ends"| SW
717:     INS -->|committed| R(["201 HvRequestResult; the worker is woken after the commit"])
718: ```

721:

723: flowchart TD
724:     S(["AdmitRequestChecks"]) --> SK{"Submitter kind Agent?"}
725:     SK -->|yes| TL[["TurnLocator: the submitting turn"]]
726:     TL -->|"InvalidIdentifier, SessionNotFound, or TurnNotFound"| E1(["400 validation_error, details.field submitter"])
727:     TL -->|found| SC
728:     SK -->|"no: Operator"| SC[["Policy HvScopeResolution"]]
729:     SC -->|refused| E2(["400 hv_scope_invalid, hv_scope_too_large, hv_scope_includes_submitting_turn, or hv_scope_empty"])
730:     SC -->|members| EL[["Policy HvAdmissionEligibility"]]
731:     EL -->|refused| E3(["409 hv_turns_not_terminal, hv_turns_pending, or hv_turns_already_reviewed, listing every turn"])

945: Every unit here is internal (R-29): its caller is process HvWorkerHost (section 16.1) or another unit of this section, never a route, tool, or client. Each returns a typed result to its caller; the codes in its list are those results, and none reaches a public surface.

947: #### ClaimHvRunCommand: claim the next probe or review [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-003, -007]
948: 
949: - Handler: `ClaimHvRunCommand(string WorkspacePath, string WorkerId) : ICommand<HvRunClaim?>`; `HvRunClaim { runId, kind, reviewerId, attempt, fenceToken, leaseExpiresUtc, hvRequestId, expectedModel, expectedEffort, probeNonce }`.
950: - Delegate: AuditLedgerGuard; then, in this order: (1) a probe: the first enabled reviewer, in pool order, with `ProbeRequestedUtc` set and fewer active runs than its `MaxConcurrentRuns`: insert its `Probe` run (`hvprobe-` key, a fresh 32-byte random `ProbeNonce` in lower-case hex), FencedLease `Claim`, clear `ProbeRequestedUtc`; (2) otherwise a review: the oldest `Queued` request (by `CreatedUtc`, then `HvRequestId`) whose assignee is eligible with capacity, or whose assignee is no longer eligible and for which policy RoundRobinAssignment finds an eligible reviewer with capacity (the reassignment is recorded on the request); insert its `Review` run (`hvrun-<hvRequestId>-<nn>`, `Attempt` = `AttemptCount` + 1), FencedLease `Claim`, set the request `Running` (with `StartedUtc` on the first attempt) and `AttemptCount` + 1, and append `hv_started`. Every run records, at claim, `ClaimedUtc` and the reviewer's `ConfigurationVersion`, `ExpectedModel`, and `ExpectedEffort`. With nothing claimable it returns null and writes nothing; a request whose turns are all frozen stays `Queued` while no reviewer is eligible (ETA `Unknown`, R-18).
951: - Concurrency: the request's state, version, and the one-live-run index are checked and written in the delegate, so two workers never claim one request (W-11).

958:     SW -->|"attempts exhausted"| E2(["409 conflict, retryable true"])
959:     SW -->|attempt| P{"An enabled reviewer with a requested probe and free capacity?"}

968:     NX -->|no| R0(["null: nothing claimable"])
969:     RR -->|"reviewer, reassignment recorded"| RV["Insert the Review run, attempt AttemptCount plus 1"]
970:     Q -->|"no Queued request"| R0
971:     RV --> L2[["FencedLease Claim"]]

1043: #### CloseHvRunOutputCommand: close a run's output [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-003, -008, -011]
1044: 
1045: - Handler: `CloseHvRunOutputCommand(string WorkspacePath, string RunId, string WorkerId, long FenceToken, int ChunkCount, HvProvenance Provenance) : ICommand<HvCloseResult>`; the worker calls it only after the reviewer process exited with code 0 and every batch was appended; any other exit goes to FailHvRunCommand. Exit code 0 only routes the run here; whether it produced a review or a probe answer is decided by V-8 or policy ReadinessProbeVerdict (R-11).
1046: - Delegate: AuditLedgerGuard; FencedLease `Guard`; `ChunkCount` equal to `OutputChunkCount`, otherwise 409 `conflict` with `details.field` `chunkCount` (the worker appends what is missing and closes again); the run becomes `OutputClosed` with `EndedUtc`, `ExitCode` 0, `RuntimeModel`, and `RuntimeEffort`; FencedLease `Release`. A `Review` run whose request is `CancelRequested` (a cancel that committed after the last heartbeat): the run becomes `Canceled` with code `canceled` instead, and policy HvRetryDecision makes the request `Canceled`, so an accepted cancellation is never lost (R-28). Any other `Review` run: the request becomes `Finalizing` and `hv_finalizing` is appended; after the commit the worker dispatches FinalizeHvRequestCommand. A `Probe` run whose `ReviewerConfigurationVersion` is no longer the reviewer's `ConfigurationVersion` (the reviewer was reconfigured while it ran): the run becomes `Failed` with `probe_stale_configuration`, and the reviewer, its readiness, and its newer probe request are left unchanged, with no incident, because only a probe of the current configuration may change readiness. Any other `Probe` run: policy ReadinessProbeVerdict decides in the same transaction: a pass makes the run `Succeeded` and the reviewer `Online` with `ResolvedModel` and `ResolvedEffort` and appends `reviewer_online`; a failure makes the run `Failed` with the policy's code and inserts an `HvIncident` (`Pending`) attributed as FailHvRunCommand attributes it: a reviewer-attributable code (`probe_nonce_mismatch`, `runtime_identity_mismatch`, `reviewer_turn_logging_unsupported`) makes the reviewer `Offline` with `DedupeKey` `hv-reviewer-<reviewerId>-<code>` and appends `reviewer_offline`; `evidence_corrupt`, a server fault, gets `hv-server-evidence_corrupt` and leaves the reviewer's readiness unchanged, with no new probe until a caller requests one.
1047: - Results: closed (`Finalizing`, request canceled, probe passed, probe failed, or stale probe); `stale_fence`; 409 `conflict`; 503 `audit_unavailable`.
1048: 
1049: ```mermaid
1050: flowchart TD
1051:     S(["CloseHvRunOutputCommand: run, fence, chunk count, provenance"]) --> SW[["SerializableWrite with AuditLedgerGuard"]]
1052:     SW -->|"audit unavailable"| E1(["503 audit_unavailable"])
1053:     SW -->|"attempts exhausted"| E2(["409 conflict, retryable true"])
1054:     SW -->|attempt| G[["FencedLease Guard"]]
1055:     G -->|stale_fence| E3(["stale_fence: nothing changed"])
1056:     G -->|guarded| C{"ChunkCount equals OutputChunkCount?"}
1057:     C -->|no| E4(["409 conflict, details.field chunkCount"])
1058:     C -->|yes| OC["Run OutputClosed: EndedUtc, exit 0, runtime model and effort"]
1059:     OC --> RL[["FencedLease Release"]]
1060:     RL --> K{"Run kind?"}
1061:     K -->|Review| CRQ{"Request CancelRequested?"}
1062:     CRQ -->|yes| CNL["Run Canceled with code canceled"]
1063:     CNL --> RD[["Policy HvRetryDecision: request Canceled, turns released, hv_canceled"]]
1064:     RD --> R4(["closed: request Canceled"])
1065:     CRQ -->|no| FZ["Request Finalizing"]
1066:     FZ --> N1[["NotificationOutbox: hv_finalizing"]]
1067:     N1 --> R1(["closed: Finalizing; the worker dispatches FinalizeHvRequestCommand"])
1068:     K -->|Probe| CV{"Probe of the reviewer's current ConfigurationVersion?"}
1069:     CV -->|no| ST["Run Failed probe_stale_configuration; reviewer and its newer probe request unchanged"]
1070:     ST --> R5(["closed: stale probe, readiness unchanged"])
1071:     CV -->|yes| PV[["Policy ReadinessProbeVerdict"]]
1072:     PV -->|passed| ON["Run Succeeded; reviewer Online with resolved model and effort"]
1073:     ON --> N2[["NotificationOutbox: reviewer_online"]]
1074:     N2 --> R2(["closed: probe passed"])
1075:     PV -->|"failed: reviewer code"| OFF["Run Failed with the code; reviewer Offline; insert HvIncident Pending, key hv-reviewer-id-code"]
1076:     OFF --> N3[["NotificationOutbox: reviewer_offline"]]
1077:     N3 --> R3(["closed: probe failed"])
1078:     PV -->|"failed: evidence_corrupt"| SVF["Run Failed evidence_corrupt; insert HvIncident Pending, key hv-server-evidence_corrupt; readiness unchanged"]
1079:     SVF --> R6(["closed: probe failed, server fault"])
1080: ```

1082: #### FailHvRunCommand: record an execution failure [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-009]
1083: 
1084: - Handler: `FailHvRunCommand(string WorkspacePath, string RunId, string? WorkerId, long FenceToken, int? ExpectedRequestStateVersion, string FailureCode, string Detail) : ICommand<HvFailResult>`. Callers: the worker (`WorkerId` set, a `Claimed` or `Running` run, `ExpectedRequestStateVersion` null) and FinalizeHvRequestCommand (`WorkerId` null, an `OutputClosed` run with its released lease, whose stored fence the finalizer passes, with the request's `StateVersion` its reads saw).
1085: - Delegate: AuditLedgerGuard; FencedLease `Guard`; for the finalizer's call, the run must still be `OutputClosed` and its request still `Finalizing` at `ExpectedRequestStateVersion`, otherwise nothing changes and the result is the stored outcome (`already_completed` when another finalization committed, `not_finalizable` otherwise), so a late verification failure never undoes a committed finalization (I-03); the run becomes `Failed` (or `Canceled` for the code `canceled`) with the code and the detail (through SecretRedactor) and `EndedUtc`, and its lease is released; `canceled` and `worker_shutdown` insert no incident and change no reviewer; every other failure inserts an `HvIncident` (`Pending`) with `DedupeKey` `hv-reviewer-<reviewerId>-<failureCode>` when the failure is attributable to the reviewer (`reviewer_launch_failed`, `reviewer_exited_nonzero`, `reviewer_output_invalid`, `reviewer_turn_unverified`, `runtime_identity_mismatch`, `verdict_binding_failed`, and the probe codes `probe_nonce_mismatch` and `reviewer_turn_logging_unsupported`, which CloseHvRunOutputCommand records), and `hv-server-<failureCode>` otherwise (`evidence_corrupt`, `snapshot_changed`, `reviewer_not_independent`); this one attribution list holds for every incident of a run, review or probe; a reviewer-attributable failure also makes the reviewer `Offline` with `ReadinessReason` the code and `OpenIncidentId`, and appends `reviewer_offline` (S-15). Then, by run kind: a `Review` run's request goes through policy HvRetryDecision, which decides and writes its next state: `Queued` again (its assignee re-evaluated at the next claim), `Failed` with `attempts_exhausted`, or, for a `CancelRequested` request, `Canceled`, each ended request with its turns released, its `Pending` responses closed, and its notification (section 15); a `Probe` run has no request, so HvRetryDecision does not apply: `worker_shutdown` sets the reviewer's `ProbeRequestedUtc` again so the probe runs after the restart, and every other probe failure leaves the reviewer as the steps above set it (`Offline` with its incident for a reviewer-attributable code), with no new probe until a caller requests one (S-15). After the commit the worker is woken to file the incident (FileHvIncidentCommand) and claim again.
1086: - Results: failed with the request's next state, or the probe outcome; `already_completed` or `not_finalizable` (finalizer's call, nothing changed); `stale_fence`; 409 `conflict`; 503 `audit_unavailable`.

1088: ```mermaid
1089: flowchart TD
1090:     S(["FailHvRunCommand: run, fence, failure code, detail"]) --> SW[["SerializableWrite with AuditLedgerGuard"]]
1091:     SW -->|"audit unavailable"| E1(["503 audit_unavailable"])
1092:     SW -->|"attempts exhausted"| E2(["409 conflict, retryable true"])
1093:     SW -->|attempt| G[["FencedLease Guard"]]
1094:     G -->|stale_fence| E3(["stale_fence: nothing changed"])
1095:     G -->|guarded| FC{"Finalizer's call?"}
1096:     FC -->|yes| ST{"Run OutputClosed and request Finalizing at the version read?"}
1097:     ST -->|no| R0(["already_completed or not_finalizable: nothing changed"])
1098:     ST -->|yes| F
1099:     FC -->|"no: the worker"| F["Run Failed, or Canceled for canceled: code, redacted detail, EndedUtc; lease released"]
1100:     F --> NI{"Code canceled or worker_shutdown?"}
1101:     NI -->|yes| KD
1102:     NI -->|no| AT{"Failure attributable to the reviewer?"}
1103:     AT -->|yes| OFF["Insert HvIncident Pending, key hv-reviewer-id-code; reviewer Offline with the code and incident"]
1104:     OFF --> N1[["NotificationOutbox: reviewer_offline"]]
1105:     N1 --> KD
1106:     AT -->|no| SI["Insert HvIncident Pending, key hv-server-code"]

1108:     KD -->|Probe| PS{"Code worker_shutdown?"}

1110:     PQ --> R4(["failed: probe requested again"])
1111:     PS -->|no| R5(["failed: probe, reviewer as recorded above"])
1112:     KD -->|Review| RD[["Policy HvRetryDecision: decides and writes the request's next state"]]

1143: #### FinalizeHvRequestCommand: verify and commit the result atomically [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-010, -011, -012, -013, -014, -021]
1144: 
1145: - Handler: `FinalizeHvRequestCommand(string WorkspacePath, string HvRequestId) : ICommand<HvFinalizeResult>` (S-03, S-06, S-07, S-10, S-13, S-21, S-23, R-15). Callers: the worker after CloseHvRunOutputCommand, and the worker's sweep for every `Finalizing` request (W-05, W-06).
1146: - Reads, with no transaction open (foundation section 3.1, "Database-only delegates"): the request (`Completed` returns the stored outcome and writes nothing, I-03; any status other than `Finalizing` returns `not_finalizable` and writes nothing); its `OutputClosed` run; every chunk decompressed and checked by policy HvFinalVerification V-1, then the reviewer's records, extracted from the stored log by the reviewer's adapter (`ExtractReviewerRecords`, the same function the worker ran, section 16.3), checked by V-2 to V-8 (section 15); when the request links responses and `Mcp:AgentContext:Mode` is not `Off`, EvaluateStalenessCommand is dispatched for them, as the foundation's grade units do before their write (foundation section 3.1).

1257: ### Policy HvScopeResolution: resolve the member turns [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-004]
1258: 
1259: Applied by SubmitHvRequestCommand inside its delegate, reading only the database. TurnLocator finds the reviewed session by `agent` and `sessionId` (`SessionNotFound` is `hv_scope_invalid`); `Turn`: the one turn by `requestId`; `Range`: both endpoint turns, then every turn between them inclusive in the session's turn order (the order develop reads a session's turns in: ascending turn row `Id`, VI-06), refused when an endpoint is missing or the start is after the end; `Session`: every turn of the session at this moment (S-11). The submitting turn is removed from a `Session` scope (`ExcludedSubmittingTurn` true) and refuses a `Turn` or `Range` scope that contains it. More than `MaxTurnsPerRequest` members is `hv_scope_too_large` with the count; no member left is `hv_scope_empty`.

1266:     K -->|Turn| T1[["TurnLocator: the turn"]]

1268:     T1 -->|found| M1["Members: that turn"]

1348: ### Policy HvFinalVerification: the eight verification steps [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-010, -011, -021]
1349: 
1350: Applied by FinalizeHvRequestCommand to the run's stored chunks before any transaction; each failed step returns its code, and the steps run in the diagram's order (V-1, V-8, V-2, V-3, V-4, V-5, V-6, V-7), so the log's integrity and completeness are known before any record is bound. They replace the foundation's eight receipt checks (A-05): `receipt_path` becomes V-1 (the evidence is held by the server, not found on disk), `request_meta` becomes V-3 and V-7 (the expected reviewer is recorded on the run), `verdict_block` becomes V-8, `verdict_binding` becomes V-2 and V-3, `verdict_match` becomes V-4, `reviewer_turn` becomes V-6, `reviewer_independent` becomes V-5 (amended, A-09), and `runtime_identity` becomes V-7.
1351: 
1352: - V-1 Evidence integrity (`evidence_corrupt`): the chunks run 1 to `OutputChunkCount` without a gap; each decompresses (GzipCodec), its SHA-256 equals the stored one, the chain hash equals `OutputChainSha256`, and every line parses as one JSON object (I-06).
1353: - V-2 Snapshot binding: each `hv_turn_assessment` names a member's ordinal, turn key, and admission snapshot hash (`verdict_binding_failed` otherwise), and TurnSnapshotBuilder over each turn now yields that hash (`snapshot_changed` otherwise; HvTurnFreeze makes it unreachable, and the step proves it, I-02).
1354: - V-3 Verdict binding (`verdict_binding_failed`): the `hv_verdict` record names this `hvRequestId` and run, its counts equal the members and the responses of the accepted request (the set admitted, whatever has happened to those responses since), its reviewer equals the run's reviewer, and each `hv_response_grade` names a response of the accepted request with the `ContentSha256` the accepted request recorded.
1355: - V-4 Verdict consistency (`reviewer_output_invalid`): every score is a valid lexeme (ScoreLexeme); each turn's verdict is `AGREE` exactly when ScoreVerdict derives `Pass` at the hostile thresholds and its findings hold no FAIL or UNKNOWN; the holistic verdict likewise at `max(threshold, 0.98)` (R-31); each response grade follows the foundation's `verdict_match` rule; and the overall verdict is the one predicate of R-31 over the holistic verdict, every turn's verdict, the response grades, and the findings of every scope.
1356: - V-5 Reviewer independence (`reviewer_not_independent`): the run's reviewer id differs from the request's submitter id and from its author id (S-17, S-28, P-01, P-07).
1357: - V-6 Reviewer turn (`reviewer_turn_unverified`): the `hv_reviewer_turn` record names a turn TurnLocator finds, whose agent AgentIdentity maps to the run's reviewer, whose session is neither the reviewed session nor the submitter's, created at or after the run's `ClaimedUtc`, persisted (not a failsafe or queued record), closed `completed` with class `Chore`, and whose stored result (its response, then its dialog parts in order with each part's header line removed, as foundation check 6 reads it) contains every reviewer record of the run in the order the extraction returned them (each `hv_turn_assessment`, the `hv_holistic`, each `hv_response_grade`, and the `hv_verdict`), each byte for byte in its stored normal form; a summary-only, open, or failed turn fails (P-06, R-24).
1358: - V-7 Runtime identity (`runtime_identity_mismatch`): the log holds at least one top-level `hv_provenance` line written by the worker from the CLI's runtime receipt of this run, and every one names the run's expected model (or, when the reviewer has no configured model, the model the last NONCE resolved) and expected effort (P-04).
1359: - V-8 Completeness (`reviewer_output_invalid`): exactly one `hv_verdict`, the last reviewer record; exactly one `hv_holistic`; exactly one `hv_turn_assessment` per member and one `hv_response_grade` per response of the accepted request; every FAIL and UNKNOWN finding of every scope (turn, holistic, and response) has a category, a location, evidence, and a remediation (S-13); the failures list equals every FAIL and UNKNOWN finding of every scope.

1362: flowchart TD
1363:     S(["HvFinalVerification: run chunks, request, members, responses"]) --> L[["VerifyLogAndBinding: V-1, V-8, V-2, V-3"]]
1364:     L -->|"failed: code"| E1(["the step's code, drawn there"])
1365:     L -->|"bound records"| R[["VerifyVerdictAndReviewer: V-4, V-5, V-6, V-7"]]
1366:     R -->|"failed: code"| E2(["the step's code, drawn there"])
1367:     R -->|passed| OK(["verified records"])
1368: ```

1418: ### Policy HvRetryDecision: requeue, fail, or cancel [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-007, -009]
1419: 
1420: Applied inside the caller's transaction by FailHvRunCommand and ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand for a review run's request, and by CloseHvRunOutputCommand for a review run whose request is `CancelRequested` at close; it decides the request's next state and writes it, so a request ends the same way whether its attempt failed, its worker died, or its cancel was found at close. A `CancelRequested` request becomes `Canceled`; otherwise, with the counted attempts (the request's runs except those that ended `worker_shutdown`, which a graceful restart causes and no reviewer does) below `MaxAttemptsPerRequest` the request returns to `Queued` (its assignee re-evaluated at the next claim, R-07); otherwise it becomes `Failed` with `attempts_exhausted`. A canceled or failed request gets `CompletedUtc`, releases its turns (HvTurnFreeze `Release`), closes its `Pending` responses with `request_ended`, and appends `hv_canceled` or `hv_failed` (NotificationOutbox).

1444: ### 16.1 Process HvWorkerHost: the durable worker [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-007, -008, -009]

1446: A hosted `BackgroundService` per workspace application (`src/QBrainAi.Services/HostileValidation/Execution/HvWorkerHost.cs`), with a worker id of the host name, process id, and a random suffix. It is the only dispatcher of the internal units (R-29). At start, while `WorkerEnabled`, it requests a NONCE for every enabled `Unverified` reviewer (StartHvReviewerNonceCommand, R-10). Then it loops, woken by an `IChangeEventBus` wake-up or at `PollInterval`: a sweep (ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand, FinalizeHvRequestCommand for every `Finalizing` request it lists, FileHvIncidentCommand for every `Pending` incident), then claims until ClaimHvRunCommand returns null, starting one process RunReviewerProcess per claim. On a graceful shutdown it stops claiming and ends each of its running runs with FailHvRunCommand code `worker_shutdown`, which files no incident, marks no reviewer offline, and does not count as an attempt (policy HvRetryDecision); after a crash the leases expire instead (W-03). A 503 `audit_unavailable` from any unit stops the loop iteration and the next iteration starts from the sweep (W-12).
