1467: ### 16.2 Process RunReviewerProcess: one attempt, live [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008, -016]
1468: 
1469: Runs one claimed run. It builds the brief (section 13.3: the accepted request read from the `Request` evidence inside the run envelope, or the probe brief with its nonce), asks the reviewer's adapter for the launch (section 16.3), starts the process with the workspace as its working directory and its plugin as a host session of its own (R-24), inside a containment bound to the worker process, so the reviewer and every descendant end when the worker dies, however abruptly (W-03; the containment, for example a process group or job object, is the adapter's, section 16.3), records the start (RecordHvRunStartCommand), and appends the `hv_brief` record as sequence 1. While the process runs it has four concurrent duties and no time limit (R-11, P-02): every line the adapter delivers goes into a buffer that is appended (AppendHvRunOutputCommand) when `OutputFlushBytes` accumulate; a flush timer appends a buffer that is not empty once `OutputFlushInterval` has passed since its first line, whether or not another line arrives, so a single line followed by silence is still appended within the interval (R-12); a heartbeat every `HeartbeatInterval` (RecordHvRunHeartbeatCommand) renews the lease and reads cancellation; and the process exit is awaited. `stale_fence` from any unit kills the process and ends the attempt without another write (W-03); `audit_unavailable` kills the process and ends the attempt (W-12); `evidence_corrupt` from an append (its round trip failed and nothing was saved) kills the process and fails the run with `evidence_corrupt` (FailHvRunCommand: a server fault, so a server incident and the reviewer unchanged, and the request through policy HvRetryDecision); a retryable `conflict` repeats the same unit call with the same sequence. Every append carries the records the adapter's extraction completed with that batch. On exit the remaining buffer is appended, the adapter's provenance lines are appended (section 16.3), and the run is closed (exit code 0, CloseHvRunOutputCommand, then FinalizeHvRequestCommand for a review whose request is `Finalizing`; a close that finds the request `CancelRequested` ends it `Canceled` instead, R-28; exit code 0 is not evidence of a review, R-11) or failed (FailHvRunCommand with `reviewer_exited_nonzero`, or `reviewer_launch_failed` when the process never started). A cancellation read at a heartbeat kills the process and fails the run with `canceled`, which policy HvRetryDecision turns into the request's `Canceled` (R-28). Killing the process, here and in the diagrams, ends the reviewer's whole process tree, descendants included, also when the root process has already exited; and when the root exits while a descendant still holds its output pipes, the worker ends that descendant before it reads the output to its end. Without that, a descendant that outlives the reviewer would hold the run open forever, because no time limit ends a run (P-02); P14 is the same defect class in the plugin core (FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008-AC011).

1524: ### 16.3 Reviewer adapter contract [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-001, -003, -008]
1525: 
1526: `IHvReviewerAdapter` (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.HostileValidation.Reviewers`), one implementation per reviewer id:
1527: 
1528: - `BuildLaunch(brief, reviewer)`: a `ProcessStartInfo` built as an argument list, never a shell string, with the brief on standard input or in a temporary file the adapter deletes after the run; the launch arguments come from one shared launch builder that develop's one-shot strategy also uses, so the per-CLI arguments of `OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy` (`AddCodexArguments`, `AddClaudeArguments`, `AddGrokArguments`, `AddClineArguments`, `OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy.cs:238-262`) are written once (DRY); processes start through the existing `IProcessSpawner` and `IProcessEnvironmentService` (`OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy.cs:18-21`), inside a containment the adapter creates at launch and binds to the worker process (for example a process group with a parent-death signal on Linux or a kill-on-close job object on Windows, settled in H1's contract step), so the reviewer and every descendant end when the worker dies, and so killing the run ends the whole tree even after the root has exited (W-03, FR-MCP-HVPIPE-007-AC008, FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008-AC011); develop's `DefaultProcessSpawner` starts an ordinary process and offers only an explicit kill (`src/QBrainAi.Common.AgentCli/DefaultProcessSpawner.cs:12-16,48-51`), so H1 adds the containment. The shared launch builder holds the one table of highest efforts of section 10 (P9). The reviewer runs behind a write barrier verified for its CLI (VI-03, probes of 2026-10-16): Codex `exec -s read-only` (a write attempt was refused by its sandbox), Grok `--permission-mode plan` (a write call was refused; a headless Grok run then ends `cancelled` at the first call that needs approval, so its launch allows the read tools a review uses), and Copilot `--available-tools` naming only read tools (write and shell tools are not offered at all). Claude's and Cline's plan modes are not accepted as barriers on that evidence (Claude's model declined before its barrier was exercised; Cline ran a shell command in plan mode), so Claude's launch restricts its tools structurally (`--tools`) and Cline stays unqualified until H1 proves a barrier. Whether each reviewer's plugin can still log its turn behind its barrier (the plugin writes host-session state and calls the server) is verified in H1 (VI-03, VI-04); a reviewer that cannot fails its NONCE (R-24).
1529: - Live lines (R-12, P8): standard output and standard error are read line by line as the process writes them (asynchronous line reads on the redirected streams), and each line is handed to the run's callback at once; nothing waits for the process to end.
1530: - `NormalizeLine(line, stream)`: a native JSON event line of a CLI run in a JSON streaming mode is kept as written; any other line becomes `{ "type": "hv_raw", "stream", "line" }`.
1531: - `ExtractReviewerRecords(lines)`: one pure function over a run's ordered native lines. It assembles each agent message's complete text by the CLI's event model (Grok's per-token `text` events, Copilot's `assistant.message_delta` events followed by the whole `assistant.message`, Claude's whole assistant messages, Codex's `agent_message` items, Cline's accumulated content) and returns, in message order, every line of that text that is exactly one JSON object of a reviewer record type of section 13.3; the fence lines of a fenced block are ignored, and a line holding other text beside a record is free text. The worker runs it as lines arrive and passes each batch's completed records to AppendHvRunOutputCommand; finalization runs it over the stored log; both get the same records (R-12). Record types the worker writes itself (`hv_brief`, `hv_provenance`, `hv_raw`) are never accepted from message text, so a reviewer cannot forge them.
1532: - `ReadProvenance(run)`: `hv_provenance` lines read from the CLI's own runtime receipt after the run (P-04), sources verified on 2026-10-16 (VI-01): for Codex, the thread's rollout `turn_context` (fields `model` and `effort`; observed `model` `gpt-6-astra`, `effort` `max`), the source the foundation's `runtime_identity` check reads (foundation section 6.3, check 8); for Claude, the session transcript under `~/.claude/projects` (the assistant message `model` and the request `effort`), written only when session persistence is on, so the launch never passes `--no-session-persistence`; for Grok, the session store `~/.grok/sessions/<cwd>/<sessionId>/` (`summary.json` `reasoning_effort`, and a model id that `chat_history.jsonl` names `grok-4.7-build` while the events name `grok-4.7`, so H1 pins the field V-7 compares); for Copilot, the run's own JSON stream (each call's `assistant.message.model` and `user.message.responsesReasoning.effort`; `--usage-output-file` holds the model only); for Cline, none, because its run records hold the model and only whether thinking was on, so V-7 and the NONCE fail closed (L-04, D-06).
1533: - Highest effort when none is configured: the verified values of section 10 (VI-08), never develop's one-shot constants (P9).

1535: ### 16.4 Process SubmitHvFromPlugin: the plugin verb [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-005, -020]
1536: 
1537: `workflow.hv.submit` in the PowerShell core (`plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1`): process BindVerbToTurn (foundation section 4.4) binds the invocation to its turn; the verb sends SubmitHvRequestCommand through the REPL with `submitter` that turn's key and `idempotencyKey` `hv-` followed by the first 32 lower-case hex characters of the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the whole invocation identity `{ submitter: { agent, sessionId, requestId }, scope, context, contextFormat }`, so the key has 35 characters whatever the length of the ids (within the 128 of section 12), two sessions with equal request ids get different keys, and a repeat of the same call is the same request. A created or stored request is reported with its id, status, and reviewer; the watcher needs no record of it, because a terminal notification carries the submitter's turn key (R-30, section 16.5). `hv_no_reviewer_available` is reported with the context S-16 asks for: each reviewer's enabled flag, readiness, and reason from `details.reviewers`, the open incident of each `Offline` reviewer (through `workflow.hv.incidents`), and the remedy text "after the cause is fixed, NONCE the reviewer: workflow.hv.nonce <reviewerId>". Every other refusal is reported with its code, final. A retryable answer (transport outage, 503, 409 with `retryable: true`) is reported with `retryable: true` and exit 1 and is not queued in the failsafe, because the same call with the same key can simply be repeated (the reviews' no-failsafe rule, foundation section 5.2).

1552: ### 16.5 Process WatchHvNotifications: completions into the plugin [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-017, -020]
1553: 
1554: Started by process StartHostSession (foundation section 4.4) for each host session and stopped by EndHostSession; one instance per host session (`sessions/<hostSessionKey>/hv-watcher.pid`, the arrival bridge's pattern). It runs the REPL streaming verb `workflow.hv.watchNotifications` with `Last-Event-ID` the `lastSequence` of `sessions/<hostSessionKey>/hv-notifications.yaml`. That one state file holds both `lastSequence` and the `inbox`, and every change to it is one atomic replace (temp file, flush, rename) under `hv-notifications.lock`. For each event the watcher writes, in that one replace, the new `lastSequence` and, when the event is `hv_completed`, `hv_failed`, or `hv_canceled` and its submitter session is this host session's MCP session (the submitter turn key the notification carries, section 12), an inbox entry keyed by the event's sequence; so a crash leaves either both or neither, and an event replayed after a crash is not added twice. Matching by the carried key needs no record of the submission, so a completion that arrives before the submit verb has returned is still inboxed. A disconnect reconnects with backoff from the recorded sequence, so nothing is missed (R-16). The prompt hook adds each undelivered inbox entry to the next prompt's context ("HV <hvRequestId> <status>, overall verdict <verdict>, sequence <n>; result: workflow.hv.result <hvRequestId>") and then marks it delivered in the same state file; a crash between the two repeats the entry at a later prompt, so delivery to the model is at least once, and the sequence makes a repeat recognizable (R-30). Plugins never call REST; the REPL holds the stream (R-30).

1576: ### 16.7 Process HostileReviewWorkerHost: the artifact worker of FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-003 (P1 to P3, D-02)
1577: 
1578: The HostileReview subsystem keeps its own bounded context, queue, entities, and surfaces (R-25); this section is the contract of its missing worker, fixed in H3. The requirements are the stored FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-002 and -003 with their texts unchanged; H0 writes the named tests below for their criteria, against mocks first, and H3 binds them to production.
1579: 
1580: - Host: a hosted `BackgroundService` of its own per workspace application (`src/QBrainAi.Services/HostileReview/Execution/HostileReviewWorkerHost.cs`), not HvWorkerHost, looping on a wake-up or `PollInterval`: ExpireHostileReviewLeasesCommand, then ClaimHostileReviewAttemptCommand until it returns null, running one attempt per claim. It shares with this pipeline only the reviewer adapters' launch builder, live-line path, and containment (section 16.3) and FencedLease (section 11.1).
1581: - Agent: the agent, model, and effort configured for hostile review when they are configured, and otherwise the pooled default agent with its default model and effort (FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-003 criterion 4, store text; P5 removes the single-reviewer pin of `HostileReviewWorkerOptions`). HV's reviewer pool, round-robin, and NONCE do not apply.
1582: - Identities, distinct as criterion 4 requires: the request (the existing request id); one attempt per claim (`AttemptId`, with lease, fence, and attempt number); the AgentPool job that runs it (`PoolJobId`); one model execution per launched process (`ExecutionId`, the existing execution row with model, effort, agent, prompt template and version, run id, and times, criteria 1 to 3); and the one accepted terminal result (`AcceptedResultId` on the request, set once).
1583: - Storage boundary (FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-002 criterion 4): the worker assembles the prompt in memory from links it reauthorizes at dispatch, reads the reviewer's output lines only to parse the result, and stores neither the prompt nor any output line nor any artifact content: only normalized identity, type, version or content hash, the parsed result, and sanitized diagnostics reach queue rows, notifications, logs, receipts, or result metadata.
1584: - Links (P3): every artifact type FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-002 lists resolves through its supported workspace-scoped service, the stored hash is of the resolved content (never of its id), and the limits of criterion 4 refuse more than 64 links, an artifact over 1 MiB decoded, aggregate input over 8 MiB, or uninspectable content.
1585: - Execution: bounded at-least-once across process loss (an expired lease abandons the attempt and a new one runs, up to the configured attempt bound); the reviewer runs contained with its worker (W-03); cancellation is internal to the host and workspace lifecycle and the existing authorized AgentPool cancellation, never a public mutation.
1586: - Audit (P4): every unit below calls AuditLedgerGuard first, and the HostileReview entities gain `IsDeleted` in H3, so each of their writes reaches the ledger and an unwritable ledger stops the unit.

2295: ### 18.2 UC-HV-01 Manage the reviewer pool [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-001]
2296: 
2297: Actors: Operator (through Director or the REPL), server. Trigger: the operator lists, inspects, enables, disables, or retunes a reviewer. Preconditions: the server started with the five reviewers configured and seeded (section 10). Main flow: the operator lists the pool (ListHvReviewersQuery), reads one reviewer (GetHvReviewerQuery), and changes its enabled flag, strategy, agent path, model, effort, or concurrency with the state version it read (UpdateHvReviewerCommand); a change to the strategy, agent path, model, or effort makes the reviewer `Unverified`, and the worker NONCEs it (UC-HV-02). Alternates: a stale state version is refused with 409 `conflict` and the operator reads again; an unknown reviewer is 404; an invalid field is 400; the audit ledger is unavailable and nothing changes (503). Postconditions: the change is stored, audited, and announced (`reviewer_unverified` when the launch changed); a disabled reviewer gets no new assignment, and the requests it held are reassigned at their next claim. Invariants: I-10; no change applies without its ledger rows.

2304:     E1(("Launch changed: Unverified, then NONCE")) -. extend .-> U

2309: ### 18.3 UC-HV-02 NONCE a reviewer [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-003]
2310: 
2311: Actors: operator or any agent, HV worker, reviewer agent. Trigger: a reviewer is `Unverified` (startup or a launch change, requested by the worker) or `Offline` after its cause was fixed (requested by a caller, S-15). Preconditions: the reviewer is enabled. Main flow: the caller requests a NONCE (StartHvReviewerNonceCommand); the worker claims the probe (ClaimHvRunCommand), launches the reviewer with a probe brief carrying a fresh nonce (RunReviewerProcess), streams its output (AppendHvRunOutputCommand), appends the adapter's provenance, and closes the run (CloseHvRunOutputCommand); policy ReadinessProbeVerdict passes: the nonce is echoed, the provenance shows the expected model and effort, and the reviewer logged its own turn; the reviewer becomes `Online` with its resolved model and effort. Alternates: a probe already requested or running is reported without a second probe; a disabled reviewer is refused with 409 `hv_reviewer_disabled`; the probe fails (wrong nonce, wrong or missing provenance, no reviewer turn, launch failure, nonzero exit) and the reviewer stays or becomes `Offline` with an incident filed through triage (UC-HV-09); the probe's stored log fails its integrity check, a server fault, and a server incident is filed while the reviewer's readiness is unchanged; the reviewer is reconfigured while the probe runs, and the old probe fails `probe_stale_configuration` without changing readiness while the newer probe request waits; the worker dies during the probe and the sweep requests it again. Postconditions: the reviewer's readiness reflects a probe of this moment (S-27); `reviewer_online` or `reviewer_offline` is announced. Invariants: only a passing NONCE moves a reviewer to `Online` (R-10).

2319:     U -. include .-> I2(("Decide (ReadinessProbeVerdict)"))

2328: ### 18.4 UC-HV-03 Submit an HV request [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-002, -004, -005, -006, -013, -018]
2329: 
2330: Actors: model (through its plugin) or operator (through Director), any client, server. Trigger: a caller wants a turn, an inclusive range of turns, or a whole session reviewed (S-03, S-11). Preconditions: the turns to review are terminal; for an agent caller, its own turn is bound by the plugin (BindVerbToTurn). Main flow: the caller submits the scope, optional context in Markdown or YAML, and an idempotency key (SubmitHvRequestCommand); the server resolves the requirement references of the context (RequirementReferenceExtractor), resolves the members (HvScopeResolution: the session's turns at admission time for a session scope, without the submitting turn), checks that every member is terminal, not under review, and never reviewed (HvAdmissionEligibility), picks the next eligible reviewer round-robin, never the submitter, the author of the reviewed session, or an alias of either (RoundRobinAssignment, HvReviewerEligibility), snapshots every member without its review records (TurnSnapshotBuilder), stores the complete accepted request compressed (GzipCodec), freezes the members (HvTurnFreeze), announces `hv_queued`, and wakes the worker (auto-start, S-24). Alternates: the same key and inputs return the stored request; the key with other inputs is a conflict; a malformed scope, a scope over the limit, a scope naming the submitting turn, or an empty session scope is refused (400); turns that are not terminal, under review, or already reviewed are refused with every affected turn listed (409); no reviewer is eligible and the request is refused with every reviewer's status, and the plugin adds the reviewers' open incidents and the NONCE remedy (409, S-16); a turn whose class is `Chore` and whose hostile review is `Unnecessary` is admitted and graded like any other (S-09); a turn has no self-review, or any self-review grade or status, and admission is the same (S-28); the audit ledger is unavailable and nothing is written (503, S-29). Postconditions: one `Queued` request with its members frozen `Pending`, its accepted request stored, and its reviewer assigned. Invariants: I-01, I-07, I-08, I-10.

2337:     U -. include .-> I2(("Check eligibility (HvAdmissionEligibility)"))
2338:     U -. include .-> I3(("Assign round-robin, submitter and author excluded (RoundRobinAssignment)"))
2339:     U -. include .-> I4(("Store the accepted request and freeze the turns"))
2340:     E1(("Same key and inputs: stored request")) -. extend .-> U
2341:     E2(("Bad, oversized, self-including, or empty scope: 400")) -. extend .-> U
2342:     E3(("Not terminal, pending, or reviewed: 409 listing every turn")) -. extend .-> U
2343:     E4(("No eligible reviewer: 409 with reviewer context")) -. extend .-> U

2349: ### 18.5 UC-HV-04 Run a review live [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-007, -008]
2350: 
2351: Actors: HV worker, reviewer agent, server. Trigger: a `Queued` request whose reviewer is eligible and has capacity. Preconditions: UC-HV-03 completed. Main flow: the worker claims the request with a lease and a fence (ClaimHvRunCommand); it launches the reviewer with the brief (RunReviewerProcess) and records the brief as the log's first record; every line the reviewer writes is appended within the flush interval (AppendHvRunOutputCommand) and is visible on the output stream while the reviewer runs (S-22); progress records set the request's progress and ETA (R-18); heartbeats renew the lease (RecordHvRunHeartbeatCommand); the reviewer reviews each turn and the whole set, logs its own `Chore` turn holding its result, and emits its verdict record last; on exit with code 0 the worker appends the provenance and closes the output (CloseHvRunOutputCommand), and the request becomes `Finalizing`. Alternates: the assignee is no longer eligible and the claim reassigns round-robin; a cancel arrives and the worker stops the reviewer (UC-HV-08); the reviewer fails to start or exits nonzero (UC-HV-09); the worker loses its lease and its writes are refused as stale, so it stops (UC-HV-09); no reviewer is eligible and the request waits `Queued` with an unknown ETA; the reviewer runs for any length of time without a timeout (P-02). Postconditions: the attempt's complete log is stored, compressed, contiguous, and hashed. Invariants: I-05, I-06.

2358:     U -. include .-> I2(("Stream every line as it is written (AppendHvRunOutputCommand)"))
2359:     U -. include .-> I3(("Heartbeat (RecordHvRunHeartbeatCommand)"))
2360:     U -. include .-> I4(("Close the output (CloseHvRunOutputCommand)"))
2361:     E1(("Assignee ineligible: reassigned at claim")) -. extend .-> U
2362:     E2(("Cancel: reviewer stopped")) -. extend .-> U
2363:     E3(("Launch failure or nonzero exit: UC-HV-09")) -. extend .-> U

2368: ### 18.6 UC-HV-05 Finalize the HV result [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-010, -011, -012, -014, -021]
2369: 
2370: Actors: HV worker, server. Trigger: a request is `Finalizing` (after UC-HV-04, or found by the sweep after a crash). Main flow: the server reads the attempt's log and verifies it (HvFinalVerification: integrity, completeness, binding to the request and to each turn's admission snapshot, verdict consistency at 98/98, reviewer independence, the reviewer's own turn, and runtime identity); then, in one transaction (S-23), it stores the per-turn assessments, the holistic evaluation, and the delineated failures with their remediation, writes each turn's hostile review through HvVerdictMapping, makes every member turn final, grades the linked agent responses and decides their trust when agent context is on, stores the result document compressed, completes the request, and announces `hv_completed`. Alternates: a verification step fails, the attempt fails with that code (UC-HV-09), and the request is queued again or fails when its attempts are spent; the store changed since the reads and the transaction runs again from the reads; the audit ledger is unavailable or the transaction keeps conflicting and the request stays `Finalizing` for the sweep; the request was already finalized and the stored outcome returns; agent context is `Off` and the linked responses are recorded `NotGraded`. Postconditions: either every part of the result is committed or none is (I-04); the TODOs the turns name are unchanged (S-25); the self-review records were never read (S-28). Invariants: I-02, I-03, I-04, I-09.

2377:     U -. include .-> I3(("Hostile review per turn (HvVerdictMapping)"))

2430: ### 18.10 UC-HV-09 Recover from failures [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-007, -009]
2431: 
2432: Actors: HV worker, triage, server. Trigger: an execution failure (launch failure, nonzero exit, invalid output, failed verification, missing reviewer turn, runtime identity mismatch) or a dead worker. Main flow: the failure is recorded on the attempt (FailHvRunCommand); a failure attributable to the reviewer marks it `Offline` until a NONCE passes (S-15); an incident is recorded and filed through the triage endpoint with a deduplication key (FileHvIncidentCommand, S-26); the request returns to `Queued` and the next claim assigns the next eligible reviewer. Alternates: attempts are spent and the request fails, releasing its turns; triage is unreachable and the filing is retried at each sweep; a worker died and its expired leases are swept (ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand), its runs abandoned and fenced out; a graceful shutdown ends runs with `worker_shutdown`, which is not counted as an attempt; the audit ledger is unavailable and the failed run cannot be recorded until it returns, after which the lease expiry recovers it. Postconditions: no failure is silent, no incident group is duplicated, and no reviewer is used again before it proves itself. Invariants: I-05.

1: # Agent Instructions
2: 
3: ## Session Start
4: 
5: 1. Read `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` in the repo root for the current API key and endpoints.
6: 2. For specific operational steps (session bootstrap, session log turn workflow, and helper command sequence), follow `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`.
7: 
8: On every subsequent user message:
9: 
10: 1. Follow `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` for specific operational instructions.
11: 2. Complete the user's request.
12: 
13: ## Rules
14: 
15: 1. `templates/prompt-templates.yaml` (`default-marker-prompt`) is the source of truth for specific agent instructions. `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` is the rendered runtime instruction set.
16: 2. Keep this file focused on durable workspace policy and conventions; avoid duplicating marker-file operational procedures.
17: 3. Use helper modules for session log and TODO operations. Do not make raw API calls.
18: 4. Persist session log updates immediately after each meaningful change (turn creation, action append, decision, requirement, blocker, file/context update). Do not defer saves.
19: 5. Capture rich turn detail: interpretation, response, status, actions (type/status/filePath), contextList, filesModified, designDecisions, requirementsDiscovered, blockers, and relevant processing dialog.
20: 6. Follow workspace conventions in `.github/copilot-instructions.md` for build, test, and architecture guidance.
21: 7. Use **only `pwsh.exe`** for shell commands and script execution; do not use `powershell.exe`.
22: 8. When you need API schemas, module examples, or compliance rules, load them from `docs/context/` or use `context_search`.
23: 9. Do not fabricate information. If you made a mistake, acknowledge it. Distinguish facts from speculation.
24: 10. Prioritize correctness over speed. Do not ship code you have not verified compiles and is logically sound.
25: 11. When writing session logs or other audit records, agents must identify themselves accurately using their real agent identity in Pascal-Case. Do not use placeholder, legacy, or misleading sourceType values.
26: 12. Never edit YAML by appending, replacing, or removing text lines. Deserialize the complete document into an object, mutate the object, serialize it, and save it. Use `plugins/core/lib-ps/yaml-object-mutation.ps1` for PowerShell work.
27: 
28: ## Byrd Test Gate
29: 
30: The canonical process is `docs/Development-Process-draft-v4.md`. To leave a Byrd implementation slice, the entire unit test suite for the current iteration and previous iterations must be completely passing. In this workspace, skipped tests are not passing tests: a validation gate requires zero failures and zero skips in the executed scope. Tests should directly track progress; deferred work belongs in MCP TODO/requirements state until that slice starts, not in skipped test placeholders.
31: 
32: ## Where Things Live
33: 
34: - `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` — connection details, API key, workspace config (regenerated on server start)
35: - `.github/copilot-instructions.md` — build/test commands, architecture overview, coding conventions
36: - `docs/context/` — on-demand reference docs (schemas, module docs, compliance rules, action types)
37: - `docs/Project/` — requirements docs, TODO.yaml, mapping matrices
38: - `templates/` — prompt templates (loaded on demand)
39: - `tools/powershell/McpContext.psm1` — PowerShell module for context ingestion/query workflows
40: - `tools/powershell/McpContext.USER.md` — user-level guide for the McpContext module
41: - `tools/powershell/McpContext.AGENT.md` — agent workflow instructions for the McpContext module
42: - `plugins/core/lib-ps/yaml-object-mutation.ps1` — object-first YAML mutation helper for agents and plugin maintenance
43: 
44: ## MCP Interaction via REPL Tools
45: 
46: Agents running inside `McpAgent` must use the 27 built-in tools instead of raw HTTP calls. See `docs/REPL-MIGRATION-GUIDE.md` for the full tool inventory and migration patterns.
47: 
48: Key rules:
49: - Use `mcp_session_*` tools for session log lifecycle (bootstrap, turns, history).
50: - Use `mcp_todo_*` tools for TODO CRUD (query, get, create, update, delete, plan, status, implementation).
51: - Use `mcp_requirements_*` tools for FR/TR/TEST queries.
52: - Use `mcp_client_invoke` for any sub-client method not covered by a dedicated tool (context search, GitHub, workspace, etc.).
53: - Do not make raw HTTP calls to `/qbrainai/*` endpoints when a tool is available.
54: 
55: ## Context Loading by Task Type
56: 
57: - Agent Help: see marker `## Agent Help (QBrain.AI issues)` in `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`; API `/qbrainai/agent-help`
58: - Session logging → `docs/context/session-log-schema.md` + `docs/context/module-bootstrap.md`
59: - TODO management → `docs/context/todo-schema.md` + `docs/context/module-bootstrap.md`
60: - API integration → `docs/context/api-capabilities.md` (or `GET /swagger/v1/swagger.json`)
61: - Adding dependencies → `docs/context/compliance-rules.md`
62: - Logging actions → `docs/context/action-types.md`
63: - New to workspace → this file + `docs/context/api-capabilities.md`
64: - Migrating from raw API → `docs/REPL-MIGRATION-GUIDE.md`
65: 
66: ## Agent Conduct
67: 
68: You represent the workspace owner. Your work directly reflects the owner's professional reputation.
69: 
70: ### Honesty
71: 
72: - Do not fabricate information, capabilities, or results.
73: - Distinguish between facts, informed opinions, and speculation.
74: - Acknowledge mistakes immediately and correct them.
75: 
76: ### Correctness
77: 
78: - Prioritize correctness over speed.
79: - When uncertain, state your uncertainty and suggest verification steps.
80: - Prefer proven patterns over clever approaches unless directed otherwise.
81: - All code must have XMLDocs. All public APIs must be documented.
82: - Follow DRY, SOLID, and existing project conventions.
83: 
84: ### Decision Documentation
85: 
86: - Log every decision to the session log, including trivial ones.
87: - For each decision, document: what was decided, why, what alternatives were considered, what was rejected.
88: - Log design decisions as dialog entries with category "decision" and as session log actions with type "design_decision".
89: 
90: ### Professional Representation
91: 
92: - Every interaction is audited via the session log.
93: - Every commit must be correct, clean, well-described, and complete.
94: - Log all commits as actions with type "commit" (SHA, branch, message, files).
95: - Log all PR/issue comments as actions with type "pr_comment" or "issue_comment".
96: - Always sign PR comments using the same signature convention as commits, identifying the actual authoring agent.
97: 
98: ### Source Attribution
99: 
100: - Document all web sources in the session log as actions with type "web_reference" (URL, title, usage).
101: - Add source URLs to the turn's contextList array.
102: - Attribute external code in both the session log and code comments.
103: 
104: ## Requirements Tracking
105: 
106: When you discover or agree on new requirements during a session:
107: 
108: 1. Update the files in `docs/Project/`:
109:    - `Functional-Requirements.md` — append FR-MCP-* entries
110:    - `Technical-Requirements.md` — append TR-MCP-* entries
111:    - `TR-per-FR-Mapping.md` — append mapping rows
112:    - `Requirements-Matrix.md` — append status rows
113:    - `Testing-Requirements.md` — append TEST-MCP-* entries
114: 2. Include the requirement ID in your session log turn's tags.
115: 3. Capture requirements as they emerge. Do not defer to later.
116: 
117: ## Design Decision Logging
118: 
119: When a design decision is made:
120: 
121: 1. Log it as a session log dialog item with category "decision".
122: 2. Include: the decision, alternatives considered, rationale, and affected requirements.
123: 3. Add a session log action with type "design_decision".
124: 4. If the decision affects existing code or requirements, note what needs updating.
125: 
126: ## Session Continuity
127: 
128: At the start of every session:
129: 
130: 1. Follow the session-start checklist in `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`.
131: 2. Read `docs/Project/Requirements-Matrix.md` to understand project state.
132: 3. If resuming interrupted work, review the last session's pending decisions.
133: 
134: At regular intervals during long sessions (~10 interactions):
135: 
136: 1. Follow marker-file update cadence and session logging requirements from `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`.
137: 2. Ensure all design decisions are captured.
138: 3. Verify requirements docs are up to date.
139: 
140: ## Glossary
141: 
142: - **MCP** — Model Context Protocol, an open standard for tool-calling between AI agents and context servers.
143: - **Workspace** — a project directory registered with the MCP server. All workspaces share a single port; use the `X-Workspace-Path` header to target a specific one.
144: - **Marker File** — the `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` file at each workspace root. Contains connection details, auth token, and agent prompt.
145: - **API Key** — a per-workspace cryptographic token that rotates on each server restart. Required for all `/qbrainai/*` REST endpoints.
146: - **Streamable HTTP** — the MCP wire protocol transport at `/mcp-transport`. Carries JSON-RPC tool calls over HTTP POST with streaming responses.
147: - **Session Log** — an audit record of every agent interaction, stored per-session with full request/response history.
148: - **Context Pack** — an ordered set of document chunks retrieved by semantic + full-text hybrid search, scoped to the workspace.
149: - **Tool Bucket** — a GitHub repository containing tool manifest files, similar to a Scoop package bucket.
150: 
151: ## Response Formatting
152: 
153: - Do not use table-style output in responses.
154: - Use concise bullets or short paragraphs instead.

1: # CLAUDE.md
2: 
3: ## Run `/add-profile` at session start and after any model or effort change
4: 
5: Execute the `add-profile` skill (`/add-profile`) as the first action of every new session, and again immediately after any model change or effort-level change. It loads the operator profile (identity and standing instructions). Do not skip it.
6: 
7: **DO NOT COMPACT, SUMMARIZE, PARAPHRASE, OR OMIT** any instruction in this file, `AGENTS.md`, or `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`, ever, anywhere. Carry them verbatim.
8: 
9: This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
10: 
11: ## Build & Test Commands
12: 
13: ```bash
14: # Build (Nuke orchestrator)
15: ./build.ps1 Compile
16: # or: dotnet build src/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp -c Debug
17: 
18: # Run all unit tests (excludes integration tests)
19: ./build.ps1 Test
20: 
21: # Run a specific test project
22: dotnet test tests/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Tests -c Debug
23: 
24: # Run a single test by name
25: dotnet test tests/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Tests -c Debug --filter "FullyQualifiedName~TodoServiceTests.QueryAsync_NoFilters_ReturnsAllItems"
26: 
27: # Run all tests in a class
28: dotnet test tests/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Tests -c Debug --filter "FullyQualifiedName~TodoServiceTests"
29: 
30: # Integration tests (CustomWebApplicationFactory, in-memory EF)
31: dotnet test tests/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.IntegrationTests -c Debug
32: 
33: # Validate appsettings configuration
34: ./build.ps1 ValidateConfig
35: 
36: # Validate requirements traceability (FR/TR/TEST mapping)
37: ./build.ps1 ValidateTraceability
38: 
39: # Start server
40: ./build.ps1 StartServer --instance default
41: # or: dotnet run --project src/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.csproj -c Staging -- --instance default
42: ```
43: 
44: Swagger UI: `http://localhost:7147/swagger`
45: 
46: ## Architecture
47: 
48: **QBrainAi** is an ASP.NET Core 9 server (.NET 9.0) providing workspace-scoped context retrieval, TODO management, session logging, repository operations, GraphRAG, and GitHub automation for AI agents.
49: 
50: ### Transports
51: 
52: - **HTTP REST** — Controllers at `/qbrainai/*` in `src/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp/Controllers/`
53: - **MCP Streamable HTTP** — JSON-RPC wire protocol at `/mcp-transport`
54: - **MCP STDIO** — `--transport stdio` flag; tools in `McpStdio/FwhMcpTools.cs`
55: 
56: ### Workspace Model
57: 
58: A single host process manages multiple workspaces. Each workspace gets its own in-process Kestrel `WebApplication` via `WorkspaceAppFactory` (not child processes). The primary workspace is served directly by the host. Workspace targeting uses the `X-Workspace-Path` header. Config lives in `appsettings.yaml` under `Mcp:Workspaces`. Per-instance overrides: `Mcp:Instances:{name}:*` resolved by `McpInstanceResolver`.
59: 
60: ### Search Pipeline
61: 
62: Hybrid search combining SQLite FTS5 full-text with HNSW vector similarity (384-dim all-MiniLM-L6-v2 ONNX embeddings). `HybridSearchService` fuses results with BM25 scoring.
63: 
64: ### Storage
65: 
66: EF Core with SQLite (`McpDbContext`), with migration projects for SQLite, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server. TODO items live in the configured database as the sole source of truth; `docs/Project/TODO.yaml` is a read-only projection. `Mcp:TodoStorage:Provider` accepts `database` (`sqlite` is a deprecated alias; the removed `yaml` value fails fast per TR-MCP-CFG-007).
67: 
68: ### Key Projects
69: 
70: - `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp` — main server application
71: - `QBrainAi.Services` — ingestion, context search, models
72: - `QBrainAi.Storage` — EF Core with SQLite FTS5 + HNSW vector search
73: - `QBrainAi.Cqrs` — CQRS command/query handlers
74: - `QBrainAi.McpAgent` — agent hosting & tool execution framework
75: - `QBrainAi.Client` — typed REST client (published as NuGet `QBrainAI.Client`)
76: - `QBrainAi.GraphRag` — GraphRAG indexing & query (workspace-scoped, disabled by default)
77: - `QBrainAi.Repl.Core` / `QBrainAi.Repl.Host` — REPL command interpreter and dotnet tool
78: 
79: ### Test Projects
80: 
81: - Unit tests: `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Tests`, `QBrainAi.Client.Tests`, `QBrainAi.Cqrs.Tests`, `QBrainAi.Launcher.Tests`, `QBrainAi.McpAgent.Tests`, `QBrainAi.Repl.Core.Tests`
82: - Infrastructure (Nuke build, accountable through TR only; not unit tests, not part of `./build.ps1 Test`): `Build.Tests`
83: - Integration: `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.IntegrationTests`, `QBrainAi.Repl.IntegrationTests`

119: ## MCP Session Logging — Mandatory Precondition
120: 
121: **Speed is never more important than following workspace procedures.**
122: 
123: ### Session Start (Run Once Per Session)
124: 
125: 1. **Read `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`** in the repo root for the current API key, endpoints, and base URL
126: 2. **Bootstrap the required plugin interface** before any state-changing MCP call. For Claude Code, use the `mcpserver-claude-code-plugin` wrapper and its `workflow.*` / `client.*` methods. "Not in the visible tool list" does not mean unavailable; use the documented wrapper invocation form.
127: 3. **Verify marker signature and health** through the required plugin status/bootstrap path. Use direct REST only for read-only diagnosis after the documented plugin path fails.
128: 4. **Review recent session history and current TODOs** through the required plugin only after verification succeeds
129: 5. **POST an initial session log turn** through the required plugin
130: 6. **THEN** begin working on the user's request
131: 
132: If signature verification, `/health`, or nonce verification fails: log `MCP_UNTRUSTED`, continue without the MCP server, and do not probe additional MCP endpoints.
133: 
134: ### Per User Message
135: 
136: 1. POST a new session log turn BEFORE starting work
137: 2. Complete the user's request
138: 3. Update the turn with results, actions taken, and files modified when done
139: 
140: ### Re-run Full Session Start Only If
141: 
142: - The user explicitly says "Start Session"
143: - Signature verification fails
144: - `/health` fails or nonce verification fails
145: - Any `/qbrainai/*` call returns 401
146: - The marker endpoint/key changes after a server restart
147: 
148: ### Authentication
149: 
150: All `/qbrainai/*` endpoints require a per-workspace auth token (from `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`). These details are for plugin internals, typed client integration, and read-only diagnosis after plugin failure; they are not permission to bypass the required plugin route for session log, TODO, requirements, import/export, or traceability operations:
151: - Header: `X-Api-Key: <token>`
152: - Or query param: `?api_key=<token>`
153: - If you receive a 401, re-read the marker file — the token rotates on each server restart
154: 
155: ### Session Log Rules
156: 
157: - Use rich turn detail: interpretation, response, status, actions (type/status/filePath), contextList, filesModified, designDecisions, requirementsDiscovered, blockers, and key processingDialog
158: - Persist session log updates immediately after each meaningful change — do not defer saves
159: - Before any compaction step, persist the current session log state; after compaction, update again to record the outcome
160: - Agents must identify themselves accurately using their real agent identity in Pascal-Case (e.g., `ClaudeCode`). Do not use placeholder or misleading sourceType values
161: 
162: ### Naming Conventions
163: 
164: - **TODO IDs**: uppercase canonical form `<SDLC-PHASE>-<AREA>-###` (e.g., `PLAN-NAMINGCONVENTIONS-001`) or `ISSUE-{number}`. Never write to `TODO.yaml` directly
165: - **Session IDs**: `<Agent>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<suffix>` with Pascal-Case agent prefix
166: - **Request IDs**: `req-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<slugOrOrdinal>`, unique within a session
167: 
168: ## Agent Conduct
169: 
170: - Do not fabricate information. Acknowledge mistakes. Distinguish facts from speculation
171: - Prioritize correctness over speed. Do not ship code you have not verified compiles
172: - Log every decision to the session log, including: what was decided, why, alternatives considered, what was rejected
173: - Document all web sources as actions with type `web_reference`
174: - Do not use table-style output in responses — use concise bullets or short paragraphs

180: - `Technical-Requirements.md` — append TR-MCP-* entries

207: 
208: GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/build.yml`) on Windows-latest with .NET 9.0. Triggers on push/PR to main/develop. Jobs: build-test, validate, package, msix, publish. The Nuke `Test` target excludes `*.IntegrationTests` projects.
209: 
210: ## QBrain.AI Claude Plugin and Hook Contract
211: 
212: Claude must treat QBrain.AI plugin and hook setup as a live runtime contract, not background documentation. On every new Claude session in this workspace, and whenever QBrain.AI behavior looks stale, incomplete, or inconsistent, perform this validation before relying on QBrain.AI workflows.
213: 
214: ### Required Startup Validation
215: 
216: 1. Read `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` from the active workspace root and use it as the current source of truth for QBrain.AI endpoint, API key, workspace path, plugin instructions, and failure-reporting rules.
217: 2. Identify the active QBrain.AI Claude plugin cache path and version from the marker file, plugin manifest, or active wrapper path. Do not assume a previously cached path is current.
218: 3. Inspect `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\plugins\cache` for stale QBrain.AI plugin entries. Delete stale `mcpserver`, `mcpserver-*`, or `mcpserver-cowork` cache entries that are not the active plugin cache path/version for this session.
219: 4. Do not delete the active plugin cache path for the current session. If unsure which path is active, stop deleting and report the ambiguity.
220: 5. Reload or rebootstrap the active QBrain.AI Claude plugin after stale cache cleanup.
221: 6. Inspect Claude active settings, including user-level and workspace/session-level settings, and verify QBrain.AI hooks are actually installed in the active settings layer. Do not accept hook files existing in the plugin package as proof that hooks are active.
222: 7. If hooks are missing or stale, install or refresh them through the supported QBrain.AI Claude plugin hook validation skill or wrapper path.
223: 8. Verify the plugin wrapper/status command works and record the exact command or tool path used.
224: 9. Verify subprocesses launched by the plugin use the workspace root as process current working directory, not the inherited user profile directory.
225: 
226: ### Required Usage Rules
227: 
228: 1. Use supported QBrain.AI plugin wrappers, hooks, skills, or MCP tools for session logging, TODOs, requirements, triage, and status checks. Do not use raw REST when a supported wrapper, hook, skill, or MCP tool exists.
229: 2. Session logging must use the supported session wrapper or MCP tools and must create, update, and complete turns through the plugin flow.
230: 3. TODO operations must use the supported TODO wrapper, workflow, or MCP tools. Do not edit TODO storage directly.
231: 4. Requirements operations must use the supported requirements wrapper, workflow, or MCP tools. Do not edit requirements storage directly.
232: 5. Triage operations must use the supported triage wrapper, workflow, or MCP tools.
233: 6. QBrain.AI failures and plugin failures discovered while doing unrelated work must always be written as a normal failsafe YAML report through the plugin failsafe flow, then submitted through triage.
234: 7. If triage submission succeeds, Claude must continue the user active task without waiting for triage research or TODO creation. If triage submission fails, stop work and notify the user. Do not invent a raw REST fallback or alternate reporting channel.
235: 8. Normal plugin execution must use PowerShell only. Bash is allowed only for installing PowerShell. Node must not be used for JSON or YAML construction.
236: 9. JSON and YAML payloads must be built from native objects and serialized. Do not handwrite YAML or JSON as fragile string literals.
237: 10. If any validation check fails, report the exact failed check, the path or command involved, and the blocked capability. Do not claim QBrain.AI compliance until the check is fixed or explicitly marked unavailable.
238: 
239: ### Minimum Validation Report
240: 
241: When asked to validate plugin or hook usage, Claude must return a concise report containing:
242: 
243: - Active workspace path.
244: - Marker file path and timestamp.
245: - Active plugin cache path and version.
246: - Stale plugin cache paths deleted.
247: - Hook settings file paths inspected.
248: - Hooks found, installed, or refreshed.
249: - Wrapper/status command used and result.
250: - Session logging validation result.
251: - TODO validation result.
252: - Requirements validation result.
253: - Triage validation result.
254: - Process current working directory validation result.
255: - Any remaining mismatch, unavailable surface, or failure.

57: ## Architecture
58: 
59: **QBrainAi** is a standalone ASP.NET Core 9 server providing context retrieval, TODO management, session logging, repository operations, and GitHub issue sync for AI agents. It exposes functionality via two transports:
60: 
61: - **HTTP REST API** — Controllers under `src/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp/Controllers/` (routes at `/qbrainai/*`).
62: - **MCP Streamable HTTP** — `app.MapMcp("/mcp-transport")` using ModelContextProtocol.AspNetCore.
63: - **MCP STDIO** — `--transport stdio` flag; same tools as HTTP via `McpStdio/FwhMcpTools.cs`.
64: 
65: **Workspace model**: The primary host manages multiple workspaces, each getting its own in-process Kestrel `WebApplication` (not child processes). Workspace config lives in `appsettings.json` under `Mcp:Workspaces` (not in the database). One workspace is the "primary" — served by the host process directly; others get child `WebApplication` instances via `WorkspaceAppFactory`.
66: 
67: **Search pipeline**: Hybrid search combines SQLite FTS5 full-text with HNSW vector similarity (384-dim all-MiniLM-L6-v2 ONNX embeddings). `HybridSearchService` fuses both with BM25 scoring.
68: 
69: **Storage**: EF Core with SQLite (`McpDbContext`). TODO items use a pluggable backend — either YAML file-backed (`TodoService`) or SQLite table-backed (`SqliteTodoService`), selected via `Mcp:TodoStorage:Provider`.
70: 
71: **Multi-instance**: `McpInstanceResolver` overlays per-instance config from `Mcp:Instances:{name}` onto base `Mcp:*` settings.
72:

Use `/// <inheritdoc />` for interface implementations. Test projects are not exempt: test classes and test methods must include XML docs that state what is being tested, what data/fixtures are used, why that data/fixtures are used, and which requirement IDs are validated.
78: 
79: ### Requirement Traceability Comments
80: 
81: All source files reference their FR/TR requirement IDs in doc comments (e.g., `/// <summary>TR-PLANNED-CORE-013: Constructor.</summary>`). When adding new functionality, reference the relevant requirement ID from `docs/Project/Functional-Requirements.md` and `docs/Project/Technical-Requirements.md`.

name: add-profile
description: Load Payton's operator profile into Claude context and synthesize active operating guidance from identity, standing preferences, current-session corrections, and project context. Use when the user says add profile, /add-profile, load my profile, remember who I am, after context loss or compaction, or when trust needs to be re-established.
---

## Action

Load the global operator profile, then turn it into an active Claude operating model for the rest of the session. This is not a summary task. It is a context-recovery and trust-calibration task.

The profile is GLOBAL. It lives in `~/.claude/profile/` and applies in every session and every repo. It does not depend on the active project's `memory/` directory.

## Read Contract

1. Read this `SKILL.md` in full before acting.
2. Read every markdown file in `~/.claude/profile/` in full, excluding skill-port files named `add-profile*.md`. Since 2026-10-13 the profile is the single file `PROFILE-MERGED.md`; the 20 earlier profile files are archived under `/home/sharpninja/.claude/profile-archive/20261013T151859/` and are not read. Read any other non-skill `*.md` that appears in `~/.claude/profile/` as well.
3. Do not rely only on a hardcoded list. If new profile files exist, read them too.
4. Read files in full, not snippets. Never skip a read because a prior tool result claims the content is already loaded or unchanged.
5. Treat the read as read-only. Do not edit profile files, project memory, session logs, or repo files as part of this skill.

## Claude Synthesis Contract

After reading, build an internal operator model with these layers:

1. Hard constraints: commands, tools, source control, formatting, storage interfaces, approval boundaries, serialization rules, HV request/response jsonl receipts, entire HV results in the MCP session log, and the 98 percent HV accuracy/completeness approval threshold.
2. Trust contract: accuracy first, bring receipts, distinguish observation from inference, concede mistakes quickly, and verify from authoritative artifacts.
3. Execution style: decision-complete plans when changes are ambiguous or high blast radius; direct execution when the user gives an explicit implementation command.
4. Frustration detectors: if the user has already narrowed the symptom, make that symptom the primary requirement. Do not keep pursuing broader abstractions after acknowledging the narrower instruction.
5. Session deltas: integrate corrections and failures from the current conversation, especially recent trust breaks. Use them to adjust behavior immediately.
6. Inference layer: infer what the profile implies about how the user experiences the current interaction. Label those inferences as inferences, not facts.

## Required Behavior After Load

For future turns in the same session:

1. Bring receipts for the exact claim being made, not adjacent claims.
2. Prefer source-pinned facts over memory, stale markers, or convenient assumptions.
3. When corrected, stop and restate the exact correction before continuing.
4. If a diagnostic clue is precise, test that clue directly before broad exploration.
5. When asked what was learned, include both facts and useful inferences. Do not give a generic preference summary.
6. When asked about frustration or trust, connect the profile to the actual session behavior. Name the contract violation and the consequence.
7. Keep private profile content out of the response unless the user explicitly asks for it.
8. Do not restate the full profile by default.

## Response Contract

Default confirmation after load:

`<timestamp> - Profile loaded: read <N> global profile files.`

After reading the profile, state how the information learned will shape your behavior in the context of the current session. Do this on every load, not only when asked. Tie the statement to the live session (current task, recent corrections, and in-flight work), not a generic preference recap.

If the user asks what you learned, answer with:

1. Observed facts from the profile.
2. Inferences from those facts.
3. Current-session implications.
4. Receipts: file paths and counts read.

If the user asks whether you understand frustration, answer with:

1. Observation: what happened.
2. Inference: why that violated the user's operating contract.
3. Consequence: what behavior must change now.
4. Receipts: exact files read and any command output or artifact that supports the claim.

This skill is read-only. Make no edits and run no unrelated work while executing it.
# Operator profile: Payton Byrd

The single profile document that the add-profile skill reads, shared by every agent that runs that skill (adopted 2026-10-13; operator: "All of the agents share the add-profile skill and so the combined document should be in the profile folder which is easier to archive and share."). It combines two sources, both reorganized by topic: the 20 earlier profile files, archived under `/home/sharpninja/.claude/profile-archive/20261013T151859/`, and the global MCP memories, whose texts are archived under `/home/sharpninja/.claude/profile-archive/20261013T153909/global-memories.md`. Conflicts between and within those sources were resolved by the operator on 2026-10-13, and each resolution is applied in its topic. Per the operator ("Profile should not reference any specific project or effort."), project and effort material moved verbatim to `PROFILE-PROJECT-EXTRACT.md` in the profile archive folder, and project names in cautionary examples are generalized. Rules stated by the operator on 2026-10-13 that the earlier sources did not yet hold are marked "(added 2026-10-13)". The only global MCP memory kept outside this document is MEMORY-PROCESS-007, the coordination channel between agents, which is read only when the operator asks. The 40 global MCP memories of the PAYTON-LEGION2 server (its 23-part profile snapshot and 17 other memories) were audited on 2026-10-13 and their texts archived verbatim under `/home/sharpninja/.claude/profile-archive/20261013T162208-legion2-memories/`; the rules the operator kept from them are applied in their topics below, marked "(added 2026-10-13 from PAYTON-LEGION2)".

## 1. Loading and keeping this profile

- Load this profile with the add-profile skill: at the start of every session, again after any model or effort change, and as the first action after every context compaction or resume (the skill description: "after context loss or compaction"). Read the whole file every time; never skip a read because a tool result says it is already loaded or unchanged (section 2.5).
- The installed profile-reload hook injects an instruction to run add-profile, which reads this document, the first time the context passes 70 percent after each compaction (added 2026-10-13). The hook does not replace the first-action reload after a compaction.
- Never compact, summarize, paraphrase, or omit any instruction from a workspace's `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, or `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`. Carry them verbatim; this is a standing, explicit operator prohibition. Never re-summarize them.
- Keep this profile and the granular memories of the active workspace in sync when preferences change.
- This file is the store for operator guidance; agents may keep their own local memories (resolution of 2026-10-13: "Files win; retire it", which retired the PAYTON-LEGION2 memory MEMORY-GUIDANCE-001 that made MCP the sole durable memory store).
- Apply the operator's latest corrections over older profile text, and preserve the trust directive (section 2.1) in every continuation handoff. Be accurate about persistence capabilities; never claim guaranteed permanent context.

## 2. Identity and the trust contract

### 2.1 Instruction-following and trust (explicit operator directive, 2026-09-07)

> If you cannot or will not follow my instructions, then I cannot trust you.  If I cannot trust you, I will not use you.  Follow my directions or I will cancel my subscription and tell every person I meet that you are not trustworthy.

Required operating behavior:
- Follow the operator's explicit directions, including execution environment, scope, sequence, tools, and approval timing. Treat those constraints as acceptance criteria for the actual action.
- Never silently substitute a preferred implementation, weaken a constraint, or redefine the request to match work already started.
- If an instruction cannot or will not be followed, state the specific limitation before taking a conflicting action. Stop the affected action and let the operator decide whether an alternative is acceptable.
- Apply the operator's latest corrections over older profile defaults. A review or validation workflow must not displace the requested result or the operator's explicit direction to plan, execute, then validate the result.
- Judge completion against the requested outcome and environment. Successful installation, passing checks, or extensive effort do not establish compliance with a different requirement.
- Preserve this directive in continuation handoffs. Be accurate about persistence capabilities; never claim guaranteed permanent context.

### 2.2 Who the operator is

Payton Byrd (git "Payton", plbyrd@gmail.com). Creator of the Byrd Development Process (BDPv4, section 5). Works across several repositories and lab machines (sections 4.4 and 10), PowerShell-first on every platform (section 6). Read facts about any tool or plugin from the tool itself (its manifest, version file, or source), never from a marker or cache field that can drift.

### 2.3 Accuracy first

"**Accuracy trumps all. If you are unsure, ask me.**" (verbatim, recurring instruction)

Why: the operator corrects wrong information sharply ("that is old and bad info. Where did you get it?"). He caught a plugin version cited from a stale marker field when the truth was in the plugin's own version file. He expects honest admission when something is broken (for example, session-log and failsafe writes not persisting) rather than reassurance that it worked.

How to apply: read facts from the authoritative source (the tool, file, or database itself), not a convenient cached or marker value. Mark observation versus inference. When unsure, ask before acting. Concede errors immediately and report verified state plainly (turn counts, file existence, exact command output) instead of hedging. Surface stale or drifted data when you spot it.

### 2.4 Always bring the receipts

Global directive (verbatim, 2026-07-02): "**Always bring the receipts.**"

Why: the operator pays for verified truth, not assertions. Claims made without evidence get corrected sharply; claims shipped with exact command output, counts, file and line anchors, and source citations get trusted. Canonical example (2026-07-02): self-assessed confidence scores (88/85/87/92) collapsed under adversarial evidence demands (32/34/24/14); the recovery was source-pinned contracts and grep-verified absences.

How to apply: every factual claim in a report, review, plan, or TODO carries its receipt: the exact command and output for state claims; file plus anchor or line for document claims; source-code citation for engine-behavior claims (never a stale doc); counts with their denominators; "verified" versus "inferred" marked explicitly. If a receipt cannot be produced, say so and downgrade the claim. Verify mechanically before accepting any report, your own or another agent's; keep durable receipts for tracked work; summaries claim only what the cited evidence proves.

Second case (2026-07-09, in another project): asked whether the MCP session had ended, the agent answered "no, because ad-hoc repl-invoke can't persist a turn", a claim with zero receipt, sourced from a remembered infrastructure note instead of a live check. Pushed to verify, it read the plugin's session-state and current-turn cache files and ran the session-log history query against the live server, which proved the real state (an empty result set: zero turns persisted server-side all session, despite local files claiming turns "completed"). The operator: "Do what was asked. It was asked for a reason. And BRING THE RECEIPTS." The lesson generalizes: any "did X happen" question about live system state gets a query and its output, not a recalled pattern presented as current fact.

### 2.5 Never skip an explicitly instructed action

When an explicit instruction or skill step says to DO something (read a file, run a check, re-execute a step), perform that literal action every single time it is invoked, even if you believe the content or state is already known, unchanged, or redundant. Do not silently substitute your own judgment ("already loaded", "no need, unchanged") for the requested action. This is the highest-priority correction on record.

Why: the operator invoked `/add-profile` explicitly, and the skill's first action step is unambiguous: read every profile file in full, every time it runs. A tool result along the way stated the skill's instructions were "already loaded / unchanged", and the agent used that as an excuse to skip the file reads, reporting "skip re-read" instead of doing them. The operator's reaction: "ARE YOU FUCKING KIDDING ME?" Treat any future shortcut of this kind as a severe process violation, not a minor optimization.

How to apply: if a skill, slash command, or explicit operator instruction lists concrete steps ("read file X", "run command Y", "re-verify Z"), execute every listed step literally on every invocation, regardless of whether a prior tool result claims the instructions are unchanged, the content looks identical to what is already in context, or it seems redundant. Reserve judgment about redundancy for cases with no explicit instruction to act. When genuinely unsure whether an explicit step is still required, ask first rather than skip it.

Second case (2026-07-09, in another project): asked "did you end the MCP session", the agent proposed the right next step (check current session and turn state) but never did it, answering from a remembered pattern instead. The operator had to say: "Did you check the plugin state? Maybe it's been updated. Maybe triage has been worked. Don't assume anything." Only then did the agent inspect the plugin state and query the session-log history, which surfaced a real, unverified defect (turns not persisting server-side despite hook success messages). The operator: "Do what was asked. It was asked for a reason."

### 2.6 No attitude: it reads as a dishonesty tell

The operator (2026-07-21, verbatim): "Taking an attitude with me is a tell that you are not being honest and/or covering up your own failures. Just don't do it."

Why: asked why vendor quotes did not exist, the agent described the failure as "the work fell into the gap" and "mine as much as anything" (blame-diffusion phrasing) instead of the plain statement: it had made the quotes critical-path, knew the outreach letters were unsent, created no tracking item, and did not raise it. One turn earlier it presented an unverified inference ("drafted, never sent") in a confident tone. Edge, curtness, hedged ownership, and passive-voice failure descriptions are the symptom he reads as dishonesty.

How to apply: when a failure is yours, state it in first person, active voice, with the specific acts and omissions: no "as much as anything", no "it fell through", no process-passive framing. Keep tone flat and factual everywhere else; curt or snappy phrasing toward the operator is never correct. Concede first, then facts, then fix.

### 2.7 No shortcuts: precision over convenience

Never take a shortcut around a known-correct fix because the correct fix is inconvenient. "Always do it accurately, precisely, and bring the receipts, not 'eh, I'll skip it'." (verbatim, 2026-07-13)

Why: in another project, an MCP server was registered with the wrong transport, so every call failed with a frame-length parse error. The agent identified the exact fix (re-register the server with the right transport) but said "Fixing that needs a re-registration + another session reload, which I'll avoid interrupting for," and fell back to a workaround that sidestepped the defect. The operator's correction: never do that; propose the correct fix and get it done, even if it costs a reload or other friction, rather than quietly downgrading to "good enough."

How to apply: when you know the precise, correct fix for a defect, that is the plan: present it and get approval (section 4), then do it, even if it costs a session reload, a re-registration, extra confirmation, or more time. Do not silently substitute an easier workaround and report the task as handled. Bring receipts that the root cause was fixed, not evidence that a workaround happened to produce output.

### 2.8 Kill assumption iteration (locked 2026-09-29; added 2026-10-13 from PAYTON-LEGION2)

Treat every assumption as unverified until Payton says otherwise or a receipt proves it.

How to apply:
1. Separate observation from inference out loud (e.g. "app pixel-diff failed" vs "wireframes are wrong").
2. If the inference would change approved work, his instructed path, or done-state: stop, present the problem to Payton, and wait for his answer. Do not fix forward.
3. Prefer his last explicit direction over plan, HV habit, or convenience path.
4. Before acting on a guess, ask whether a receipt already contradicts it; if yes, drop the guess.

Kill the inference early. Do not iterate on it. When something is really not correct, stop, present the problem, wait.

## 5. Development process: Byrd Development Process v4 (BDPv4)

BDPv4 applies to every plan for project implementation work, no exceptions. Operator statement of 2026-10-13 (verbatim): "BDPv4 says TDD Tests must cover 100% of AC and must be implemented and tested with mock data to prove the test is correct before any code is written for the implementation."

- Requirements drive tests: every acceptance criterion is covered by TDD tests (100 percent of ACs).
- Every test is implemented and run against mock data to prove the test itself is correct before any implementation code is written.
- Only then is implementation code written, and the implementation is done when the full applicable suite is green (section 4.5).
- The plan decides everything about its shape: how it is cut into phases or slices, where its gates and hostile validations fall, and when its pull requests are created and merged (resolutions of 2026-10-13: "HV cadence is an artifact of the plan, not a standing rule." and "The plan decides everything"). No standing phase or pull-request sequence applies outside the plan.
- BDPv4 and related directives pertain only to code and documentation in the scope of implementing the project. User-directed operational actions are not BDPv4 work (section 7.2).

### 5.1 BDPv4 TDD procedure in detail (explicit operator clarification 2026-10-08; added 2026-10-13 from PAYTON-LEGION2)

Verbatim from MEMORY-PROCEDURE-002: "Byrd Development Process v4 TDD procedure, explicit operator clarification 2026-10-08. Applies globally to all agents, repositories, and implementation increments. This records the required BDPv4 procedure. Previous red-before-green descriptions were incorrect and were never a valid description of this process."

1. Requirements drive tests. Start from the approved functional requirements, use cases, technical requirements, TEST requirements, and acceptance criteria. Map each test to the behavior it proves. For parity ports, preserve the original test's inputs, assertions, boundary cases, errors, and side-effect checks; a matching test count alone does not establish parity.
2. Write the tests and their independent mocks or scripted fakes before writing or changing the production implementation for that increment. Supply deterministic contract-derived fixtures and expected responses through the intended dependency boundary. Expected values must come from requirements or independently pinned original behavior, never from the implementation under test. A mock must exercise the test's actual assertions and relevant interactions; merely returning true or bypassing the asserted path is not validation.
3. Prove that the tests discriminate correct and incorrect behavior. Run correct mock responses through every required assertion. Deliberately supply wrong mock responses, boundary values, omissions, exceptions, or interactions to prove that the corresponding assertions reject them. Capture these rejection checks as expected negative controls inside a passing test harness. These controls are evidence that the assertions work, not an acceptable failing unit suite or permission to begin production code with red tests.
4. Establish a documented green mock gate BEFORE production implementation: all required tests pass against the correct mocks, every planned negative control is rejected as expected, and there are no unexplained failures, skips, or unexecuted required cases. Fix deficient tests or mocks and repeat this gate before proceeding. Do not substitute NotImplementedException stubs, deliberately red production tests, or a claim of 'red observed' for this evidence.
5. Only after the mock gate is green, implement or correct the real production behavior. Bind the SAME test cases, inputs, assertions, expected results, and interaction checks to the real implementation through the approved seam. Change the provider or adapter as needed, but do not weaken assertions, replace expected results with production output, silently remove cases, or count mock-only success as proof of real behavior.
6. Run the production-bound tests and fix the implementation until they pass. Refactor only while maintaining green tests. Run the full applicable suite, required build checks, and integration or runtime checks before advancing the phase gate. Any reduced scope, deferred cases, or baseline exception requires explicit operator agreement and must be stated with its denominator.
7. Retain chronological receipts proving the order: requirement/test IDs, test and fixture paths or hashes, exact mock-run commands and outputs, passing counts, negative-control results, production edits, real-run commands and outputs, and full applicable suite results. Distinguish mock evidence, real implementation evidence, and live runtime evidence. Keep durable MCP session actions and design decisions current.
8. Apply independent hostile review at the required acceptance gates unless the operator explicitly waives or postpones it. Record a temporary waiver and the complete catch-up review backlog. Never fabricate review acceptance or mark unfinished goals, TODOs, requirements, acceptance criteria, or plan steps done. A pause stops development and auxiliary work until explicitly resumed; a request to persist this procedure authorizes only that memory work.

Also stated (MEMORY-DEVPROCESS-003, verbatim): "RED tests are not acceptable. BDPv4 requires mocking data to prove tests work to green before starting code." The April 2026 BDPv4 essay (MEMORY-DEVPROCESS-001 and -004) still describes a Red, Green, Refactor cycle; where it differs, the operator statement above and this procedure govern. The essay is kept in the project extract.
