561: ### 13.4 Standard result document (S-13)
562: 
563: `GET /requests/{hvRequestId}/result` returns `HvResultDocument`:
564: 
565: `{ schema: "qbrainai.hv.result/1", hvRequestId, status, scope, submitter, reviewer: { reviewerId, expectedModel, expectedEffort, runtimeModel, runtimeEffort, runId, attempt, reviewerAgent, reviewerSessionId, reviewerRequestId }, request: <the complete accepted request of section 13.3>, responseLog: [<every JSONL record of the finalized run, in order, starting with its hv_brief record>], turnAssessments: [{ ordinal, agent, sessionId, requestId, correctness, completeness, verdict, mappedReviewStatus, summary, findings }], holistic: { correctness, completeness, verdict, summary, crossTurnFindings }, failures: [{ ordinal, scope, turnOrdinal, agent, sessionId, requestId, responseId, check, outcome, category, location, requirementRef, claimId, evidence, remediation }], responseGrades: [{ responseId, disposition, gradeId, verdict, correctness, completeness, findings }], overallVerdict, thresholds: { correctness, completeness }, evidence: { request: { sha256, bytes, compressedBytes }, responseLog: { chainSha256, bytes, lines, chunks }, result: { sha256 } }, todoIds: [string], finalizedUtc }`.
566: 
567: - `turnAssessments` lists every requested turn with its score (S-21); `failures` is the delineated list of every FAIL and UNKNOWN of every scope (`Turn`, `Holistic`, `Response`), each with its remediation (S-13); `responseGrades` lists every response of the accepted request with its grade record and findings, and its `disposition` (`Graded`, or `Closed` when the response left the review before the commit, whose grade record is kept here but applied to nothing); `request` and `responseLog` are complete (S-13); `evidence.result.sha256` is `ResultSha256`, the digest of the stored `Result` payload, which excludes this field (section 12); `todoIds` is information only (R-22).
568: - With `Accept-Encoding: gzip` the document is sent compressed; the `responseLog` array is streamed from the chunks, so the server holds no uncompressed copy (R-14).
569: - Before finalization the route answers 409 `hv_result_not_ready` with the request's status; after evidence removal it answers 410 `hv_evidence_removed` with the hashes and sizes it still holds.
570: 
571: ### 13.5 Streams
572: 
573: - Output stream: event `hv_output` with `id` `<runId>:<sequence>` and data `{ runId, sequence, lines: [string] }`, one event per stored chunk; event `hv_run_closed` with data `{ runId, status }` when the run ends; a new attempt starts a new run id in the same stream, so `Last-Event-ID` `<runId>:<sequence>` resumes after that chunk of that run. Per S-18 a caller attaches to "any running hv": the stream serves the request's runs in attempt order.
574: - Notification stream: event `<kind>` with `id` `<sequence>` and data `HvNotificationDto`; `Last-Event-ID` `<sequence>` resumes after it. The stream is workspace-scoped (S-19: notifications of HV completion in the plugins).
575: 
576: ### 13.6 Error codes
577: 
578: New entries of the one `ErrorCodes` table (foundation section 3.5.2), each with its status and retryable flag:
579: 
580: - `audit_unavailable` 503, retryable (AuditLedgerGuard).
581: - `review_hostile_pipeline_only` 403 (A-06).
582: - `turn_immutable` 409 with `details.reason` `hv_pending` or `hv_final` and `details.hvRequestId` (the code exists in the foundation's typed failures, C9; A-07 adds the reasons).
583: - `hv_no_reviewer_available` 409 with `details.reviewers` (each reviewer's id, enabled flag, readiness, reason, and open incident) (S-16).
584: - `hv_scope_invalid` 400 (`details.field`: an unknown kind, a missing or extra scope field, an unknown session, an endpoint turn not in the session, or a range whose start is after its end).
585: - `hv_scope_too_large` 400 (`details.count`, `details.max`).
586: - `hv_scope_includes_submitting_turn` 400.
587: - `hv_scope_empty` 400 (a session scope with no turn left after the submitting turn's exclusion).
588: - `hv_turns_not_terminal`, `hv_turns_pending`, `hv_turns_already_reviewed` 409, each with `details.turns` (and `details.hvRequestIds` for the second and third).
589: - `hv_request_not_cancelable` 409 (`details.status`).
590: - `hv_request_active` 409 (`details.status`: evidence removal of a request that is not `Completed`, `Failed`, or `Canceled`).
591: - `hv_reviewer_disabled` 409 (a NONCE requested for a disabled reviewer).
592: - `hv_result_not_ready` 409 (`details.status`).
593: - `hv_evidence_not_available` 404 (a kind not produced yet) and `hv_evidence_removed` 410.
594: - `conflict` 409: `retryable: false` for an idempotency key reused with other inputs or a reviewer update whose `expectedStateVersion` is stale (`details.field` `expectedStateVersion`), `retryable: true` when SerializableWrite or ReadableKeyAllocator is exhausted.
595: - `not_found` 404 with `details.resource` `reviewer`, `hv_request`, or `run`.
596: - `evidence_corrupt` 500: a GZIP round trip failed inside admission (SubmitHvRequestCommand) and nothing was saved; on runs it is also an internal failure code.
597: - Internal codes, stored on runs and incidents and never returned by a public route: `stale_fence`, `probe_stale_configuration`, `evidence_corrupt`, `reviewer_launch_failed`, `reviewer_exited_nonzero`, `reviewer_output_invalid`, `reviewer_turn_unverified`, `reviewer_turn_logging_unsupported`, `runtime_identity_mismatch`, `verdict_binding_failed`, `reviewer_not_independent`, `snapshot_changed`, `probe_nonce_mismatch`, `lease_expired`, `attempts_exhausted`, `canceled`, `worker_shutdown`.
598: 
599: ## 14. Units of work (CQRS handlers)
600: 
601: Each unit is one command or query record and its handler, two files in the folders of section 4. WorkspaceResolutionBehavior runs after the dispatch and before every handler (foundation section 3.5.1); each unit lists its 400 `validation_error` with `details.field` `workspacePath` and does not draw it. Every command runs its checks and its save as one SerializableWrite delegate (foundation section 3.5.2) and calls AuditLedgerGuard first inside it (R-19), so each command lists 503 `audit_unavailable` and 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true` (attempts exhausted, nothing saved) and draws them once as the exits of its SerializableWrite call. Reviewer ids in routes and filters pass through AgentIdentity, so an alias addresses its reviewer.

1524: ### 16.3 Reviewer adapter contract [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-001, -003, -008]
1525: 
1526: `IHvReviewerAdapter` (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.HostileValidation.Reviewers`), one implementation per reviewer id:
1527: 
1528: - `BuildLaunch(brief, reviewer)`: a `ProcessStartInfo` built as an argument list, never a shell string, with the brief on standard input or in a temporary file the adapter deletes after the run; the launch arguments come from one shared launch builder that develop's one-shot strategy also uses, so the per-CLI arguments of `OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy` (`AddCodexArguments`, `AddClaudeArguments`, `AddGrokArguments`, `AddClineArguments`, `OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy.cs:238-262`) are written once (DRY); processes start through the existing `IProcessSpawner` and `IProcessEnvironmentService` (`OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy.cs:18-21`), inside a containment the adapter creates at launch and binds to the worker process (for example a process group with a parent-death signal on Linux or a kill-on-close job object on Windows, settled in H1's contract step), so the reviewer and every descendant end when the worker dies, and so killing the run ends the whole tree even after the root has exited (W-03, FR-MCP-HVPIPE-007-AC008, FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008-AC011); develop's `DefaultProcessSpawner` starts an ordinary process and offers only an explicit kill (`src/QBrainAi.Common.AgentCli/DefaultProcessSpawner.cs:12-16,48-51`), so H1 adds the containment. The shared launch builder holds the one table of highest efforts of section 10 (P9). The reviewer runs behind a write barrier verified for its CLI (VI-03, probes of 2026-10-16): Codex `exec -s read-only` (a write attempt was refused by its sandbox), Grok `--permission-mode plan` (a write call was refused; a headless Grok run then ends `cancelled` at the first call that needs approval, so its launch allows the read tools a review uses), and Copilot `--available-tools` naming only read tools (write and shell tools are not offered at all). Claude's and Cline's plan modes are not accepted as barriers on that evidence (Claude's model declined before its barrier was exercised; Cline ran a shell command in plan mode), so Claude's launch restricts its tools structurally (`--tools`) and Cline stays unqualified until H1 proves a barrier. Whether each reviewer's plugin can still log its turn behind its barrier (the plugin writes host-session state and calls the server) is verified in H1 (VI-03, VI-04); a reviewer that cannot fails its NONCE (R-24).
1529: - Live lines (R-12, P8): standard output and standard error are read line by line as the process writes them (asynchronous line reads on the redirected streams), and each line is handed to the run's callback at once; nothing waits for the process to end.
1530: - `NormalizeLine(line, stream)`: a native JSON event line of a CLI run in a JSON streaming mode is kept as written; any other line becomes `{ "type": "hv_raw", "stream", "line" }`.
1531: - `ExtractReviewerRecords(lines)`: one pure function over a run's ordered native lines. It assembles each agent message's complete text by the CLI's event model (Grok's per-token `text` events, Copilot's `assistant.message_delta` events followed by the whole `assistant.message`, Claude's whole assistant messages, Codex's `agent_message` items, Cline's accumulated content) and returns, in message order, every line of that text that is exactly one JSON object of a reviewer record type of section 13.3; the fence lines of a fenced block are ignored, and a line holding other text beside a record is free text. The worker runs it as lines arrive and passes each batch's completed records to AppendHvRunOutputCommand; finalization runs it over the stored log; both get the same records (R-12). Record types the worker writes itself (`hv_brief`, `hv_provenance`, `hv_raw`) are never accepted from message text, so a reviewer cannot forge them.
1532: - `ReadProvenance(run)`: `hv_provenance` lines read from the CLI's own runtime receipt after the run (P-04), sources verified on 2026-10-16 (VI-01): for Codex, the thread's rollout `turn_context` (fields `model` and `effort`; observed `model` `gpt-6-astra`, `effort` `max`), the source the foundation's `runtime_identity` check reads (foundation section 6.3, check 8); for Claude, the session transcript under `~/.claude/projects` (the assistant message `model` and the request `effort`), written only when session persistence is on, so the launch never passes `--no-session-persistence`; for Grok, the session store `~/.grok/sessions/<cwd>/<sessionId>/` (`summary.json` `reasoning_effort`, and a model id that `chat_history.jsonl` names `grok-4.7-build` while the events name `grok-4.7`, so H1 pins the field V-7 compares); for Copilot, the run's own JSON stream (each call's `assistant.message.model` and `user.message.responsesReasoning.effort`; `--usage-output-file` holds the model only); for Cline, none, because its run records hold the model and only whether thinking was on, so V-7 and the NONCE fail closed (L-04, D-06).
1533: - Highest effort when none is configured: the verified values of section 10 (VI-08), never develop's one-shot constants (P9).

Check the dependency chain and the rollout order for each new case, not just the AC text.
290: 
291: ### 7.6 When findings come back
292: 
293: - Ask "What did I miss?", not only "How do I fix this?". Classify each finding (crash window, cross-session addressing, traceability drift, field-set drift, use case vs requirement contradiction, metadata drift, and so on) and sweep the whole artifact for siblings of each class before the next round.
294: - Verify each finding against source before acting.
295: - Separate implementer fixes from operator decisions, and batch operator decisions into one question.
296: - Recurrence signal: when one design area produces new findings in round after round, the problem is structural, usually a missing traceable key or a missing single source of truth. Stop patching. Diff the area against the known-good pattern (for example single writer, one ordered log, idempotency key), return to it, and delete the mechanism the patches added. One design area failed for five rounds until a single minter reading one ordered log replaced the patches.
297: - Indistinguishable inputs: when two histories produce byte-identical inputs (a redelivery of one event versus a separate event with equal fields), no derived key can separate them. Adding per-invocation state such as a counter or salt breaks idempotence instead. Run the what-if on both histories, then state the honest limit: fail closed under an existing rule, probe how often it happens, and document it. Never promise two invariants the inputs cannot support. Before a fix, check it against every invariant the old value satisfied (purity, retry reuse, the two-process tests), not only the finding it repairs.
298: 
299: ### 7.7 Writing fixes
300: 
301: - Fix the deficient requirement. Reconcile with existing requirements first, strengthen an existing AC second, create a new requirement only when the need is genuinely new.
302: - Do not add design mechanism (protocols, algorithms, crash choreography) to plan text. State the observable, testable outcome; the how belongs to the contract step of the plan's phase or slice.
303: - Make each fix minimal, then attack it yourself before the next round; fixes are the main source of new findings. Do not churn text that a prior round accepted.
304: 
305: ### 7.8 Design principle and coordination
306: 
307: - Always have a traceable relationship when coordinating two disparate entities: every record, event, or message carries the root ids of whatever it is a child of or depends on, so it is attributable on its own. A missing parent id is a design failure. Find the commonality first when relating something new to existing knowledge. Where an external format lacks the key, say so and compensate in your own records; never infer it silently.
308: - Coordinating with another agent: use one append-only channel with read-back verification (the global memory MEMORY-PROCESS-007 is that channel). Accept counters that expose real defects; fold refinements in only as minimal ACs. Each effort keeps its own required reviewer and gates; keep cross-effort dependencies acyclic and order-independent. A decision relayed by one agent may not satisfy the other agent's approval controls; the operator may need to state it to each agent directly.
309: 
310: ## 8. MCP server workspaces: marker, session log, TODOs, requirements, triage
311: 
312: These rules apply in every workspace that uses the operator's MCP server and its agent plugin.
313: 
314: - The workspace's own `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` are the authority for the plugin contract, its endpoints, and its startup validation. Read them in full at session start and carry them verbatim; do not keep a copy of them in this profile (resolution of 2026-10-13: "Reference, don't copy"). The one exception is section 6.4.
315: - Operator rule (2026-10-09): Always read the ENTIRE AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml marker at session start, every line, never a partial read. "NEVER do this. The marker is there for YOU, not me." A partial read caused a missed Commit Signing rule.
316: - The MCP server is the only interface to TODO, session-log, and requirement storage. Never edit those files directly; use the plugin wrapper, REPL, or skills, never raw REST. Operative rule that must never be dropped: "Not in the visible tool list" does not mean unavailable; use the documented wrapper invocation form.
317: - Hook validation: refresh missing or stale hooks through the plugin's hook validation skill only when CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT is set; without it, report the hooks as unverified instead of repairing, because the validator then reports hooks missing and its installer re-adds duplicate bridge hooks (section 10; resolution of 2026-10-13: "Caution as a precondition").
318: - Plugin failures and MCP server failures found while doing other work are filed through the plugin's triage route; if the submission succeeds, continue the active task; if it fails, stop and tell the operator.
319: - Confirm turns with a live history query before claiming session-log traceability; never treat a hook's "turn active" message as proof of a server-side write.
320: - Never print or commit secrets; redact HV streams before committing, because reviewers read marker files.
321: 
322: ### 8.1 Who logs what
323: 
324: - Agents always log (added 2026-10-13; operator, verbatim: "BG agents should NEVER skip logging.  NEVER."): every agent that does work (a subagent, a background agent, a reviewer) opens, updates, and completes its own session-log turn through the plugin route and reports its session and request ids; no brief may tell an agent to stay out of the session log.
325: - One turn per real request, per agent (resolution of 2026-10-13: "Per request, per agent"): each agent logs one turn for each real request it handles; a subagent's turn carries the parent turn's session and request ids (section 7.8), so the work is attributable without counting the request twice. Replace real turns canceled by a later open.
326: - A background event with no work of its own (a completion notice) is not an agent: its hook-opened turn is failed as system_event_phantom, and the work it reports is logged by the agent that does it (resolution of 2026-10-13: "Events aren't agents").
327: 
328: ### 8.2 Decisions are conclusions
329: 
330: In the session log, decisions are conclusions and judgments with their consequences, not the steps taken. They go in the turn's design decisions, distinct from its actions. Every sync or wrap-up pass enumerates the real judgment calls of the turn and logs them. Never report "0 decisions (folded into actions)"; that phrasing is the failure mode itself.
331: 
332: Why: the operator has been trying to get agents to log session decisions reliably since February 2026. The pattern: the keystroke trail (actions) gets captured while the reasoning (design decisions) is under-recorded or buried inside action text. He pays for the reasoning, not just the steps. On 2026-06-29 the first sync pass of a 12-round review loop logged 0 decisions and called them "folded into actions", exactly the gap he has been fighting. He flagged it directly: "Decisions are about your conclusions, not the actions you take" and "It feels like you have been deliberately avoiding session logging... especially details of decisions."
333: 
334: How to apply: on every sync or wrap-up, after appending actions, explicitly list the conclusions made this turn, each as judgment plus consequence plus affected requirements or files, and write them to design decisions, append-only (read existing first, send existing plus new, preserve order). A turn that made genuine judgment calls but logs zero decisions is a red flag; re-check before reporting. Heavy reads can time out and render existing decisions blank; that is a read artifact, not an empty section, so re-read before assuming you must recreate. Write the decision when it happens; do not reconstruct it later.
335: 
336: ### 8.3 Turn titles summarize the request
337: 
338: Session-log turn titles are a concise summary of the operator's request: never the literal placeholder "User prompt", and not a verbatim first-line truncation of the prompt.
339: 
340: Why: the operator reviews the session log by turn title; "User prompt" and raw first lines make turns unscannable and indistinguishable.
341: 
342: How to apply: when opening, updating, or completing a turn, set the title to a short request summary. The plugin's prompt hook auto-titles from the prompt's first line and falls back to "User prompt" on empty prompts (Stop-hook continuation turns hit this); the hook cannot summarize, so the agent must refine the title. Never leave a turn titled "User prompt".

1576: ### 16.7 Process HostileReviewWorkerHost: the artifact worker of FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-003 (P1 to P3, D-02)
1577: 
1578: The HostileReview subsystem keeps its own bounded context, queue, entities, and surfaces (R-25); this section is the contract of its missing worker, fixed in H3. The requirements are the stored FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-002 and -003 with their texts unchanged; H0 writes the named tests below for their criteria, against mocks first, and H3 binds them to production.
1579: 
1580: - Host: a hosted `BackgroundService` of its own per workspace application (`src/QBrainAi.Services/HostileReview/Execution/HostileReviewWorkerHost.cs`), not HvWorkerHost, looping on a wake-up or `PollInterval`: ExpireHostileReviewLeasesCommand, then ClaimHostileReviewAttemptCommand until it returns null, running one attempt per claim. It shares with this pipeline only the reviewer adapters' launch builder, live-line path, and containment (section 16.3) and FencedLease (section 11.1).
1581: - Agent: the agent, model, and effort configured for hostile review when they are configured, and otherwise the pooled default agent with its default model and effort (FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-003 criterion 4, store text; P5 removes the single-reviewer pin of `HostileReviewWorkerOptions`). HV's reviewer pool, round-robin, and NONCE do not apply.
1582: - Identities, distinct as criterion 4 requires: the request (the existing request id); one attempt per claim (`AttemptId`, with lease, fence, and attempt number); the AgentPool job that runs it (`PoolJobId`); one model execution per launched process (`ExecutionId`, the existing execution row with model, effort, agent, prompt template and version, run id, and times, criteria 1 to 3); and the one accepted terminal result (`AcceptedResultId` on the request, set once).
1583: - Storage boundary (FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-002 criterion 4): the worker assembles the prompt in memory from links it reauthorizes at dispatch, reads the reviewer's output lines only to parse the result, and stores neither the prompt nor any output line nor any artifact content: only normalized identity, type, version or content hash, the parsed result, and sanitized diagnostics reach queue rows, notifications, logs, receipts, or result metadata.
1584: - Links (P3): every artifact type FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-002 lists resolves through its supported workspace-scoped service, the stored hash is of the resolved content (never of its id), and the limits of criterion 4 refuse more than 64 links, an artifact over 1 MiB decoded, aggregate input over 8 MiB, or uninspectable content.
1585: - Execution: bounded at-least-once across process loss (an expired lease abandons the attempt and a new one runs, up to the configured attempt bound); the reviewer runs contained with its worker (W-03); cancellation is internal to the host and workspace lifecycle and the existing authorized AgentPool cancellation, never a public mutation.
1586: - Audit (P4): every unit below calls AuditLedgerGuard first, and the HostileReview entities gain `IsDeleted` in H3, so each of their writes reaches the ledger and an unwritable ledger stops the unit.
1587: - One accepted terminal result (P2): only CompleteHostileReviewAttemptCommand writes a result, under the attempt's fence, and only while the request has none; a duplicate or late completion returns the accepted result and changes nothing, replacing `AcceptReviewerOutputAsync`'s unfenced overwrite.
1588: - Named tests (H0 against mocks, H3 production): `HostileReviewWorkerUsesConfiguredOrPooledDefaultAgent`, `HostileReviewIdentitiesDistinctRequestAttemptPoolJobExecutionResult`, `HostileReviewAttemptRerunsAfterProcessLossBounded`, `HostileReviewDuplicateOrLateCompletionOneAcceptedResult`, `HostileReviewCancellationInternalOnly` (FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-003 criterion 4); `HostileReviewStoresNoRawArtifactPromptOrOutput`, `HostileReviewLinkLimitsRefused`, `HostileReviewEveryListedArtifactTypeResolvesWithContentHash` (FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-002 criterion 4 and P3).

331: Claims, renews, and takes over the lease of one row, and guards every fenced write, following develop's handoff-ingestion pattern (`HandoffIngestionService.cs:724-735,782-807`). 2: # Architecture Amendment 1: Durable Multi-Agent Hostile Validation
3: 
4: Status: proposed amendment, documentation only. It is not approved, not hostile-validated, and not an authorization to implement. It amends the foundation architecture `docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md` (the "foundation"; at develop `36783b79` it is byte-identical to the copy in the `session-20261009` worktree, SHA-256 `6E5D4F418E78CF9A76AB366F64D4F24002C09E3C3F024502ED89D77C6E77295E`). The plan derived from this amendment is the TODO `PLAN-HVPIPELINE-001`; the problems found while writing it are the TODO `REMED-HVPIPELINE-001`, which that plan pulls in (operator, 2026-10-16, verbatim: "keep track of problems to fix as a single todo item that will be pulled into the plan.").
5: 
6: Operator directive for this document (verbatim): "Create an amendment to the architecture document with the same level of rigor for diagrams, interfaces, AC, UC, and descriptive documentation."
7: 
8: How to read this amendment:
9: 
10: - It follows the foundation's conventions (foundation section 3) unless a clause below amends one. Its diagrams use the foundation's notation (foundation, "How to read the diagrams"): activity diagrams are Mermaid flowcharts read top to bottom, a double-bordered node (`[["..."]]`) is a call to a shared component, policy, or process drawn once where it is defined, every error exit ends in a terminal that names its code, and sequence diagrams list every response a caller can receive in `alt` blocks.
11: - A unit of work is exactly one CQRS command or query with its handler (operator, 2026-10-11: "I want to be clear, unit of work maps to one CQRS handler"). A policy is a rule a handler applies. A process is orchestration that calls handlers (the worker host, the reviewer run, plugin verbs, Director commands).
12: - Section numbers of this amendment are its own (1 to 22, then Addendum B). "Foundation section X" always names the foundation document.
13: - Every statement is marked by its origin: a settled operator requirement is quoted verbatim with its source (section 3); a design resolution is labelled R-n and states its rationale and the alternatives it rejects (section 5); an amended foundation clause is labelled A-n (section 6). Anything else is derived from those three and cites them.
14: - Requirement, test, and use-case identifiers in this document are proposed. The 63 requirement records of section 19 (FR, TR, and TEST `-MCP-HVPIPE-001` to `-021`) and their 21 mappings were created in the canonical store on 2026-10-16 between 16:32:30 and 16:37:30 local, status `pending`, so the requirements are captured as they emerge; the use cases are created in H0 (section 19).
15: 
16: ## 1. Scope, relationship to the foundation, and precedence
17: 
18: - Scope: the durable, multi-agent hostile validation (HV) pipeline the foundation deferred (foundation section 3.1, "Model grade": "We are going to add an HV pipeline in the future, but not in this effort."). The pipeline admits HV requests over session-log turns, schedules them across a pool of five reviewer agents, runs each review as a durable, leased, live-streamed execution, keeps complete compressed evidence, and finalizes per-turn and holistic results in one transaction.
19: - Relationship: the foundation stays the authority for turn logging (Phase A), turn reviews (Phase B), and stateless agent context (Phase C). This amendment adds one bounded context, HostileValidation, and amends the foundation clauses listed in section 6, which are exactly the clauses that assume a manual HV with one configured grader.
20: - Precedence: where section 6 names a foundation clause as amended, the amendment's text governs; every other foundation clause stands unchanged. Because the foundation's plan (PLAN-SESSIONTURNREVIEW-001) was approved on 2026-10-10, the amended clauses are a change to that plan, and the foundation's own rule applies to them: "a change to this document after the plan is approved is a plan change that needs a new hostile validation" (foundation, introduction).
21: - Implementation status of the foundation (verified 2026-10-16 by a search of `src` at `36783b79`): of the foundation's new types only `IDispatcher` exists (`src/QBrainAi.Cqrs/IDispatcher.cs:9`); `SerializableWrite`, `IdempotentCreate`, `ReadableKeyAllocator`, `TurnLocator`, `ScoreLexeme`, `ScoreVerdict`, `ClassifiedErrorException`, `WorkspaceResolutionBehavior`, `RecordSessionTurnReviewCommand`, `CreateAgentContextHvRequestCommand`, and `RecordModelGradeCommand` are architecture only. Every amendment of section 6 is therefore a document change; no migration of an existing table or route is involved.
22: - Authorization: the operator authorized documentation and plan persistence for this work, not implementation. The standing code freeze applies (no new code until the operator approves the plans).
23: 
24: ## 2. Goals and non-goals
25: 
26: Goals:
27: 
28: 1. A durable HV queue whose admission, scheduling, ownership, and finalization survive server restarts, worker crashes, and concurrent workers without losing or duplicating a review result.
29: 2. A reviewer pool of five agents (Cline, Copilot, Claude, Codex, Grok), selected round-robin among the ready reviewers, never the submitter, the agent that wrote the reviewed turns, or an alias of either.
30: 3. Complete evidence: the complete accepted request and the complete response log of every review, compressed at rest with GZIP, verified lossless, retained until explicitly removed, and streamed live while the review runs.
31: 4. Per-turn assessments and a separate holistic evaluation for every request, committed atomically with the turns' hostile reviews; reviewed turns and final results are immutable.
32: 5. Independence: an agent's self-review never affects HV admission, execution, or verdict, and an HV verdict never completes a TODO.
33: 
34: Non-goals (each settled by the operator, section 3): access roles; a force re-review flag; automatic TODO state changes; automatic retention expiry; execution time limits; a second HV verdict store beside this one for turn reviews.
35: 
36: ## 3. Settled requirements (verbatim sources)
37:

Sources: the Cline session `/home/sharpninja/.cline/data/sessions/1792165626722_56f98/1792165626722_56f98.messages.json` (message index in brackets, every operator message read in full on 2026-10-16), the operator's messages in the Claude Code session that wrote this amendment, and the operator profile's standing HV rules. 131: Ownership: the HostileValidation bounded context owns every unit, policy, entity, and process of this amendment. It calls the foundation's SessionTurnLogging (TurnLocator, TurnWritePipeline), TurnReviews (ScoreLexeme, ScoreVerdict, policy HvVerdictMapping), ResponsesAndTrust (RecordModelGradeCommand, DecideAgentResponseTrustCommand), and SharedComponents (SerializableWrite, IdempotentCreate, ReadableKeyAllocator, PagedQuery, ClassifiedErrorException, ContentHasher, SecretRedactor) through their Phase 2 seams, and the existing `ITriageService` (POST `/qbrainai/triage/reports`, `src/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp/Controllers/TriageController.cs:13-14,33`). Namespaces follow the foundation rule (foundation section 3.5): commands in `src/QBrainAi.Services/HostileValidation/Commands/` (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.HostileValidation.Commands`), queries in `.../Queries/`, policies in `.../Policies/`, the worker in `.../Execution/`, adapters in `.../Reviewers/`, entities in `src/QBrainAi.Storage/Entities/HostileValidation/` (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Storage.Entities.HostileValidation`), DTOs in `src/QBrainAi.Client/Models/HostileValidation/` (namespace `QBrainAi.Client.Models.HostileValidation`), one type per file.

133: Trust boundaries:
134: 
135: - Callers authenticate with the workspace API key, as every route does; there are no access roles (S-29). Agent identity is therefore not authenticated by the server: the submitter's identity is the agent of the submitting turn the server finds (R-08), and the limit of that model is stated in section 8.
136: - The reviewer CLI is untrusted input to the server. Its output is evidence to verify, never an instruction; the server parses only the records the reviewer contract defines (section 13.3) and verifies them before anything is finalized (policy HvFinalVerification, section 15).
137: - Turn text sent to a reviewer passes through `SecretRedactor` (foundation section 3.5.2) before it leaves the server; the stored request evidence is the redacted brief exactly as sent.

139: ## 5. Design decisions and resolutions
140: 
141: Each resolution names the settled requirements it implements, its rationale, and the alternatives it rejects. Resolutions are proposals for the operator's approval; the settled requirements of section 3 are not reopened.
142: 
143: - R-01 One bounded context. HostileValidation owns the pipeline and is not gated by `Mcp:AgentContext:Mode`: HV of turns works in every Mode, because the operator's HV requirements (S-01 to S-30) name turns, not agent-context responses. Rejected: extending the foundation's `AgentContextHvRequest` in ResponsesAndTrust (draft 103), because that record is mode-gated (foundation section 3.5.1) and lists responses, not turns, so a turn with no response would silently drop out of review (draft 213, "turn coverage versus response coverage").
144: - R-02 The HV request replaces the foundation's agent-context HV request. `HvRequest` keeps the foundation's key format `hvr-<sessionId>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>` (with `-<nn>` from the second key of one second, ReadableKeyAllocator) and lists turns (`HvRequestTurn`); the agent responses of those turns are linked as `HvRequestResponse` items when Phase C has recorded any. CreateAgentContextHvRequestCommand, GetAgentContextHvRequestQuery, QueryAgentContextHvRequestsQuery, and their entities are superseded (amendment A-04). Rejected: keeping two HV request records (one per turn, one per response), which would need a cross-record consistency rule the foundation never needed.
145: - R-03 Model grades come from finalization only. FinalizeHvRequestCommand dispatches the foundation's RecordModelGradeCommand for each linked response inside its own transaction; the public model-grade route, the two-step `codex exec resume` protocol, and `ModelGrader:*` are removed, and the eight receipt checks become the verification steps V-1 to V-8 of policy HvFinalVerification against evidence the server itself captured (amendment A-05). Rationale: the pipeline launches the reviewer and records its complete output, so the server no longer has to trust receipts written by a runner it did not control. Rejected: keeping the reviewer-submitted grade route beside the pipeline, which would let a grade bypass reviewer exclusion and atomic finalization (S-17, S-23).
146: - R-04 Freeze at admission, finality at finalization (S-06, S-07). Admission sets each member turn's HV state to `Pending` in the same transaction that creates the request; finalization sets it to `Final`. Every write to a `Pending` or `Final` turn or its children, from every surface and origin, is refused with 409 `turn_immutable` and `details.reason` `hv_pending` or `hv_final` (policy HvTurnFreeze), except the one write of finalization itself (origin `HvFinalization`). A request that ends `Canceled` or `Failed` releases its turns back to `None`. Rationale: the reviewed content equals the finalized content without a content comparison race, and the operator's "may not allow updates" is one guard in the existing write path. Rejected: letting writes continue and refusing finalization on a changed snapshot hash, which would waste completed reviews and still leave a window between the last check and the commit.
147: - R-05 Only terminal turns are admitted. A member turn that is not terminal (`TurnStatus.IsTerminal`, foundation section 3.5.3) refuses the whole request with 409 `hv_turns_not_terminal`, naming each turn. The submitting turn is never a member: a session scope excludes it and reports the exclusion in the result, and a turn or range scope that names it is refused with 400 `hv_scope_includes_submitting_turn` (the foundation's rule that "the request's own turn is never a candidate, a dependency, or cited evidence", foundation section 3.1). A Code or Docs turn that needs HV before it can complete is completed first with `hostileReview` `Other` (for example "HV requested hvr-..."), which the foundation already allows and never counts as an AGREE (foundation C8); finalization then replaces that `Other` with the HV result. Rationale: no turn changes status after it is frozen, so there is no close-inside-finalization path. Rejected: admitting in-progress turns with a declared close intent (draft 213, section 3.B), which adds a mechanism and still freezes a turn the model is working in.
148: - R-06 Hostile reviews are written only by the pipeline. On agent surfaces a `hostileReview` write may carry only `status` `Other` (with its required `otherNotes`); a write naming `Pass`, `Fail`, or `Running`, or carrying `hvVerdict`, is refused with 403 `review_hostile_pipeline_only` (amendment A-06). Process ConvertHvReceiptToReview is retired. Rationale: a manual Pass or Fail would bypass reviewer exclusion, complete evidence, and atomic finalization, and no surface may bypass them (draft 213, H5, adopted). Rejected: keeping the manual route for emergencies; a reviewer can be enabled and checked instead (S-27).
149: - R-07 Assignment at admission, durable round-robin. The submit transaction picks the next eligible reviewer after the workspace's round-robin cursor and advances the cursor in the same SerializableWrite (policy RoundRobinAssignment), so assignment survives restarts and two concurrent submissions never pick from the same cursor value. When the assigned reviewer is no longer eligible at claim time (offline, disabled), the claim reassigns through the same policy and records the reassignment. Rejected: assignment at claim only, which hides the assignee from the submitter and lets claim order, not round-robin order, pick reviewers.
150: - R-08 One agent identity, server-attributed. `AgentIdentity` (namespace `QBrainAi.Client.Agents`, shared by the server, the REPL, and, through the golden contract, the PowerShell core) maps every known alias to one of the five reviewer ids: Claude (`claude`, `claudecode`, `claude-code`, `claudecowork`, `claude-cowork`, `cowork`), Codex (`codex`), Copilot (`copilot`), Grok (`grok`, `grokcode`, `grok-code`, `grokbot`, `grok-bot`), Cline (`cline`, `cline-v2`, `clinev2`), case-insensitively and ignoring separators. The submitter is the agent of the submitting turn, located by its full turn key (TurnLocator); a free-text name never overrides it. The author is the agent of the reviewed session (one request names turns of one MCP session, R-26), stored normalized as `AuthorReviewerId`. A reviewer whose id equals the submitter's or the author's is never eligible (S-17, S-28, P-01, P-07). Develop holds three alias maps with different canonical forms (`src/QBrainAi.Repl.Host/MarkerFileClientOptionsResolver.cs:64-81`, `src/QBrainAi.Repl.Core/TodoSelectionStore.cs:166-171`, the plugin's `Get-ReplCanonicalAgentName`); they are context under the DRY ruling and are not changed by this amendment. Exclusion is by agent family, not by model vendor (D-01, settled): S-17 names "the agent submitting the review", P-01 constrains the agent family and asks separately for the agent and the model, and the operator runs Cline on `gpt-6-astra` (provider `openai-codex`, VI-01 receipt) while keeping Cline and Codex as two reviewers (S-02); a model a reviewer shares with the submitter stays visible in the run's provenance, and the operator can disable that reviewer (UpdateHvReviewerCommand). Exclusion covers the author as well as the submitter (D-05, settled): a review by the agent that wrote the turns is a self-review, which S-28 rules out of HV and P-07 rules out of validation.
151: - R-09 Operator submissions. A caller with no session-log turn (Director, an operator at the REPL) submits with `submitter.kind` `Operator` and a name; no reviewer is excluded for the submitter, and the author of the reviewed session is still excluded (R-08). Agent surfaces (plugin verbs, MCP tools, the REPL workflow verb) always send the submitting turn's key, which the plugin binds automatically (foundation process BindVerbToTurn). Limit (section 8): every caller holds the same workspace key, so the server cannot prove that an `Operator` submission did not come from an agent.
152: - R-10 Readiness through NONCE (S-15, S-27). A reviewer is `Unverified`, `Online`, or `Offline`, and separately enabled or disabled. "NONCE the agent" is a probe run of the reviewer through its adapter with a fresh random nonce: it passes when the reviewer answers with the probe record that echoes the nonce and the adapter's runtime provenance shows the reviewer's resolved model and effort (P-04). Only a passing NONCE moves a reviewer to `Online`. An execution failure moves it to `Offline` until a later NONCE passes. The worker host NONCEs every enabled `Unverified` reviewer at startup and after a configuration change; an `Offline` reviewer is NONCEd only when a caller asks (S-15: "until resolved"). Rejected: a liveness ping or the server health nonce, which S-27 rules out.
153: - R-11 No execution time limit (P-02). A run has no timeout and no deadline. Liveness is the worker's lease, renewed by heartbeats; a stalled run stays visible (`lastOutputUtc`, the last progress record) and anyone can cancel it (S-18). The only expiry is the lease of a dead worker (R-13). This replaces the 30-minute `ExecutionTimeout` of the separate HostileReview options (`src/QBrainAi.Services/Options/HostileReviewWorkerOptions.cs:45-46`) for HV runs only. The process exit code is never the outcome of a run: the reviewer's records decide it (V-8 for a review, policy ReadinessProbeVerdict for a probe), because a CLI can end a refused or empty run with exit code 0 (VI-03: a headless Grok run whose write call was refused ended `cancelled` with exit 0, and two Copilot permission variants exited 0 with no output).
154: - R-12 True live output (S-22, P8). Each reviewer adapter delivers every output line as the process writes it, through a line callback, never after the process ends; the worker appends lines in batches (at most `OutputFlushInterval`, default 250 ms, or `OutputFlushBytes`, default 64 KiB, whichever comes first) through AppendHvRunOutputCommand, which stores each batch as one GZIP chunk and wakes the streams. The output stream replays stored chunks and then follows new ones (shared component OrderedEventReplay). Develop's one-shot strategy yields its output only after completion (`src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy.cs:57-75`), so the adapters need a real line path (section 21, P8). Acceptance criterion FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008-AC003 makes the difference testable: a line is observable on the stream while the reviewer process is still running. The reviewer's records are read from each agent message's complete text, assembled from the CLI's native events (Grok's `streaming-json` sends message text one token per event, and Copilot sends deltas and then the whole message, as the probe runs of 2026-10-16 show), by one extraction function that the worker runs as lines arrive and finalization runs over the stored log (section 16.3), so a record split across events is read exactly once and both read the same records (FR-MCP-HVPIPE-010-AC006).
155: - R-13 Leases and fences (handoff requirement 10). A run is owned through a lease (owner, expiry) and a fence token that increases on every claim and takeover, the pattern develop already uses for handoff ingestion (owner and expiry with a `StateVersion` takeover, `src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/HandoffIngestionService.cs:724-735`, and a fenced terminal write that matches owner and version, `:782-807`). Every worker write carries the fence; a write with a stale fence changes nothing and returns `stale_fence`, and the worker that receives it stops its process. Expired leases are swept (ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand): the attempt becomes `Abandoned` and the request is queued again until `MaxAttemptsPerRequest` (default 3) is spent, then `Failed`, or `Canceled` when a cancel was requested; policy HvRetryDecision writes that outcome, with its turn release and its notification, for the sweep exactly as for FailHvRunCommand. Rejected: the unused lease options of the HostileReview subsystem (`HostileReviewWorkerOptions.cs:30-46`), which no code reads (section 21, P1).
156: - R-14 Evidence in the relational store, GZIP at rest (S-13, S-29, S-30). The accepted request is one GZIP blob written at admission; the response log is the run's ordered GZIP chunks; the result document is one GZIP blob written at finalization. No uncompressed copy of an evidence item is stored in the evidence tables, and each evidence item is stored there once (the structured rows of section 12, such as the request's `Context` and the findings, are records the units derive, not copies of the evidence blobs). The audit ledger keeps its own history of every evidence write, as it does for every audited entity: develop's ledger snapshots every property of an audited entity, binary columns included (`src/QBrainAi.Storage/McpDbContext.cs:1540-1589`), compressed with GZIP (`src/QBrainAi.Storage/Entities/DataAuditLogEntity.cs:119-147`), and a removal never changes it (R-20, I-13). Retrieval returns `application/gzip` (download name `<hvRequestId>-<kind>.jsonl.gz` or `.json.gz`) or, when asked, the decompressed bytes. The pattern is develop's audit ledger, which stores GZIP payloads in the database (`src/QBrainAi.Storage/Entities/DataAuditLogEntity.cs:66-147`). Rationale: S-23 ("Single trx at end") and S-29 (the database audit log) both hold only when the evidence is in the same transactional store as the result, and no crash window between a file system and the database remains. Rejected: `.jsonl.gz` files beside the database, which would need a two-store protocol, keep evidence outside the audit ledger, and split backups.
157: - R-15 Atomic finalization (S-23). FinalizeHvRequestCommand verifies the evidence and the reviewer output before it opens a transaction, then commits in one SerializableWrite: the result document, the per-turn assessments, the holistic evaluation, the failures, each turn's `hostileReview` through policy HvVerdictMapping (origin `HvFinalization`), each turn's `Final` HV state, the linked responses' model grades and trust decisions (when Mode is not `Off`), the request's `Completed` state, its notification, and the audit rows. The transaction re-checks everything the earlier reads relied on (the run's fence, the chunk manifest, the request and turn states). Crash windows are in section 9.
158: - R-16 Transactional notification outbox (S-19). Every state change that callers observe writes an `HvNotification` row in its own transaction, numbered by a per-workspace sequence that the same transaction advances, so the sequence has no gaps and no row is visible before its change commits. The notification stream replays rows after the caller's `Last-Event-ID` and then follows new ones (OrderedEventReplay). Delivery is at least once; consumers deduplicate by sequence. `IChangeEventBus` (develop's in-memory bus, `src/QBrainAi.Services/Notifications/IChangeEventBus.cs:4`) is used only to wake waiting streams and the worker, never as the record.
159: - R-17 Incidents through the triage endpoint (S-15, S-26). An execution failure writes an `HvIncident` row in the failure's transaction; FileHvIncidentCommand then submits it through `ITriageService` with its `dedupeKey` (`hv-reviewer-<reviewerId>-<failureCode>` for a failure attributable to the reviewer, `hv-server-<failureCode>` otherwise, section 12), which triage groups as `dedupe:<key>` (`src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/TriageService.cs:1475-1476`), and records the returned report and group ids. A filing that fails stays `Pending` and is retried by the worker host's sweep. Rejected: new incident tables with their own deduplication (S-26: "File through endpoint").
160: - R-18 Honest ETA (S-18, P-03). The ETA a caller sees is the reviewer's own latest progress record (`percentComplete`, `etaSeconds`), with `etaStatus` `Reported` and the record's time; with no progress record it is `etaStatus` `Unknown` and no number. The server never estimates.
161: - R-19 Audit participation and hard stop (S-29). Every HV entity carries `IsDeleted`, so `McpDbContext` writes its ledger rows for every HV mutation in the same `SaveChanges` (develop audits only entities with that property, `src/QBrainAi.Storage/McpDbContext.cs:1620-1627`). The ledger is append-only for HV: no HV unit or process updates or deletes a ledger row (I-13). Because develop skips the ledger when the audit table is unavailable (`McpDbContext.cs:1507-1538`), every HV unit first calls the shared component AuditLedgerGuard, which refuses with 503 `audit_unavailable` and writes nothing when the ledger cannot be written. Evidence reads (GetHvEvidenceQuery, GetHvResultQuery, the output stream, and GetHvRequestQuery when it returns output lines) write an explicit `read` ledger row before returning bytes, and a read whose row cannot be written is refused (the "protected-log access" of draft 213 participates in the audit log, S-29).
162: - R-20 Retention until removal (S-29). No unit deletes, expires, or compacts HV evidence except RemoveHvEvidenceCommand, an explicit call that removes the evidence bytes of one request, keeps its result rows, hashes, and sizes, records who removed it and why, and is audited. It clears the evidence tables only and never changes or deletes an audit ledger row: the ledger keeps the history of the evidence's writes and gains the record of the removal, because an audit log is never purged (I-13). There are no roles: any caller with the workspace key can call it, as S-29 requires.
163: - R-21 Self-review independence (S-28). No HV unit, policy, or process reads `agentReview`. The turn snapshot sent to a reviewer omits both review records (shared component TurnSnapshotBuilder), so a reviewer never sees a self-review grade. S-12 (a plugin list of missing agent reviews) is met by the foundation's Stop-gate remedy, which already lists each open turn's missing `agentReview` (foundation section 3.4, Stop gate, and `Get-CloseRemedy`, section 3.5.6), and is not an HV input. Reconciliation with the foundation's completion gate: HV admits only terminal turns (R-05), and the foundation's gate needs an `agentReview` status of `Pass`, `Fail`, or `Other` before a turn can close `completed` (foundation section 5.3, CompletionPolicy); that is a rule of closing a turn, not of HV, it is met by `Other` with a note as well as by a grade, and a turn closed `failed` or `canceled` needs no agent review at all; HV admission, execution, and verdict read none of it, and FR-MCP-HVPIPE-013 proves that every terminal turn is admitted and judged identically whatever its self-review.
164: - R-22 Verdict only (S-25). No HV unit writes TODO state. A result names the reviewed turns' `todoId` values for information only.
165: - R-23 Requirement references (S-14). The submitted context is stored as written (Markdown, YAML, or text, declared by `contextFormat`) and parsed for requirement references: FR, TR, and TEST ids of the form `<KIND>-<AREA>-<NNN>` with optional further dash-separated area segments, acceptance criteria written as `<FR id>-AC<NNN>` or `<FR id> ac-<n>`, and use cases by their store id or exact title. Each reference is resolved against the workspace's effective requirements and use cases and handed to the reviewer as a delineated list with its resolution status; an unresolved reference is listed as unresolved, never refused (shared component RequirementReferenceExtractor).
166: - R-24 The reviewer's own turn (P-06). The brief tells the reviewer to log its review as its own session-log turn, classified `Chore` so that its turn never needs an HV of its own (foundation completion policy: Chore needs no hostile review), and to store its entire result there. Finalization requires that turn to exist, to be persisted (not a failsafe or queued record), to have been created at or after the run's claim, to be closed `completed` as a `Chore`, and to contain every reviewer record of the run byte for byte in its stored normal form (V-6). A reviewer whose host cannot log turns fails its NONCE with `reviewer_turn_logging_unsupported`. The reviewer's plugin runs as a host session of its own: a review or probe run never reads or changes the plugin state or the session-log session of a live session of the same agent in the workspace (FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008-AC008), which matters because a reviewer starts in the workspace (section 16.2) and Grok's headless hooks write their host state under the working directory's `.mcpServer/grok/` (VI-04).
167: - R-25 The HostileReview subsystem stays separate. FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-001 to -006 (its queue, artifact links, findings, and query surface) are not changed by this amendment, as the foundation already states (foundation section 5.4); the problems found in it (section 21, P1 to P3) are tracked in REMED-HVPIPELINE-001. It stays separate (D-02, settled): it reviews artifacts (TODO, FR/TR/TEST, plans, files, commits; FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-002) while this pipeline reviews session turns (S-03), the approved foundation keeps it separate, and consolidating it is scope the operator has not named. Its missing worker (P1) has its own contract (section 16.7) and shares only the execution primitives that fit it (the reviewer adapters' launch builder, live-line path, and containment, and FencedLease), so reviewer execution exists once (the DRY ruling); nothing of this pipeline's evidence model applies to it, because FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-002 forbids storing a raw artifact or an assembled prompt.
168: - R-26 Scope limits. One request names turns of one MCP session. `MaxTurnsPerRequest` (default 200, the foundation's `HvRequest:MaxTurns` default) bounds every scope; a session scope above it is refused with 400 `hv_scope_too_large` naming the count, never truncated.
169: - R-27 One open review per turn. A turn is `Pending` in at most one open request (a unique filtered index on the turn key where the item is `Pending`); admission over a pending turn is refused with 409 `hv_turns_pending` naming the turns and their requests, and over a final turn with 409 `hv_turns_already_reviewed` (S-06, S-20).
170: - R-28 Cancellation by anyone (S-18). `Queued` becomes `Canceled` at once; `Running` becomes `CancelRequested`, and the worker stops the process at its next heartbeat and closes the run `Canceled`; a repeat on a `CancelRequested` or `Canceled` request returns 200 unchanged; `Finalizing`, `Completed`, and `Failed` refuse with 409 `hv_request_not_cancelable`. A cancel, a close, and a finalization of the same request are serialized on the request row, so exactly one of them commits first and the others see its state: a close that finds `CancelRequested` ends the run `Canceled` instead of making the request `Finalizing`, so an accepted cancellation is never lost (CloseHvRunOutputCommand).
171: - R-29 Worker units are internal. ClaimHvRunCommand, RecordHvRunStartCommand, RecordHvRunHeartbeatCommand, AppendHvRunOutputCommand, CloseHvRunOutputCommand, FailHvRunCommand, ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand, FinalizeHvRequestCommand, and FileHvIncidentCommand have no REST route, MCP tool, or client method; only the worker host dispatches them, in-process, through `IDispatcher`. The public mutations are submit, cancel, reviewer update, NONCE, and evidence removal.
172: - R-30 Plugins consume notifications through the REPL. Plugins never call REST (foundation section 3); the REPL gains a streaming verb that follows the notification stream, and the PowerShell core runs it in the background per host session (process WatchHvNotifications), keeping the last sequence and the inbox in one state file of the host session, so one atomic replace records both, and handing completions of requests that host session's MCP session submitted to the next prompt as context. A terminal notification carries the submitter's turn key (section 12), so the watcher matches it by that key and needs no local record of the submission, and a completion that arrives before the submit verb has returned is still delivered. Delivery to the model is at least once: a crash between adding a completion to a prompt and recording it delivered can repeat it, and each entry carries its sequence so a repeat is recognizable (the outbox rule of R-16).
173: - R-31 The 98/98 bar for the overall verdict (P-05), one predicate stated once here. The overall verdict is `AGREE` exactly when all of these hold: the holistic correctness and completeness both meet `max(configured hostile threshold, 0.98)` (ScoreVerdict, foundation section 3.5.4) and the holistic verdict is `AGREE`; every member turn's verdict is `AGREE`; every response grade of an admitted response that is still `Pending` at commit is `AGREE` under the foundation's `verdict_match` rule; and no finding of any scope (turn, holistic, or response) is FAIL or UNKNOWN. Otherwise it is `DISAGREE`. Per-turn hostile reviews keep the foundation's configured hostile thresholds through HvVerdictMapping. V-4 checks the reviewer's overall verdict against this predicate.
174: 
175: ## 6. Amended foundation clauses
176: 
177: Each amendment names the foundation clause it replaces and states the replacement; nothing else in the named section changes.
178: 
179: - A-01 Foundation section 3.1, "Trust" and "Model grade", and section 6.1, fourth bullet: "model grades come only from the configured grader (default Codex, `gpt-6-astra`, `max`, the plan's HV reviewer)" and "this effort builds no grading worker or HV pipeline" are replaced by: model grades come only from FinalizeHvRequestCommand, for the reviewer the pipeline assigned to the request (R-03); the HV pipeline is this amendment.
180: - A-02 Foundation section 3 ("Process") and section 8.1: "a Codex gpt-6-astra max hostile validation" for every gate is replaced by: a hostile validation by the reviewer the operator names for the session, never of the requesting agent's family (P-01). The HV of a plan's own work does not use the pipeline that plan is building until that pipeline has passed its own end-to-end verification (section 20.3).
181: - A-03 Foundation section 6.2: `ModelGrader:AgentName`, `ModelGrader:RequiredModel`, `ModelGrader:RequiredEffort`, `ModelGrader:ReceiptRoot`, and `HvRequest:MaxTurns` are removed; the reviewer pool and `MaxTurnsPerRequest` of `HostileValidationOptions` (section 10) replace them. The startup validation of an empty grader identity and receipt root is removed with them.
182: - A-04 Foundation sections 6.3 (`AgentContextHvRequestEntity`, `AgentContextHvRequestItemEntity`), 6.4 (`CreateAgentContextHvRequestRequest`, `AgentContextHvRequestResult`, `AgentContextHvRequestQuery`), 6.5 (CreateAgentContextHvRequestCommand, GetAgentContextHvRequestQuery, QueryAgentContextHvRequestsQuery with their nested activities), 6.7 (their sequences), and Addendum A.9 are superseded by `HvRequest`, `HvRequestTurn`, `HvRequestResponse` (section 12), SubmitHvRequestCommand, GetHvRequestQuery, QueryHvRequestsQuery (section 14), and Addendum B. Every foundation reference to an HV request's `HvRequestId` (the grade's root id and foreign key, the finding's root id) now names `HvRequest`. ResponseStatusTransition's side effect ("the response's `Pending` items in `Open` HV requests become `Closed` with that reason, and each request left with no `Pending` item becomes `Completed`") becomes: the response's `Pending` `HvRequestResponse` items become `Closed` with that reason; the HV request's own state is decided by its turns and is never completed by a response transition.
183: - A-05 Foundation section 6.5, RecordModelGradeCommand: its whole contract (input, guards, checks, side effects, and diagrams, including the nested activities ReadModelGradeInputs, CheckGradeTarget, and SaveModelGrade) is replaced by the internal unit of section 14.5; its caller becomes FinalizeHvRequestCommand only (internal dispatch inside the finalization transaction, origin `HvFinalization`); the REST route `POST /qbrainai/agent-context/responses/{responseId}/grades/model`, the MCP tool `agent_context_record_model_grade`, the client and REPL methods, and `New-McpAgentContextRecordModelGradeParams` are removed; 403 `agent_context_grader_not_allowed` becomes "grader is not the reviewer assigned to the HV request"; the eight receipt and reviewer checks of foundation section 6.3 are replaced by the verification steps V-1 to V-8 of policy HvFinalVerification (section 15), which finalization runs before it dispatches the grade; the receipt path, rollout, and thread columns of `AgentResponseGradeEntity` become the run reference `RunId` and the evidence hashes (section 12).
184: - A-06 Foundation section 3.1, "Review record" ("One record per kind per turn; latest write wins") and section 5.2, RecordSessionTurnReviewCommand: on agent surfaces a `hostileReview` write may carry only `status` `Other`; `Pass`, `Fail`, `Running`, and `hvVerdict` are refused with 403 `review_hostile_pipeline_only` (R-06); `Unnecessary` and `Unstarted` stay server-managed as before. Policy HvVerdictMapping is applied only by FinalizeHvRequestCommand. Section 5.4, process ConvertHvReceiptToReview, and its plugin function `ConvertFrom-McpHvReceipt` are retired, with the `hvReceiptPath` parameter of the plugin verbs.
185: - A-07 Foundation section 3.1, "Reviews remain writable on terminal turns", section 3.4 (section PUT and DELETE), and section 3.5.3, TurnWritePipeline: every turn write, review write, review reset, section replace or clear, dialog append, title change, and session-level replace or delete that would change a turn whose HV state is `Pending` or `Final`, or any of that turn's children, is refused with 409 `turn_immutable` (`details.reason` `hv_pending` or `hv_final`, `details.hvRequestId`), from every origin except `HvFinalization` (policy HvTurnFreeze, R-04). TurnWritePipeline runs that policy after TurnLocator and before every other policy.
186: - A-08 Foundation section 3.5.3, `WriteOrigin`: a fifth origin `HvFinalization` is added; it is exempt from the completion gate (it never moves a turn's status) and is the only origin that may write a turn whose HV state is `Pending`.
187: - A-09 Foundation section 6.3, check 7 (`reviewer_independent`, "not a different agent name, so an independently launched Codex reviewer grades a Codex-authored response"): replaced by V-5, which requires both a separate session and a reviewer id different from the submitter's and the author's (R-08, S-17, P-01, P-07).
188: - A-10 Foundation section 7.8 (UC-7, "Record a hostile validation review with receipts") is replaced by the use cases of section 18 (UC-HV-03 to UC-HV-05); foundation section 7.12 (UC "Submit and grade an agent response") keeps its flow, and its model grade now comes from UC-HV-05.
189: - A-11 Foundation section 5.1, `SessionLogTurnEntity`: two columns are added, `HvState` (16: `None`, `Pending`, `Final`; database default `None`) and `HvRequestId` (128, null while `None`), written only by the migration that adds them, which sets `HvState` `Final` (with `HvRequestId` null) on every turn whose hostile review is already `Pass` or `Fail`, because S-07 forbids updates to a turn with an HV review, and then by SubmitHvRequestCommand, CancelHvRequestCommand, CloseHvRunOutputCommand, FailHvRunCommand, and ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand (the last three through policy HvRetryDecision), and FinalizeHvRequestCommand, through policy HvTurnFreeze's state changes (Addendum B.8).
190: - A-12 Foundation section 6.1, "Existing records and stores", the FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW bullet: unchanged in substance (R-25); its phrase "because this effort builds no grading worker" is replaced by "because turn HV runs through the HostileValidation pipeline of Amendment 1".

P0 creates each record with the title and statement below (exactly: the title is the row text after its id up to ` Tests:`, without its final period; in the statement, <AC list> is the row's Validates and Also validates lists with ranges such as AC001..AC004 expanded, and <test classes> is its Tests: list); the statement is \"Validates <AC list> with <test classes>; every listed new or changed AC has a RED receipt before implementation and a green receipt at the slice gate, and every listed baseline-green AC has a green receipt.\" Every record carries the same three ACs, with its own id prefix: `<TESTID>-AC001` every listed new or changed FR and TR AC has at least one named test that failed (RED) before implementation and passes after, and every listed baseline-green AC has a named test that passes; `<TESTID>-AC002` the mocks-green run and its negative check are recorded on the slice TODO; `<TESTID>-AC003` the listed suites run with zero failures and zero skips in the slice gate. (TEST-SUPPORT-024 uses `ac-1`..`ac-3` with the same texts, matching its family.) Span and satisfaction: a TEST record belongs to the slices in its TR's bracket, every slice labelled in parentheses in its row (for example `(S5)`), and every slice, earlier or later, whose task line names one of its cases or test suites. So TEST-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-008 spans S1, S5, S6, S8, S9, and S10 (S5 and S6 name its golden-map case, S10 its real-gate cases), TEST-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-009 spans S8, S9, and S11 (whose task names `SessionLogReviewDocsContractTests`), and TEST-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-001 spans S1, S3, S4, S5, and S6. Each slice's gate runs the cases that slice owns plus those of every earlier slice in the span, and the record's three ACs are set satisfied only when the last slice of its span completes. Every case a row names is owned by a slice of that span. Where an AC's bracket names several surfaces, each TEST covers the surfaces its own span implements, and the other surfaces are covered by the TESTs of the slices that implement them (a row says so explicitly where it hands one off, as in \"via TEST-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-004\")."

4400: ##### Nested sequence: SubmitOneModelGrade (loop body of the RecordModelGradeCommand sequence)
4401: 
4402: The reviewer sends `client.AgentContext.RecordModelGradeAsync` through the REPL, whose lossless normalizer keeps `correctness` and `completeness` as their exact lexemes (`ScoreLexeme`, section 3.5.4), so `verdict_match` compares the verdict entry's own lexemes. `ScoreLexemeJsonConverter` refuses an invalid lexeme at deserialization, before the dispatch and before any lookup, with 400 `review_score_format`, `review_score_precision`, or `review_score_out_of_range`. The request carries `hvRequestId`, the scores and findings copied from the reviewer's `grades` entry, the receipt paths, the reviewer's turn ids, and `reviewerThreadId`. The model grade reads before it writes, in the order of section 3.1 ("Database-only delegates"): every read-only check (the response, the HV request and its item, and the eight receipt, reviewer, and runtime-identity checks), then the EvaluateStalenessCommand dispatch, then the SerializableWrite. Nested sequence ReadModelGradeInputs looks the stored grade up read-only, checks the response, the HV request, and its item, reads the receipt files and the reviewer's own turn for the eight checks of section 6.3, and only then dispatches EvaluateStalenessCommand for the response (the only writer of `Stale`, which evaluates outside any transaction); the handler then derives the verdict with `ScoreVerdict` at the 0.98 floor, in memory. The SerializableWrite then locks the response and reads and writes only the database: it looks the grade up again, which finds a concurrent continuation that stored it first; re-checks the response's `StatusVersion` and the HV request's status and item that the reads saw (a change ends the attempt, and the unit runs again from its reads); inserts the grade with its findings, receipt hashes, and the thresholds in force, stamps `RecordedUtc`, marks the item `Graded`, completes the HV request with `CompletedUtc` when no item is `Pending`, and dispatches DecideAgentResponseTrustCommand (not gated), whose decision reads the stored status and the latest grades; all of it commits together. 1444: ### 16.1 Process HvWorkerHost: the durable worker [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-007, -008, -009]
1445: 
1446: A hosted `BackgroundService` per workspace application (`src/QBrainAi.Services/HostileValidation/Execution/HvWorkerHost.cs`), with a worker id of the host name, process id, and a random suffix. It is the only dispatcher of the internal units (R-29). At start, while `WorkerEnabled`, it requests a NONCE for every enabled `Unverified` reviewer (StartHvReviewerNonceCommand, R-10). Then it loops, woken by an `IChangeEventBus` wake-up or at `PollInterval`: a sweep (ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand, FinalizeHvRequestCommand for every `Finalizing` request it lists, FileHvIncidentCommand for every `Pending` incident), then claims until ClaimHvRunCommand returns null, starting one process RunReviewerProcess per claim. On a graceful shutdown it stops claiming and ends each of its running runs with FailHvRunCommand code `worker_shutdown`, which files no incident, marks no reviewer offline, and does not count as an attempt (policy HvRetryDecision); after a crash the leases expire instead (W-03). A 503 `audit_unavailable` from any unit stops the loop iteration and the next iteration starts from the sweep (W-12).

1467: ### 16.2 Process RunReviewerProcess: one attempt, live [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008, -016]
1468: 
1469: Runs one claimed run. It builds the brief (section 13.3: the accepted request read from the `Request` evidence inside the run envelope, or the probe brief with its nonce), asks the reviewer's adapter for the launch (section 16.3), starts the process with the workspace as its working directory and its plugin as a host session of its own (R-24), inside a containment bound to the worker process, so the reviewer and every descendant end when the worker dies, however abruptly (W-03; the containment, for example a process group or job object, is the adapter's, section 16.3), records the start (RecordHvRunStartCommand), and appends the `hv_brief` record as sequence 1. While the process runs it has four concurrent duties and no time limit (R-11, P-02): every line the adapter delivers goes into a buffer that is appended (AppendHvRunOutputCommand) when `OutputFlushBytes` accumulate; a flush timer appends a buffer that is not empty once `OutputFlushInterval` has passed since its first line, whether or not another line arrives, so a single line followed by silence is still appended within the interval (R-12); a heartbeat every `HeartbeatInterval` (RecordHvRunHeartbeatCommand) renews the lease and reads cancellation; and the process exit is awaited. `stale_fence` from any unit kills the process and ends the attempt without another write (W-03); `audit_unavailable` kills the process and ends the attempt (W-12); `evidence_corrupt` from an append (its round trip failed and nothing was saved) kills the process and fails the run with `evidence_corrupt` (FailHvRunCommand: a server fault, so a server incident and the reviewer unchanged, and the request through policy HvRetryDecision); a retryable `conflict` repeats the same unit call with the same sequence. Every append carries the records the adapter's extraction completed with that batch. On exit the remaining buffer is appended, the adapter's provenance lines are appended (section 16.3), and the run is closed (exit code 0, CloseHvRunOutputCommand, then FinalizeHvRequestCommand for a review whose request is `Finalizing`; a close that finds the request `CancelRequested` ends it `Canceled` instead, R-28; exit code 0 is not evidence of a review, R-11) or failed (FailHvRunCommand with `reviewer_exited_nonzero`, or `reviewer_launch_failed` when the process never started). A cancellation read at a heartbeat kills the process and fails the run with `canceled`, which policy HvRetryDecision turns into the request's `Canceled` (R-28). Killing the process, here and in the diagrams, ends the reviewer's whole process tree, descendants included, also when the root process has already exited; and when the root exits while a descendant still holds its output pipes, the worker ends that descendant before it reads the output to its end. Without that, a descendant that outlives the reviewer would hold the run open forever, because no time limit ends a run (P-02); P14 is the same defect class in the plugin core (FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008-AC011).

1524: ### 16.3 Reviewer adapter contract [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-001, -003, -008]
1525: 
1526: `IHvReviewerAdapter` (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.HostileValidation.Reviewers`), one implementation per reviewer id:
1527: 
1528: - `BuildLaunch(brief, reviewer)`: a `ProcessStartInfo` built as an argument list, never a shell string, with the brief on standard input or in a temporary file the adapter deletes after the run; the launch arguments come from one shared launch builder that develop's one-shot strategy also uses, so the per-CLI arguments of `OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy` (`AddCodexArguments`, `AddClaudeArguments`, `AddGrokArguments`, `AddClineArguments`, `OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy.cs:238-262`) are written once (DRY); processes start through the existing `IProcessSpawner` and `IProcessEnvironmentService` (`OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy.cs:18-21`), inside a containment the adapter creates at launch and binds to the worker process (for example a process group with a parent-death signal on Linux or a kill-on-close job object on Windows, settled in H1's contract step), so the reviewer and every descendant end when the worker dies, and so killing the run ends the whole tree even after the root has exited (W-03, FR-MCP-HVPIPE-007-AC008, FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008-AC011); develop's `DefaultProcessSpawner` starts an ordinary process and offers only an explicit kill (`src/QBrainAi.Common.AgentCli/DefaultProcessSpawner.cs:12-16,48-51`), so H1 adds the containment. The shared launch builder holds the one table of highest efforts of section 10 (P9). The reviewer runs behind a write barrier verified for its CLI (VI-03, probes of 2026-10-16): Codex `exec -s read-only` (a write attempt was refused by its sandbox), Grok `--permission-mode plan` (a write call was refused; a headless Grok run then ends `cancelled` at the first call that needs approval, so its launch allows the read tools a review uses), and Copilot `--available-tools` naming only read tools (write and shell tools are not offered at all). Claude's and Cline's plan modes are not accepted as barriers on that evidence (Claude's model declined before its barrier was exercised; Cline ran a shell command in plan mode), so Claude's launch restricts its tools structurally (`--tools`) and Cline stays unqualified until H1 proves a barrier. Whether each reviewer's plugin can still log its turn behind its barrier (the plugin writes host-session state and calls the server) is verified in H1 (VI-03, VI-04); a reviewer that cannot fails its NONCE (R-24).
1529: - Live lines (R-12, P8): standard output and standard error are read line by line as the process writes them (asynchronous line reads on the redirected streams), and each line is handed to the run's callback at once; nothing waits for the process to end.
1530: - `NormalizeLine(line, stream)`: a native JSON event line of a CLI run in a JSON streaming mode is kept as written; any other line becomes `{ "type": "hv_raw", "stream", "line" }`.
1531: - `ExtractReviewerRecords(lines)`: one pure function over a run's ordered native lines. It assembles each agent message's complete text by the CLI's event model (Grok's per-token `text` events, Copilot's `assistant.message_delta` events followed by the whole `assistant.message`, Claude's whole assistant messages, Codex's `agent_message` items, Cline's accumulated content) and returns, in message order, every line of that text that is exactly one JSON object of a reviewer record type of section 13.3; the fence lines of a fenced block are ignored, and a line holding other text beside a record is free text. The worker runs it as lines arrive and passes each batch's completed records to AppendHvRunOutputCommand; finalization runs it over the stored log; both get the same records (R-12). Record types the worker writes itself (`hv_brief`, `hv_provenance`, `hv_raw`) are never accepted from message text, so a reviewer cannot forge them.
1532: - `ReadProvenance(run)`: `hv_provenance` lines read from the CLI's own runtime receipt after the run (P-04), sources verified on 2026-10-16 (VI-01): for Codex, the thread's rollout `turn_context` (fields `model` and `effort`; observed `model` `gpt-6-astra`, `effort` `max`), the source the foundation's `runtime_identity` check reads (foundation section 6.3, check 8); for Claude, the session transcript under `~/.claude/projects` (the assistant message `model` and the request `effort`), written only when session persistence is on, so the launch never passes `--no-session-persistence`; for Grok, the session store `~/.grok/sessions/<cwd>/<sessionId>/` (`summary.json` `reasoning_effort`, and a model id that `chat_history.jsonl` names `grok-4.7-build` while the events name `grok-4.7`, so H1 pins the field V-7 compares); for Copilot, the run's own JSON stream (each call's `assistant.message.model` and `user.message.responsesReasoning.effort`; `--usage-output-file` holds the model only); for Cline, none, because its run records hold the model and only whether thinking was on, so V-7 and the NONCE fail closed (L-04, D-06).
1533: - Highest effort when none is configured: the verified values of section 10 (VI-08), never develop's one-shot constants (P9).

562: 
563: `GET /requests/{hvRequestId}/result` returns `HvResultDocument`:
564:
