7: # Session Log Management
8: 
9: ## Overview
10: 
11: To manage agent session logs, use the `workflow.sessionlog.*` REPL command namespace through the plugin wrapper (`lib/repl-invoke.ps1` / `Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1`). Session logging captures agent activity, reasoning dialog, file operations, and design decisions as a structured audit trail.
12: 
13: `workflow.sessionlog.*` is a plugin workflow/REPL namespace, not a literal native MCP tool namespace. Native McpServer `/mcp-transport` discovery uses names such as `sessionlog_*`, `todo_*`, and `requirements_*`; hosted-agent adapters may expose `mcp_session_*` aliases, and your agent's tool discovery may show configured MCP tools with native names such as `sessionlog_submit`, `todo_list`, and `requirements_generate`. Do not call this plugin unavailable solely because `workflow.*` names are absent from generic MCP discovery.
14: 
15: `workflow.*` result envelopes may include `deprecated: true`. This is success metadata that tells callers the workflow namespace is legacy-compatible and should migrate toward the canonical `client.*` surface where available; it is not a failure signal and is not a reason to use raw REST. Treat an empty `workflow.sessionlog.queryHistory` result as a valid no-match result, not as an inert wrapper. Re-check the workspace current directory, the explicit `agent` or `sourceType`, and local plugin cache/session state through the wrapper before reporting history as unavailable.
16: 
17: This skill covers manual operations, history queries, and the full lifecycle for agents that need direct control.
18: 
19: ## Preferred Workflow
20: 
21: For most work sessions:
22: 
23: 1. Bootstrap session logging once.
24: 2. Open or resume the session.
25: 3. On each user request, begin a turn.
26: 4. Consult current session/task state before asking the user for context.
27: 5. Update the turn with relevant files, decisions, and actions.
28: 6. Complete the turn after verification, or record failure if blocked.
29: 
30: ## Running the Workflow Methods
31: 
32: When the plugin's hooks (in `hooks/`) are active, most session management is automated and you do not need to drive it by hand. When hooks are not active for your agent, drive the lifecycle yourself through the plugin wrapper, never by hand-piping envelopes to REPL stdio:
33: 
34: ```pwsh
35: pwsh -NoProfile -File "<plugin-root>/lib/repl-invoke.ps1" -Method <method> -ParamsYaml @'
36: <yaml params>
37: '@
38: ```
39: 
40: The equivalent function form is `Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1 "<method>" "<yaml params>"`. For a one-shot bootstrap plus session open, prefer `<plugin-root>/lib/session-start.ps1 <workspace-path>`.
41: 
42: The YAML envelope blocks in this skill document the wire contract each method maps to. Pass the `params:` body to the wrapper; it wraps it in the request envelope, validates documented params, and emits single-line JSON to REPL stdio for you. If you bypass the wrapper for diagnostics and write to REPL stdio directly, send one single-line JSON request envelope per message, never formatted YAML.
43: 
44: Why the wrapper and not raw stdio:
45: 
46: - `workflow.sessionlog.beginTurn` and `openSession` are not server routes. Calling them raw returns `method_invocation_error` / `method_not_found`. The wrapper treats them as local no-ops and tracks turn state in `cache/current-turn.yaml`.
47: - Persisting a turn goes through `client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync`, which is strict: `actions[].order` must be an unquoted integer (`order: 1`, never `order: "1"`) or you get `JSON value could not be converted to System.Int32`. The wrapper builds the envelope with correct types.
48: - There is no `session.init` method. Bootstrap with `workflow.sessionlog.bootstrap` only.
49: 
50: ## Identifier Naming Conventions
51: 
52: ### Session IDs
53: 
54: Format: `<Agent>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<suffix>`
55: 
56: Regex: `^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*-\d{8}T\d{6}Z-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$`
57: 
58: - Agent name must be PascalCase (e.g. `YourAgent`)
59: - Timestamp must be ISO 8601 compact UTC: `yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ`
60: - Suffix must be lowercase kebab-case: `feature-auth`, `bugfix-timeout`
61: 
62: Valid examples: `YourAgent-20260409T120000Z-implement-auth`, `YourAgent-20260304T113901Z-refactor-session`
63: 
64: Invalid: `youragent-20260409T120000Z-task` (lowercase agent), `YourAgent-20260304-feature` (missing time component)
65: 
66: ### Request IDs
67: 
68: Format: `req-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<slugOrOrdinal>`
69: 
70: Regex: `^req-\d{8}T\d{6}Z-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$`
71: 
72: Valid examples: `req-20260409T120001Z-add-jwt-001`, `req-20260409T120002Z-query-todos`
73: 
74: Invalid: `request-20260409T120001Z-task` (wrong prefix), `req-20260409-task` (missing time)

194: Valid `category` values: `reasoning`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `observation`, `decision`.
195: 
196: Valid `role` values: `model`, `tool`, `system`, `user`.
197: 
198: ### Step 6 - Append Actions
199: 
200: To record file operations and other work artifacts:
201: 
202: ```yaml
203: type: request
204: payload:
205:   requestId: req-20260409T120005Z-actions-001
206:   method: workflow.sessionlog.appendActions
207:   params:
208:     actions:
209:       - order: 1
210:         description: Created TokenService with JWT generation
211:         type: create
212:         status: completed
213:         filePath: src/Services/TokenService.cs
214:       - order: 2
215:         description: Created JwtValidator for token validation
216:         type: create
217:         status: completed
218:         filePath: src/Services/JwtValidator.cs
219:       - order: 3
220:         description: Chose HS256 for JWT signing (internal service, symmetric key)
221:         type: design_decision
222:         status: completed
223:         filePath: ""
224: ```
225: 
226: Standard action `type` values: `edit`, `create`, `delete`, `design_decision`, `commit`, `pr_comment`, `issue_comment`, `web_reference`, `dependency_add`.
227: 
228: `actions[].order` must be an unquoted integer (`order: 1`, never `order: "1"`).
229: 
230: ### Step 7 - Complete Turn
231: 
232: To finalize a turn as successfully completed (immutable after this call):
233: 
234: ```yaml
235: type: request
236: payload:
237:   requestId: req-20260409T120006Z-complete-001
238:   method: workflow.sessionlog.completeTurn
239:   params:
240:     response: |
241:       JWT authentication implemented:
242:       - TokenService generates HS256-signed tokens
243:       - JwtValidator validates and extracts claims
244:       - Services registered in Startup.cs
245:       - All unit tests passing
246: ```
247: 
248: ### Failing a Turn
249: 
250: To mark a turn as failed with an error description:
251: 
252: ```yaml
253: type: request
254: payload:
255:   requestId: req-20260409T120007Z-fail-001
256:   method: workflow.sessionlog.failTurn
257:   params:
258:     errorMessage: Unable to complete - missing System.IdentityModel.Tokens.Jwt package
259:     errorCode: dependency_missing
260: ```
261: 
262: Both `completeTurn` and `failTurn` produce an immutable terminal state. No further `updateTurn`, `appendDialog`, or `appendActions` calls are allowed on a completed or failed turn.
263: 
264: ## Querying Session History
265: 
266: To browse previous sessions for context continuity:
267: 
268: ```yaml
269: type: request
270: payload:
271:   requestId: req-20260409T120008Z-history-001
272:   method: workflow.sessionlog.queryHistory
273:   params:
274:     agent: YourAgent
275:     limit: 10
276:     offset: 0
277: ```
278: 
279: ```yaml
280: type: result
281: payload:
282:   requestId: req-20260409T120008Z-history-001
283:   result:
284:     sessions:
285:       - agent: YourAgent
286:         sessionId: YourAgent-20260409T120001Z-implement-auth
287:         title: Implement JWT authentication
288:         model: <model-id>
289:         started: 2026-04-09T12:00:01Z
290:         lastUpdated: 2026-04-09T12:30:00Z
291:         status: completed
292:         turnCount: 3
293:         filesModifiedCount: 5
294:         tags: [auth, jwt, security]
295:     totalCount: 1
296:     offset: 0
297:     limit: 10
298: ```
299: 
300: Omit `agent` to query across all agents. Use `offset` and `limit` for pagination.
301: 
302: ## Turn Lifecycle State Machine
303: 
304: A turn transitions through these states only in forward order:
305: 
306: 1. `in_progress` - created via `beginTurn`, open for updates
307: 2. `completed` - finalized via `completeTurn` (immutable)
308: 3. `failed` - finalized via `failTurn` (immutable)
309: 
310: Any attempt to call `updateTurn`, `appendDialog`, or `appendActions` on a `completed` or `failed` turn returns a `turn_immutable` error.
311: 
312: ## Error Handling
313: 
314: ```yaml
315: type: error
316: payload:
317:   requestId: req-20260409T120003Z-update-001
318:   code: turn_immutable
319:   message: Turn is immutable (status: completed)
320:   details:
321:     turnRequestId: req-20260409T120002Z-add-jwt-001
322:     currentStatus: completed
323:     hint: Begin a new turn instead
324: ```
325: 
326: Common error codes:
327: 
328: - `session_not_found`: no active session; call `openSession` first
329: - `session_already_exists`: session ID already in use
330: - `invalid_session_id`: session ID format violation
331: - `invalid_request_id`: request ID format violation
332: - `turn_not_found`: no active turn; call `beginTurn` first
333: - `turn_already_exists`: turn with same request ID already exists
334: - `turn_immutable`: cannot modify completed or failed turn
335: 
336: ## Session Continuity After Restart
337: 
338: After a server restart or agent reconnect:
339: 
340: 1. Call `workflow.sessionlog.queryHistory` to review past sessions
341: 2. Decide whether to continue in a new session referencing the previous one in the title, or to re-open fresh
342: 3. Re-read `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` for the rotated API key before making any calls
343: 4. Call `bootstrap` again (idempotent) then `openSession` for the new session
344: 
345: ## Model-Authored Session Logging
346: 
347: Plugins do not import local chat transcripts for normal session logging. The active model must write its own session log through `workflow.sessionlog.beginTurn`, `workflow.sessionlog.appendDialog`, `workflow.sessionlog.appendActions`, and `workflow.sessionlog.completeTurn` or `workflow.sessionlog.failTurn`.
348: 
349: ### Turn Completion
350: 
351: Plugin stop/final-response helpers may complete an active turn through `lib/repl-invoke.ps1`, but the turn payload must already be model-authored through the session-log workflow. The runtime builds request envelopes with PowerShell objects and serializers. Secret values (API keys, Bearer tokens) are redacted before logging.
352: 
353: ### Subagent Logging
354: 
355: Subagents are responsible for writing their own turns through the same session-log workflow. Parent or child models may include parent request IDs, agent names, and source metadata as tags or actions when those values are available, but plugin packages must not parse transcript files to populate session logs.

1348: ### Policy HvFinalVerification: the eight verification steps [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-010, -011, -021]
1349: 
1350: Applied by FinalizeHvRequestCommand to the run's stored chunks before any transaction; each failed step returns its code, and the steps run in the diagram's order (V-1, V-8, V-2, V-3, V-4, V-5, V-6, V-7), so the log's integrity and completeness are known before any record is bound. They replace the foundation's eight receipt checks (A-05): `receipt_path` becomes V-1 (the evidence is held by the server, not found on disk), `request_meta` becomes V-3 and V-7 (the expected reviewer is recorded on the run), `verdict_block` becomes V-8, `verdict_binding` becomes V-2 and V-3, `verdict_match` becomes V-4, `reviewer_turn` becomes V-6, `reviewer_independent` becomes V-5 (amended, A-09), and `runtime_identity` becomes V-7.
1351: 
1352: - V-1 Evidence integrity (`evidence_corrupt`): the chunks run 1 to `OutputChunkCount` without a gap; each decompresses (GzipCodec), its SHA-256 equals the stored one, the chain hash equals `OutputChainSha256`, and every line parses as one JSON object (I-06).
1353: - V-2 Snapshot binding: each `hv_turn_assessment` names a member's ordinal, turn key, and admission snapshot hash (`verdict_binding_failed` otherwise), and TurnSnapshotBuilder over each turn now yields that hash (`snapshot_changed` otherwise; HvTurnFreeze makes it unreachable, and the step proves it, I-02).
1354: - V-3 Verdict binding (`verdict_binding_failed`): the `hv_verdict` record names this `hvRequestId` and run, its counts equal the members and the responses of the accepted request (the set admitted, whatever has happened to those responses since), its reviewer equals the run's reviewer, and each `hv_response_grade` names a response of the accepted request with the `ContentSha256` the accepted request recorded.
1355: - V-4 Verdict consistency (`reviewer_output_invalid`): every score is a valid lexeme (ScoreLexeme); each turn's verdict is `AGREE` exactly when ScoreVerdict derives `Pass` at the hostile thresholds and its findings hold no FAIL or UNKNOWN; the holistic verdict likewise at `max(threshold, 0.98)` (R-31); each response grade follows the foundation's `verdict_match` rule; and the overall verdict is the one predicate of R-31 over the holistic verdict, every turn's verdict, the response grades, and the findings of every scope.
1356: - V-5 Reviewer independence (`reviewer_not_independent`): the run's reviewer id differs from the request's submitter id and from its author id (S-17, S-28, P-01, P-07).
1357: - V-6 Reviewer turn (`reviewer_turn_unverified`): the `hv_reviewer_turn` record names a turn TurnLocator finds, whose agent AgentIdentity maps to the run's reviewer, whose session is neither the reviewed session nor the submitter's, created at or after the run's `ClaimedUtc`, persisted (not a failsafe or queued record), closed `completed` with class `Chore`, and whose stored result (its response, then its dialog parts in order with each part's header line removed, as foundation check 6 reads it) contains every reviewer record of the run in the order the extraction returned them (each `hv_turn_assessment`, the `hv_holistic`, each `hv_response_grade`, and the `hv_verdict`), each byte for byte in its stored normal form; a summary-only, open, or failed turn fails (P-06, R-24).
1358: - V-7 Runtime identity (`runtime_identity_mismatch`): the log holds at least one top-level `hv_provenance` line written by the worker from the CLI's runtime receipt of this run, and every one names the run's expected model (or, when the reviewer has no configured model, the model the last NONCE resolved) and expected effort (P-04).
1359: - V-8 Completeness (`reviewer_output_invalid`): exactly one `hv_verdict`, the last reviewer record; exactly one `hv_holistic`; exactly one `hv_turn_assessment` per member and one `hv_response_grade` per response of the accepted request; every FAIL and UNKNOWN finding of every scope (turn, holistic, and response) has a category, a location, evidence, and a remediation (S-13); the failures list equals every FAIL and UNKNOWN finding of every scope.

Items are the agent responses whose `RequestId` lies in the range when the request is created and whose status is `Submitted`, `Grading`, `Trusted`, or `Stale` (a `Rejected` or `Superseded` response is never listed, and a response already `Pending` in another `Open` request is not listed again, `HvRequestResponsePendingInOpenRequestNotListedAgain`); when a listed response becomes `Rejected` or `Superseded` while the request is `Open`, ResponseStatusTransition (section 3.5.5, called by RejectAgentResponseCommand or SupersedeAgentResponseCommand) sets its item `Closed` with that reason in the same SerializableWrite and, when no item stays `Pending`, sets the request `Completed` with `CompletedUtc` (`HvRequestRangeWithRejectedResponseNotListed`, `HvRequestItemRejectedMidReviewClosedAndRequestCompletes`, `HvRequestItemSupersededMidReviewClosed`).

2834: Receipt and reviewer verification (RecordModelGradeCommand), before a model grade is saved; each failure refuses the grade with 422 `agent_context_receipt_unverified` and `details.check` naming the check:
2835: 
2836: 1. `receipt_path`: both jsonl paths resolve inside the workspace under `ModelGrader:ReceiptRoot`.
2837: 2. `request_meta`: the request jsonl's first line is a JSON object with `type` `hv_request_meta` whose `reviewer.agent` contains `ModelGrader:AgentName`, `reviewer.model` equals `ModelGrader:RequiredModel`, and `reviewer.effort` equals `ModelGrader:RequiredEffort` (the HV runner writes exactly this object), and the request jsonl's body record names the `hvRequestId`.
2838: 3. `verdict_block`: the response jsonl records a completed turn (`turn.completed`) whose last agent message contains exactly one `=== VERDICT JSON ===` block that parses as one JSON object.

Verdict semantics: each `grades` entry carries `verdict` `AGREE` or `DISAGREE` for its one response, and the verdict JSON's `overallVerdict` is the request's; an entry's `verdict` is `AGREE` exactly when ScoreVerdict derives `Pass` from its scores and counts at `max(Trust:Correctness, 0.98)` and `max(Trust:Completeness, 0.98)` (section 3.5.4) and its findings hold no FAIL or UNKNOWN, and `DISAGREE` otherwise, and `overallVerdict` is `AGREE` exactly when every entry is `AGREE`; any other combination is refused (`ModelGradeDisagreeVerdictPassingScoresRefusedVerdictMatch`, `ModelGradeAgreeVerdictFailingScoresOrFailFindingRefusedVerdictMatch`, `ModelGradeOverallAgreeWithDisagreeEntryRefusedVerdictMatch`). A consistent `DISAGREE` entry is a legitimate failing grade and is recorded, and in a mixed range each response's grade is recorded from its own entry under an overall `DISAGREE` (`ModelGradeConsistentDisagreeEntryRecordedFailingGrade`, `ModelGradeMixedRangeEachEntryRecordedOverallDisagree`).

2568:   - AC004 Given triage unreachable, or a crash after the incident committed and before its filing (W-08), when filing, then the incident stays `Pending` with the error and the next sweep files it (`IncidentFilingRetriedUntilFiled`).
2569:   - AC005 Given attempts spent, when the last attempt fails, then the request is `Failed` with `attempts_exhausted`, its turns are `None`, and `hv_failed` is appended (`AttemptsExhaustedRequestFailedTurnsReleased`).
2570:   - AC006 Given a server-attributable failure (`evidence_corrupt`, `snapshot_changed`, `reviewer_not_independent`), when recorded, then an incident with `hv-server-<code>` exists and the reviewer is unchanged (`ServerFailureIncidentReviewerUnchanged`).
2571:   - AC007 Given an unwritable ledger, when an incident is filed, then the triage service is never called and the incident stays `Pending`; given a ledger that fails after triage accepted, then the incident stays `Pending` and the retry joins the same triage group; given a filing that succeeds, then `Filed` and `incident_filed` commit in one transaction (H3: `IncidentFilingNeverCallsTriageWhileLedgerUnavailable`).

1: # Session Log Schema Reference
2: 
3: Load this file when you need to create, update, or query session logs.
4: For specific agent operational instructions, follow `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`.
5: 
6: 
7: Session-log mutations (every source type, including QBAgent) persist without the turn-transaction
8: coordinator or keyserver on `develop` and on the live Linux box MCP (FR-MCP-173). Keep live
9: `Mcp:TurnTransactions:Enabled=true` for QuadBrain; do not disable it to make session-log writes
10: succeed. Workspace-stamp repair remains fail-closed.
11: 
12: ## Endpoints
13: 
14: - `POST /qbrainai/sessionlog` — create or update a session log
15: - `GET /qbrainai/sessionlog?limit=N&offset=M&planFile=&todoId=&turnStatus=&staleOlderThanHours=` — query recent session logs; optional exact `planFile` and `todoId` filters after the same normalize/expand rules as persist; optional `turnStatus` plus `staleOlderThanHours` list sessions that still have matching turns older than N hours (BUG-TRIAGE-121). The query is read-only and does not cancel or complete those turns.
16: - `POST /qbrainai/sessionlog/{agent}/{sessionId}/{requestId}/begin` - first persist of a turn; body `SessionLifecycleBeginRequest` requires `planFile` and `todoId` (`None` when none)
17: - `POST /qbrainai/sessionlog/{agent}/{sessionId}/{requestId}/dialog` - stream reasoning dialog (incremental persist; not a full-session upsert)
18: 
19: ## Submit acknowledgement (FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-003)
20: 
21: `POST /qbrainai/sessionlog` returns a durable-write receipt only after the storage service
22: has completed its awaited save. The receipt retains `id`, `sourceType`, and `sessionId`,
23: and adds `persisted: true`, `degraded: false`, and `queued: false`. It includes `requestId`
24: for a single-turn submission; zero-turn and multi-turn submissions return a null request ID.
25: Failed or canceled persistence never produces this successful receipt.
26: 
27: `SessionLogSubmitResult` preserves these fields through the typed client and REPL YAML
28: transport. A legacy response that omits `persisted` is not durable-write confirmation.
29: Update both the service and the installed REPL when deploying this contract. Failsafes
30: must remain until the plugin receives the required persistence acknowledgement.
31: 
32: Whole-session snapshots cannot reopen a terminal turn with a supplied nonterminal status
33: or replace it with a different cancellation status. This prevents a late hook or failsafe
34: replay from overwriting completed history after an acknowledgement failure. Same-status
35: and omitted-status enrichment, cancellation of active turns, and recovery from canceled
36: to completed remain supported. Deliberate corrections and reopening use the explicit
37: single-turn update API. Relational submissions protect the read/check/save sequence with
38: serializable isolation and acknowledge after the owned transaction commits. A conflicting
39: write that cannot serialize fails rather than acknowledging overwritten terminal history;
40: its failsafe remains available for retry. Caller-owned, ambient, and enlisted transactions
41: are rejected before mutation because submission cannot acknowledge their uncommitted writes.
42: Reused contexts refresh the target session graph inside the transaction; pending edits to
43: that graph are rejected without discarding them, and unrelated tracked changes are retained.
44: 
45: ## Outbound sanitization (FR-MCP-SESSIONLOGSAN-001)
46: 
47: Query, GET, MCP, and stdio reads clone the DTO and apply `Mcp:SessionLogSanitization` rules before the payload leaves the process. Raw storage is unchanged. Replacement tokens include the rule Id (for example `[REDACTED:example-internal-token]`). A secret in a stored turn still participates in text filtering and does not change paging metadata. Invalid or duplicate rule Ids fail options validation. Regex timeout redacts fail-closed and does not log the input.
48: 
49: ## Stale in_progress turns (BUG-TRIAGE-121)
50: 
51: Forward-only. Do not mass-close historical `in_progress` turns. Recurrence of completed-then-canceled is the UserPromptSubmit isolation path: background briefs `reuse` an in-progress root work turn and `isolate-skip` a completed root turn.
52: 
53: Operator listing of stale open turns (sessions that contain at least one matching turn; inspect `turns[].status` and `turns[].timestamp`; complete or fail individually):
54: 
55: ```
56: GET /qbrainai/sessionlog?turnStatus=in_progress&staleOlderThanHours=24
57: ```
58: 
59: MCP tool `sessionlog_query` with the same fields: `turnStatus=in_progress`, `staleOlderThanHours=24` (any positive hour count). Omit either field to relax that half of the filter. Mass close is out of scope.
60: 
61: ## Required turn context (normative)
62: 
63: - First persist and replace of a turn require both `planFile` and `todoId`.
64: - Accepted `planFile`: workspace-relative path, exact absolute path, `~/` home-relative path, or the exact sentinel `None` (case-sensitive). `..` is rejected.
65: - Accepted `todoId`: canonical MCP TODO id (`PHASE-AREA-###` or `ISSUE-N`) or `None`. FR/TR/TEST ids are rejected.
66: - Additive updates that omit either field keep the stored value. Replace that omits either field is rejected, except the canceled/cancelled hook-supersede persist: when the incoming turn status is `canceled` or `cancelled` and either field is omitted or blank, the server stamps `None` then validates. That is the only first-persist omission path (FR-MCP-SESSIONLOGCTX-001 AC-003 plus STORE-006).
67: - Reads never return null for these fields. Import, ingest, and federation persist a validated pair (`None` if extraction finds nothing).
68: 
69: ## Naming Conventions (Normative)
70: 
71: - `sessionId` must match `<Agent>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<suffix>`.
72: - `sessionId` regex: `^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*-\d{8}T\d{6}Z-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$`
73: - `sessionId` must start with the exact `sourceType`/`agent` prefix (case-sensitive).
74: - `requestId` must match `req-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<slugOrOrdinal>`.
75: - `requestId` regex: `^req-\d{8}T\d{6}Z-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$`
76: - Valid IDs:
77:   - `sessionId`: `Copilot-20260304T113901Z-namingconv`
78:   - `requestId`: `req-20260304T113901Z-plan-namingconventions-001`
79: - Invalid IDs:
80:   - `sessionId`: `copilot-20260304T113901Z-namingconv`, `Copilot-2026-03-04-namingconv`
81:   - `requestId`: `req-plan-namingconventions-001`, `request-20260304T113901Z-task-01`
82: 
83: ## SessionLog (POST body)
84: 
85: ```json
86: {
87:   "sourceType": "string — YOUR agent name (e.g. 'Copilot', 'Cline', 'Cursor')",
88:   "sessionId": "string — required format <Agent>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<suffix> (e.g. 'Copilot-20260304T113901Z-feature-audit')",
89:   "agentSessionId": "string|null — provider-native root session identifier from the host payload; empty when unknown (the MCP sessionId is never echoed here)",
90:   "agentSessionTranscriptFile": "string|null — provider-native transcript path; only set when the file exists on disk, empty otherwise (never synthesized)",
91:   "agentExecutablePath": "string|null — resolved executable path for the agent host",
92:   "agentExecutableVersion": "string|null — executable version resolved from the agent host, or 'unknown' when discovery fails (never the plugin version)",
93:   "title": "string — brief session summary, keep updated",
94:   "model": "string — AI model name (e.g. 'claude-sonnet-4-20250514')",
95:   "started": "string — ISO 8601 timestamp when session began",
